Honest Review After 30 Days Usage
  
  _____________________________________
  


  Why we want a Mobile???
  
  No wonder the outlook has been largely changed. We look for higher specs, like a 2+GHz 8 Core Processor, 4GB+ RAM, 32-64+GB Internal and a battery with 4000+mAh.
  
  However, Other common features like tough and big screen, good camera, metal body and all high tech aspects are tweaked with almost all mobiles now a days.
  

  We became so tech hungry and get involved in tech aspects that, we almost forgot the basic need of a phone. That's right, we actually forgot it. A good phone should give us good voice call experience and a good network for connecting to to the world of internet.
  

  That's actually needed isn't it!!!
  

  So, why are we compromising with this basic accessibilities with some value added technologies. What's the need of a phone if you can't talk with somebody with out any distortion. It really matters a lot. This phone actually doesn't support good voice quality and network coverage. What you will do with 2 days of charge if you don't get good network connection for voice/data.
  

  It's a serious issue with all the Chinese mobile manufacturers. This mobile is indeed a manufactured in India but the fact is it's allegiance is from China.
  

  I am not against any community or geography but it's a fact that Chinese devices are mostly suited for look and feel but inside it's just a poof!!

First of all a big thanks to big million day, got my Mi Max 2 in 13500Rs. Thanks to flipkart for fast delivery, got my phone in 2nd day.
  
  Now about Mi Max 2:
  

  Screen.
  
  The huge 6.44" screen might make it uncomfortable to put the phone in pocket,
  
  but the pleasure it gives while watching videos, reading, playing games is unbeatable.
  
  Besides, the brightness and contrast of the screen is also good, and you can also change it manually
  
  to suit your needs.
  

  Battery
  
  The beast comes with the humongous 5300 mAh battery, which lasts almost 36 to 40 hours
  
  with normal usage (watching videos, playing games, internet turned on).
  
  I had to charge it only 3 times during whole week.
  
  And it also charges quickly takes around 2.5 hrs to charge it completely, which is pretty fast
  
  considering the capacity.
  

  Body.
  
  The phone comes with fully metal uni-body, it's very sleek and smooth.
  
  And with high possibilities of sleeping out of hands. So, use it carefully.
  
  Get a cover immediately as soon as you purchase the phone.
  

  UI
  
  The MIUI gives a nice experience, comes in with many inbuilt tools, like cleaner, battery optimizer,
  
  TV Remote ,app lock, Dual apps( you can use two different accounts of Facebook, whatsap etc.)
  
  It also gives you the privilege to select which app should auto-start and which shouldn't(on other devices,you need root permission for this.)
  
  The notification panel is also impressive, you can sort the shortcuts as per your need.
  
  It also has the setting to select whether or not to show the notification symbol in status bar or not.
  
  It also comes with the Read-mode, so you don't need to have any third party white light filter app.
  

  Camera
  
  Camera is a bit disappointment. Mi says it uses Sony sensors, but the picture quality isn't up to the mark.
  
  Especially, for low light pictures.The stock camera app gives you less quality pictures. But if you use any
  
  third party apps, you can get nice pics.
  

  CPU, RAM and GPU
  
  The processor and the RAM performs to the satisfaction. I'm playing Asphalt 8, Gods of Rome, Real racing 3
  
  and not facing any lagging issues or graphics problems. Works smoothly.
  
  At any given moment, you get at least 2 GB RAM free, which is quite sufficient.
  

  Sensors
  
  The fingerprint sensors is pretty much faster than some of the other devices I've used.
  
  You can use your finger print to as a screen lock, as well as the app lock.(The app lock feature also comes in MIUI)
  

  Storage
  
  Comes with the 64 GB internal storage, out of which 53 GB is available to user. It is very sufficient.
  
  You don't need the memory card.
  

  The phone has hybrid sim slot, which means you can use either two sims, or one sim+ memory card.
  
  But considering the internal storage you get, you probably don't need to have additional memory card.
  

  Calling quality is good and crispy. It does support the VoLTE, so you can use your Jio card in it. ;)
  

  The phone does show two speaker slots at the bottom, and Xiaomi also says the phone has dual speaker,
  
  but actually, speaker is only on the left side of the phone, and on the right side it has mic.
  
  But while watching videos, the earpiece works as the speaker(not very loud though), and you get a stereo effect.
  

  It's slightly heavy(211 g, as said in specs) so your hands may get stressed if you keep it holding for too long.
  

  So, considering the features, and the price, the phone is worth buying, if you're looking for a
  
  big screen and bigger battery.
  
  Just go for it.

column6: Read it before u buy it.... Clarifies all ur doubts...
column7:
If u r really interested in the device read it because its a very long detailed review....
  

  But before review let me answer 2 qtns
  
  Is it worth the money?
  
  Yes, off course..... no doubt in that.... but Please choose between 3gb and 4 gb variant..... not the 2 gb one please
  
  Is it worth upgrading fron redmi note 3?
  
  No....not much improvement in the redmi note 4 compared to note 3.....so upgrading is not worth it
  
  Unboxing:
  
  Handset - I have purchased the redmi note 4 3/32 gb dark grey variant for 10999 rs. Delivered on 25th jan 2017.
  
  No earphones.... but everyone know it.... not a surprise...
  
  Usb cable(good qwality, may be 1 mtr lenght)
  
  Travel adapter( its a 2A adapter that means this handset has fast charging but not quick charge like in leeco le2) ...
  
  Battery is builtin and non removable
  
  User guide and no screen protector (quite disappointing)
  
  as soon as u setup ur device u will get a 1.4 gb update..... do take the ota update....
  

  Reviewing after 1 day usage
  
  Body:
  
  It has speakers placed at edge....
  
  but the device is not completely metak body and has plastic at top and bottom and metal at the backside centre.
  
  U can see this design in indian variants.... may be due to cost cutting..... but visually u dont find any difference with the mobile body.... so no worries
  
  Volte (9/10)
  
  Both sims support 4g volte..... no issue with the call qwality..... voice over lte works fine and u can use ur jio sim to call fron the default dialer without turning on mobile data
  
  IR blaster:(9/10)
  
  Good feature and mi has a pre installed remote app.... but its not a universal remote though.....
  
  Setting this for a new device is bit uneasy..... but once u set it u can through ur old remote and use ur mobile to control all ur devices.
  

  Display :(9/10)
  
  2.5d glass covering the sharp hp display.....no issue with the viewing angles..... has led indicator and supports all the colors.....u can customize the color of led light witb respect to different apps and different functionalities
  

  Sound:(9.5/10)
  
  Speaker output is very good.... No issues with it.... side speakers avoids sound muffles...
  
  Earphn output is also good ....it supports all d earphns.... I tested my samung and philips earphn.... It works well the pause and play button works and even the volume contrl button of the earphn works.....
  

  Camera:(8/10)
  
  Gives very good photos under day light.... In nights only closeup shots appear good....low light Images are soft and not really sharp.....front cam clicks good selfies.... Selfie lovers vil not be disappointed
  
  Battety:(9/10)
  
  Its 4100 mah battery and battery backup is really impressive and but the charge timing is quite disappointing .... It charges from 5% to 100% in 2hour and 25 minutes...
  
  Software :
  
  It runs on 6.0.1 Marshmallow .... Very less bloatwares installed and almost 1.3 gb of ram free even on running 8 to 10 apps in the background.... Its confirmed from xiomi that the redmi note 4 will soon receive the andorid N update.
  
  Hardware:
  
  I'm a not a geek and I dont play heavy games but played spiderman and asphault 8(medium graphics) .... But it doesn't heat up much..... so snapdragon 625 is a good move by xiomi
  
  Sim card slots:
  
  It has hybrid sim slot.... So u can use 2 sims or a sd card and a sim.... Both the sim support 4g.... I have tested it with airtel 4g and jio 4g
  
  Call quality :(9/10)
  
  Call quality is good.... No issues and it has 2 microphones.... 4g and 3 g signal reception is also good....volte call qwality is good....
  

  Fingerprint sensor:(10/10)
  
  Its far far better than one plus three finger print sensor.... It detects ur finger at any degree and even the sweaty fingers.... It unlocks the device instantly in less than micro secs.... U can select other operations for ur finger like opening an app directly from lock screen.... calling a number directly.... it also has inbuilt fingerprint app locker..... But this fingerprint app locker is buggy..... once u open a locked app then even if u close and open it again it wont ask for fingerprint unless u lock and unlock the phn again.... this bug may be fixed in next ota update.
  

  Conclusion
  
  Cons:
  
  1. quick charge technology missing .....really a much needed one for this 4100 gaint battery......In the same price segment u get quick charging in leeco le2 which charges the device in 1.30 hrs.... but this takes around 2.40 hrs to charge completely
  
  2.Setting up the mi remote for a new device.... quite tedious job...
  

  3.Buggy inbuilt app locker..
  
  4.Not upto the expectation low light camera.....
  
  Pros:
  
  Battery backup
  
  speaker qwality and its placement
  
  Fingerprint sensor
  
  Ir blaster....
  
  as usual the miui customisations

  1. MIUI and RAM consumption: I am assuming over 90% of the reviews of this phone were conducted using the 4GB RAM version of the phone. Clearly, the performance of that phone would be better than that of the 2gb or 3gb variant. That is because out of 3GB RAM(the variant i purchased), at any given time without any app open, the UI takes OVER HALF OF THE RAM (1.5 TO 1.6GB). Compare it to phones with stock android or lighter UI(cool iu) and you will see that the take up a mere 500 to 600 MB of RAM. Now you can pacify yourself saying you dont need more than 1.5 gigs of RAM at a time anyway, youll regret it after a few months due to generic disease that android carries with itself by the name of garbage collection that generally slows down the overall performance of the phone.
  

  2. Laggy UI: I received the 8.1 MIUI update out of the box and there was no significant improvement. The UI is laggy and there are many basic features that are overlooked and all the focus is diverted to the animations and feel of the UI. column6: Read it before u buy it.... Clarifies all ur doubts...
column7:
If u r really interested in the device read it because its a very long detailed review....
  

  But before review let me answer 2 qtns
  
  Is it worth the money?
  
  Yes, off course..... no doubt in that.... but Please choose between 3gb and 4 gb variant..... not the 2 gb one please
  
  Is it worth upgrading fron redmi note 3?
  
  No....not much improvement in the redmi note 4 compared to note 3.....so upgrading is not worth it
  
  Unboxing:
  
  Handset - I have purchased the redmi note 4 3/32 gb dark grey variant for 10999 rs. Delivered on 25th jan 2017.
  
  No earphones.... but everyone know it.... not a surprise...
  
  Usb cable(good qwality, may be 1 mtr lenght)
  
  Travel adapter( its a 2A adapter that means this handset has fast charging but not quick charge like in leeco le2) ...
  
  Battery is builtin and non removable
  
  User guide and no screen protector (quite disappointing)
  
  as soon as u setup ur device u will get a 1.4 gb update..... do take the ota update....
  

  Reviewing after 1 day usage
  
  Body:
  
  It has speakers placed at edge....
  
  but the device is not completely metak body and has plastic at top and bottom and metal at the backside centre.
  
  U can see this design in indian variants.... may be due to cost cutting..... but visually u dont find any difference with the mobile body.... so no worries
  
  Volte (9/10)
  
  Both sims support 4g volte..... no issue with the call qwality..... voice over lte works fine and u can use ur jio sim to call fron the default dialer without turning on mobile data
  
  IR blaster:(9/10)
  
  Good feature and mi has a pre installed remote app.... but its not a universal remote though.....
  
  Setting this for a new device is bit uneasy..... but once u set it u can through ur old remote and use ur mobile to control all ur devices.
  

  Display :(9/10)
  
  2.5d glass covering the sharp hp display.....no issue with the viewing angles..... has led indicator and supports all the colors.....u can customize the color of led light witb respect to different apps and different functionalities
  

  Sound:(9.5/10)
  
  Speaker output is very good.... No issues with it.... side speakers avoids sound muffles...
  
  Earphn output is also good ....it supports all d earphns.... I tested my samung and philips earphn.... It works well the pause and play button works and even the volume contrl button of the earphn works.....
  

  Camera:(8/10)
  
  Gives very good photos under day light.... In nights only closeup shots appear good....low light Images are soft and not really sharp.....front cam clicks good selfies.... Selfie lovers vil not be disappointed
  
  Battety:(9/10)
  
  Its 4100 mah battery and battery backup is really impressive and but the charge timing is quite disappointing .... It charges from 5% to 100% in 2hour and 25 minutes...
  
  Software :
  
  It runs on 6.0.1 Marshmallow .... Very less bloatwares installed and almost 1.3 gb of ram free even on running 8 to 10 apps in the background.... Its confirmed from xiomi that the redmi note 4 will soon receive the andorid N update.
  
  Hardware:
  
  I'm a not a geek and I dont play heavy games but played spiderman and asphault 8(medium graphics) .... But it doesn't heat up much..... so snapdragon 625 is a good move by xiomi
  
  Sim card slots:
  
  It has hybrid sim slot.... So u can use 2 sims or a sd card and a sim.... Both the sim support 4g.... I have tested it with airtel 4g and jio 4g
  
  Call quality :(9/10)
  
  Call quality is good.... No issues and it has 2 microphones.... 4g and 3 g signal reception is also good....volte call qwality is good....
  

  Fingerprint sensor:(10/10)
  
  Its far far better than one plus three finger print sensor.... It detects ur finger at any degree and even the sweaty fingers.... It unlocks the device instantly in less than micro secs.... U can select other operations for ur finger like opening an app directly from lock screen.... calling a number directly.... it also has inbuilt fingerprint app locker..... But this fingerprint app locker is buggy..... once u open a locked app then even if u close and open it again it wont ask for fingerprint unless u lock and unlock the phn again.... this bug may be fixed in next ota update.
  

  Conclusion
  
  Cons:
  
  1. quick charge technology missing .....really a much needed one for this 4100 gaint battery......In the same price segment u get quick charging in leeco le2 which charges the device in 1.30 hrs.... but this takes around 2.40 hrs to charge completely
  
  2.Setting up the mi remote for a new device.... quite tedious job...
  

  3.Buggy inbuilt app locker..
  
  4.Not upto the expectation low light camera.....
  
  Pros:
  
  Battery backup
  
  speaker qwality and its placement
  
  Fingerprint sensor
  
  Ir blaster....
  
  as usual the miui customisations

I am going to write an honest review about the phone. I heard all the praises for this phone over multiple sites and channels and bought the phone. However, I'll mention the things they forgot to mention.
  


  1. MIUI and RAM consumption: I am assuming over 90% of the reviews of this phone were conducted using the 4GB RAM version of the phone. Clearly, the performance of that phone would be better than that of the 2gb or 3gb variant. That is because out of 3GB RAM(the variant i purchased), at any given time without any app open, the UI takes OVER HALF OF THE RAM (1.5 TO 1.6GB). Compare it to phones with stock android or lighter UI(cool iu) and you will see that the take up a mere 500 to 600 MB of RAM. Now you can pacify yourself saying you dont need more than 1.5 gigs of RAM at a time anyway, youll regret it after a few months due to generic disease that android carries with itself by the name of garbage collection that generally slows down the overall performance of the phone.
  

  2. Laggy UI: I received the 8.1 MIUI update out of the box and there was no significant improvement. The UI is laggy and there are many basic features that are overlooked and all the focus is diverted to the animations and feel of the UI. For example, you can't expand notifications (the drop down menu expands instead) which is basic and quite annoying not to have.

column6: The GOOD, BAD & UGLY Things About Xiaomi Mi3
column7:
Hey guys, I did manage to have an early access and got my hands on Xiaomi's flagship model Mi3 day before yesterday and thought I'd share my experience with others. This is 100% my experience and 100% true. So, let's begin.
  

  The Good Stuff About Mi3
  

  What I liked most about Mi3 is the fantastic display, awesome user interface, and amazing performance. The device is faster than you'd imagine - my previous phone is Samsung Galaxy 7"7 imported; games and apps that hang in that phone are playing with zero hassles in Mi3 - excellent, incredible, amazing. YES!!
  

  Snapdragon is truly amazing. It's damn fast. Also, you'd love the MIUI interface, simple, stable and very handy. You don't need any tech knowledge to take 'good' care of your phone. The one big issue I had with Samsung was taking care of the permissions and also optimizing my phone - with MIUI - this is incredibly simple and smooth. I love it.
  

  The display is fantastic - super clear and super charming - love that too.
  

  Super sensitive touch screen. Trust me, you'd love it. Mi3 will also give you very good quality sound. So that are the good stuff about Mi3.
  

  Now, there are some features/specs that are just OKAY - let me explain those:
  

  Camera. For an 13MP camera, we will expect better quality pictures. You'd be disappointed if you're expecting super quality pictures. I'm a photographer enthusiast with Nikon DSLR, so the picture quality is definitely not as good as we expect, especially in low light ambiance. I tried taking pics in different light settings but the quality is definitely not upto mark - its not BAD, but it's definitely not great. I really wish this could produce amazing pics with the 13MP camera it has - maybe because I'm used to quality pic from my Nikon gear.
  

  Battery: The battery performance isn't bad - but this isn't great as well. If you use Wifi for an hour surfing net, watching videos, downloading stuff - battery drains quick. But still it's okay for normal users.
  

  Build: The design is amazing in the first look, but you'd gradually have an okay feel when you used to have the phone in your hands. Maybe it's just me. For example take the Mi4 or M8 (of course they are expensive - just to let you know what I mean) they have a look and feel like a solid stuff - integrity. Mi3 doesn't have that.
  

  The bad:
  

  The body is delicate/fragile - easy to get scratches and marks. Don't try this, but if you let the phone fall from even a chair height, it will bend. Check Xiaomi Singapore page to see photos and once you handle the phone, you'd totally get that point. As a rough user, I'm waiting for the screen guard and flip cover before using it to full. I'm really afraid i might damage the body.
  

  With about fifteen minutes of Wifi or Gaming the device heats up. Not sure if it's just in my case. Share your experience on that as well.
  

  Memory: Only 16GB and memory is available and it is non expandable. So if you're savvy user, you'd need to keep transferring stuff to your computer/other storage devices every now and then. That's definitely a bad thing. I used to keep a lot of videos and songs - but that wont be possible with this limited space. But not really complaining about this as we know that only 16GB is available, before we purchased it - and you can use cloud if you want to store your music and video files - but that will need a high speed bandwidth and unlimited data transfer - think about accessing an one GB movie file - that's not as easy as you think. But still.
  

  The ugly:
  

  This is the worst part, the sim tray, go through the comments in Mi India page and you can see at least a dozen people have a bad experience there. It doesn't get ejected with a decent push. You'd need to push really hard to make it eject.. And this will definitely harm/damage the edges of your sim tray point (the edges of the small hole) take your phone and closely watch the edges of your sim tray point, you will definitely see some damages or scratches at least. I was very careful with this but still got some marks in the edges. This needs to be taken care at least for the future ones - it should be gentle like what we do with iphones and all - and the edges aren't solid, if you touch the edges with your sim tray ejecting pin, it would definitely damage it.
  

  Conclusion: It's a fantastic device for the price. You get to enjoy the best experience. Worth every penny. I'd definitely recommend this to anybody.
  

  There's another bad thing which isn't related to the phone. But anyway, Xiaomi should have released at least the flip cover and screen guard along with the phone launch. These are a necessity to take good care of the phone. Please make it fast Xiaomi - that was a stupid decision of yours - don't tell us you don't have them in stock - check other regions sites, accessories are never sold out. So make it quick before we damage our phones.

Switched to the Mi3 from the Moto X. Although, it isn't nearly as perfect as the X, it's a near perfect device for the value it offers at the price it is being sold.
  

  Display: Bright, crisp and clear. Won't go into any specifications but the touch is responsive and the text clear. The fonts tend to be slightly clunky. Although the size can be adjusted there's something that still feels weird about it.
  

  Camera: I don't really use the camera much but it's an efficient shooter. Tends to exaggerate the colours a bit but still workable.
  

  Battery: Considering the large battery stuffed into the casing, I'm a bit let down by the performance. I don't really blame the hardware cause I'm pretty certain it's due to the software on board.
  

  UI: The UI is familiar - will remind you both of stock Android and iOS in parts. There's not much of a learning curve with the device and it's fairly easy to get the hang of it.
  

  Themes: The device surely finds a sweet spot with its themeable interface courtesy MIUI. There are tons of themes to choose from but majority of the offerings end up displaying stray chinese characters.
  

  Apps: The app selection is as per the Play Store. Apps run well but there's a certain noticeable lag when you fire up a new app. Applications like Facebook end up missing certain characters while displaying newsfeeds.
  

  Build: The build is thin... especially when you come from a device like a Moto X or an iPhone 5. But there's nothing you can take away from the construction of the device at the price which it is offered in the market. The design isn't disruptive and it isn't intuitive. It's good looking and average at the same time. The cosmetic appeal would most certainly be subjective. The back panel tends to pick up a fair bit of marks. The unit I bought came with a scratched MI chrome logo at the back out of the box.
  

  Accessories: The box includes a USB cable and a charger plug. While the cable seems solid, I found the the charger plug / socket of very doubtful quality.
  

  Charging Time: The phone charges well and considering the size of the battery in this device, it takes anywhere from 1.5 to 2.5 hours to complete a full charge. The battery discharge would obviously vary from user to user. The jump from 99% to 100% takes a bit too long for comfort but I'm sure that's a software issue again.
  

  Call Quality: Call quality is cheap. Yes. The sound in the earpiece is very loud yet a bit noisy and muffled. Not the best call quality experience I've had over the years.
  


  CONCLUSION: I ended up buying this device at Rs. 13,749 from Flipkart. From the price, the offering on the table is remarkable. It's not perfect, as I've said before, but it's near perfect. It's a chunky device, difficult to hold with edges that pinch you while it's in your pocket. Yet, it is sleek, good looking and well constructed. It isn't without it's share of bugs. The software and UI does indeed reflect that this is a derivation from a Chinese MIUI but the localization of the UI should get better with the passage of time. What remains to be seen now is the level of post purchase service offered by Xiaomi. I'm giving it 4 stars.
  

  SIDE NOTE: Do not buy the Karpine Screen Protector. Ruins the touch experience and makes the phone unusable.

column7:
Hi Guys, I bought this phone on the 22nd and was probably the first one to place the order. My order log showed 12:00PM dot! I placed the order from my office and everything was smooth for me. After that i heard buying was a total nightmare from my other colleagues in office. Of all the people trying to buy this phone only my neighbor was able to buy this at the 39th minute after which the product went out of stock. For the first few minutes i was not sure whether my order went through since i didn't receive any confirmation from flipkart and could not see my order. I did receive a confirmation from the payment gateway though.  Enough about the buying experience. About the product.
  

  The product arrived next day evening and i was very excited to receive it. On opening it the first thing i checked was whether the sim card tray popped out since some people were reporting problems with this. Fortunately for me it worked just fine, it does take a little pressure though. We tend to be more delicate than we should since the phone is new.
  

  Another thing i read on reviews on face book was about how the screen blanks out during a call. I realized this is only because people do not remove the factory screen guard which covers the proximity sensor making the phone think that the phone is against your ear during a call and hence turning the screen light off.
  

  Pros:
  
  1)The price!!!!
  
  2) Its super smooth. The screen is really sensitive. I had a gionee S5.5 before this and the difference in screen response is visible.
  
  3) The hardware on the phone is really awesome. It ships with a snapdragon 801 SOC and not 800 and no this is not an error in CPUZ. When Xiaomi launched the specs, Qualcom had just announced this chipset and later they classified it as 801. A little google can help you find this info.
  
  4) The Battery life is super awesome! with lots of whats app and on 3g all day fiddling with my new phone the battery is at 73% now after 9 hours.
  
  5) Gaming performance is good too.
  
  6) Too many to list. Overall the phone is too good at this price.
  
  7) MIUI is awesome. There is already a firmware update out for our phones from v16.0 to v18.0 which is supposed to be a stable version. Although it said that it was over 500MB for some reason it downloaded really fast on my 8mbps line i.e it took as much time as an normal app takes from the playstore or a corrupt torrent takes to download. I wasnt sure if the update happened correctly but it says version 18.0 now and says im on the latest verstion. The changelog was huge and i didnt bother reading all of it. One visible difference that i could spot was that my contacts used to stutter a lot when scrolling through them. This has been fixed and now scrolling is smooth.
  
  8) Signal strength was pointed out as a problem by some but i found it to be good so far. I checked with a friends xperia and we both get around the same signal in office on 3g around -85 dBM ( the closer it is to 60 the better it is i guess)
  

  Cons
  
  1)) The audio quality is decent at best and not what i thought it would be. This was one of the primary reasons i ditched the gionee as that had very bad audio quality. I was lead to believe that this phone uses a cirrus logic DAC the same as on the iPhones and expected the sound with earphones to be audiophile quality. But its just decent at best. Maybe a software can fix it i dont know for sure. I currently use the sony MDR XBA90 which i think are above average earphones. I used poweramp and managed to tweak it to suit my taste but the sound stage is very narrow and sometimes the bass eats into the mids. But overall tolerable audio quality if you are not an audiophille. Certainly not as bad as the gionee s5.5.
  
  2) Camera is decent. I haven't played around with it much in good light. But inside the office images were of poor quality and appeared to be very grainy and not so sharp.
  
  3) Minor software issues like i cant get the operator name to not show in my notification on my lock screen.
  
  4) Previously i owned the Galaxy S, The SII and then the gionee s5.5 so yes i miss the punchy AMOLED colours. Dont get me wrong. This screen by all means is beautiful but just lacks that little extra punch. Some say AMOLEDs are too artificial in their colour rendering but i guess its a personal choice.
  
  5) The size is pretty big and while the Gionee was of equal size i still wouldnt feel it in my pocket due to its slim form. This i can really feel if my pants are a little tight. I use an S-line TPU case which probably adds to the bulk.
  
  6) Shortage of accessories. After the launch date the same TPU case that i bought for 350 on ebay a day before the launch is now retailing for 1199 same with all other screen guards and accessories.
  

  Overall I am super happy with the purchase. For this price i cant ask for more. I really hope all of you out there who want to buy this are able to do so next time. My good wishes are with you guys.

column6: MIUI hangs frequently, slippery design, service centres useless: no
column7:
I have never written a 1-star review before on Flipkart, but after Rs 20,000 in, I feel compelled to warn other respectable members of society what they are getting themselves into. It's an awful product.
  

  First of all, MIUI was a horrible software user experience. Apps like WhatsApp and Pocket frequently kept crashing, and these are some of the lighter and best built apps around. It can be so frustrating when you are in the middle of writing a long message and the entire app crashes. Felt like I was using Windows on a phone! Blue screen of death indeed.
  

  Next, the actual phone itself is so terribly built it's ridiculous. The shiny MI logo at the top is so distracting and really ruins any video viewing experience. It is so unnecessary, I mean it is such a peculiar looking phone people will literally stop you in the streets to ask you what you are carrying. They did to me. More than just once, I assure you.
  

  The screen itself is so poorly designed, it's almost an achievement! The bezels on the sides are so thin, when you are holding the phone and reading say, a news article, you may often see issues with you palm accidentally touching the end-to-end screen. Within one month, the lower-half of the screen was completely non-responsive and the touchscreen only worked in the top-half of the phone.
  

  Don't even get me started on the back case. If after reading this review you still somehow want to buy this awful device, please get two things, a brain scan and a phone case. The back cover is so slippery it's not even funny. I kept dropping it because of the slippery brushed metal back and round edges.
  

  The phone marketing claims that it has been drop-tested from a height of 3 feet hundreds of times. Well this is news to me, since after simply dropping it from less than half a foot on a table, there was a very tiny, quarter-inch crack in the top right corner of the screen. When I took it to the Xiaomi service centre the next day, I was told that the entire screen would have to be replaced and that would cost Rs 7,000.
  

  Apparently, the warranty doesn't mean anything! And there is no additional Apple Care-like option where we can pay some sort of insurance against scratches and cracks, especially for a screen that is nearly 5 inches and very likely to have more than a few scuffs. Bravo! /sarcasm/
  

  What on earth is the point of setting up so many service centres across the country if the cost of repairing the phone is half the price of the actual phone? The main reason people bought the phone was they looked at the specs online, looked at the price and knew that it was a real company with paying customers in China. Well turns out specs are useless if the UI keeps crashing, and low cost is a joke when repairing a tiny scratch costs Rs 7000.
  

  Very disappointed. Horrible User Experience in the software, slippery hardware and expensive servicing. 13k down the drain, phone is unusable now. Maybe it was just me, maybe it was Xiaomi, I guess it just wasn't meant to be.

  The instances of loudspeaker not working, the touch screen behaving erratic and the phone not responding to the touch.
  
  I shared my troubles with FLIPKART customer service, and was given a reluctant service in 3 days.Those initial 3 days, very very anxious moments for me, because i wanted to believe the XIAOMI story, and was fully on board it, but the product was not living upto its promise.Adding to the woes were FLIPKART's challenged TECH SUPPORT team, who could not even tell me the correct procedure to upgrade my ROM, for which eventually i had to google out the method, thanks to the MIUI FORUM in English (i had not expected it then ), my day was saved.
  
  However once the ROM was upgraded to 33.0, the troubles went away, and it has been a trouble free experience so far. In fact a new upgrade to ROM 34.0 was made available two days ago, and post up gradation, though there is no substantial changes that i can feel, but the good thing is that the phone works the way it should, and i face no new troubles.
  

  All the tech specs, and the other reviews from the INTERNET will make you understand the product, hence will not get into those.
  
  However, i would like to point out the other softer aspects of the device and its interface, which has been really thought through.
  
  THE TOP 4 POSITIVES ARE :
  
  1) AMAZING BATTERY LIFE, gives me upto 40 hrs, i.e almost 2 days on a single charge. ( all this while, my mobile data or WIFI is alternatively on, and i have moderate gaming for 15-30 mins a day on games like asphalt 8 / subway surfer, each day.
  
  However pls note that each day fron 12 in the night to 5 in the morning, the phone is on the airplane mode>>> this can be done with the help of the power saving feature, and tuned as per one's wish.
  
  2) VERY CLEAN and simple UI, a very refreshing change from STOCK ANDRIOD, and no learning curve required to understand MIUI.
  
  3) Ability to manage the individual permissions of each app, i.e. which app can access what features like GPS, CAMERA, CONTACTS etc. ( would like to bring to attention, that, as far as my knowledge goes, stock andriod phones, generally don't have this feature>> pls correct me, if i am wrong here )
  
  4) Supports sync with BLUE TOOTH LOW ENERGY devices like FITBIT ONE ( BLE Support ). I had a FITBIT ONE, and was very excited when it synced to the FITBIT app on MI3.
  

  TOP 4 NEGATIVES
  

  1) Absence of service center for the devices, barring the METROS & of all the reviews and experiences of others i have read on the internet, it is not at all encouraging.
  
  2) Absence of the MI3 piston headphones, to go along with the phone. ( i had ordered it, when it was made available for a short period, but the product never got delivered to me, apparently, lost in transit >> i seriously believe that some smart alec in the logistic chain would have realized the potential to black market it, and made good of it. The reason, i say this is because some sellers on ebay india is selling so called original piston headphones for Rs 2999/- )
  
  3) Radio no longer works without a headphone. In the ROM version 32, one could listen to the RADIO, even without plugging the external headphone, but post the upgrade to 33 & subsequent ROM 34, it is gone.
  
  4) Not impressive LOUDSPEAKER
  

  Having outlined, the +ves as well as the -ves, i think this device is worth a buy, if the flash sales open up again, for people who are looking for a good bargain, and don't want to splurge money, yet want to be savvy

column6: More Than Worth The Price....!!! Wonder How Xiaomi Does That ! (Do Read the Bugs Section of this Review)
column7:
This is a totally unbiased review of the device. I'm writing this review after having used the device for more than 10 says. Apart from a few bugs that I noticed (see the bugs section below), Mi3 worked perfectly to my satisfaction.
  

  Core Performance-    The phone is working flawlessly. You won't notice any lags whatsoever. In fact its much less laggy than the Galaxy S5 and even the LG G3. In gaming also I did't notice any kind of frame drop. 1080p videos played flawlessly. In terms of fluidity of the UI and gaming performance, Mi3 definitely puts the likes of S5 and G3 to shame.
  

  Camera- To give you an idea about the camera, all that I would say is the camera on Mi3 is comparable to the camera on Galaxy S4. Yes, S5's camera is definitely slightly better (mark the word slightly here), thanks to its faster focusing capability. Mi3's camera is much better than that of Nexus 5. Also, both the cameras are capable of 1080p HD video recording.
  

  Display-  Hats off to Xiaomi in this department. The  display of Mi3 is just Fabulous. Even the auto brightness works very well.
  

  Call Quality- Excellent. One of the best I've ever seen (rather heard) on any smartphone. Crystal Clear is the word.
  

  Audio Output - This is actually one of the strongest areas of Mi3. Xiaomi has provided some audio profiles for headsets and these profiles, I must say, work great. The music quality that you get from the earphone is Mind Blowing !
  

  UI - In the UI department I'd say it depends on your preference. As far as my personal preference  is concerned, though I have no issues with the MIUI, but still, I personally find stock Android slightly better to my taste. Again, its strictly a matter of personal preference. Many people install MIUI even on their Nexus. (For the uninitiated, MIUI is actually a custom ROM, just like CynogenMod and can be installed on almost any device after rooting).
  

  Battery Life-  The battery life was definitely not great, but still above average. I must say it was much better than Nexus 5. You may expect a full 1 day of battery life in normal usage. Maximum Screen On time that I got was around 4 hours or so. I used the device in High Performance mode without any power saving enabled.
  

  Bugs- Lastly I'd like to talk about a few bugs that I encountered on Mi3. Before you read about the bugs, I'd like to mention that almost all the devices have their own share of bugs and no device is actually bug free. So there is no need to form a bad impression of Mi3 after reading about the bugs. Following are the few bugs (or issues) that I found on Mi3.
  

  1.) Music playback sometimes suddenly stops while multitasking. This usually happens while browsing on device photos (especially using the G+ Photos app). Sometimes it also happens while using the Chrome browser. And this happens even with third party music players. Again I'd like to mention, it doesn't happen everytime (though while browsing on device photos using G+ photos app it happens most of the times, but rarely happens while using the default Gallery app for the purpose). Most of the times I've seen it happen when the device has not been rebooted for more than 48 hours.
  

  2.) "OK Google" keyword doesn't work well. It works within the Google Now app, but doesn't work well from any screen.
  

  3.) If alarm is set using Google Now (Voice Command) using the default clock app, the Snooze option doesn't work when the alarm rings, instead the cloak app just crashes (becomes unresponsive). However, there is no problem if the alarm is set from within the app (not using Google Now Voice Command). This is not a big problem, and can easily be solved by using a third party alarm clock app that supports Google Now instructions. You can easily find many such apps for free on the Play Store.
  

  4.) "Prevent Pocket Dial" option under Display settings doesn't seem to work. Nothing really to worry about that. Just lock the screen before putting the phone in your pocket.

column6: Review - Pros and Cons of  MI3
column7:
There are lots of detailed technical reviews about Xiomi MI3 on the internet. Most, but not all, is true. I will not repeat them. The review below is my personal experience with Xiaomi and Flipkart.
  

  Got a hit on my third attempt at Flipkart on 26th aug. Took about 30 minutes to confirm order and pay online. The promised delivery date was 1st Sep but was delivered on 28th Aug afternoon exactly 48 hours after placing order. Brilliant!
  

  Good packing material. A bit disappointed with the manual. The phone, cable and charger and steel pin (for ejecting SIM card were OK.
  

  I put in my airtel 2G sim card (normal size). Phone worked satisfactorily. Though I had disabled GPRS the MI3 activated the GPRS and  connected to the internet on its own! The speed was slow so I upgraded to 3G and  things improved considerably.
  

  Now for the Pro's and Con's.
  
  The CON's first.
  
  My main worries are about the service. What happens if there is a major fault after 30 days. What about battery replacement?
  
  The software is good but far below apple's IOS.  APP's are limited.
  
  The software on the MI3 works reasonably well. A lot of brilliant features but also lots of glitches. It picks up a lot of details and photos about your contacts from gmail, facebook etc. and messes up your contact list. Wants to repeatedly access your contact list.
  

  Loading files from PC to mobile on Kitkat 4 is not easy. Using FTP (but only with wireless) I was able to transfer from Mobile to PC but not the other way around.
  

  The speakers are a bit tinny.
  

  The PRO's
  
  The MI3 looks real good. Colleagues and even causal strangers noticed it  and wanted to see and admire it. The screen resolution and size, especially its thickness (8mm) is amazing!
  
  I was able to install and use whatsapp and mobile banking software with ease. Lots of software features make it a real pleasure to use the MI3.  The speed is excellent. Wireless, 3G, etc spot on.
  
  The 13 MP camera is superb. The dual LED flash good.
  

  CONCLUSION: If XIAOMI can address the service problems and a few glitches on its software the MI3 is a hands down winner. It looks and performs better than phones twice its cost.

column6: My hands on experience after 1 weeks use.
column7:
Its been a  week since I am using Xiaomi Mi3, so I will be of a great help to others if I put my review for this phone.
  
  Before that, let me clarify that:
  
  1)	Xiaomi Mi3 is the first product I bought on flipkart.com. I succeeded in second try.
  
  2)	I am in no way attached or interested in doing Xiaomi publicity.
  
  I ordered this phone at flipkart.com on 19th of August and received it on 22nd August.
  
  Flipkart had delivered quickly in a good packing by cash on delivery. I appreciate their services.
  
  On opening the box, I was stunned to look at this premium looking handset. The build quality is by far the best a smart phone can have as per my view. This is a very slim phone. The corning gorilla glass is pretty obvious by merely looking and touching it. I have not used any screen guard since 1 week and their isn't a single scratch on it.
  
  The 2 negatives as per my opinion are
  
  1)	Size, it is large for a 5' screen due to large space at top & bottom. It might have been smaller.
  
  2)	The sharp corners may feel a bit uncomfortable in the pocket. It might have been curved on corners. (but I let go on these points on account of premium looks)
  
  Now lets talk about MIUI. This is the OS highly customized from android kitkat on which the Xiaomi Mi3 operates. No bloatwares are installed and all the customizations are very user friendly. Several preinstalled apps are very useful like cleaner, power saver, virus scanner, torch etc. The UI is clean, attractive and pleasant to use.
  
  The screen is 5' with 441 ppi density. HD videos play smooth. Colours are attractive and pleasant. U can set the color temperature and saturation.
  
  The operations are very smooth. There is no lags or hangs at all while browsing, playing games or using apps. It does heat a little bit while heavy browsing and playing games while 3G is on, but never in normal routine use or calls.
  
  Camera quality is awesome outdoors & indoors and good in very low light conditions using flash. Video shooting is amazing in even 720p. There is simple mode given with minimal settings for regular user and advance mode if u want to set the settings as per ur requirement. Front camera detects ur age and sex when u look at it..!! (although error range is very high as it relies on ur looks :-D to decide). it's a kind of fun to use this like talking tom and talking ginger.
  
  People out there are claiming that their battery lasted for 3 days, but in my 1 week use it has lasted for 1 day and 8 hour at max and 22 hour minimum. It used to take 2 hour 30 min for 100% charging. Upto 60%, charging is very fast within 1 hr but there after its slow. Its heats a little bit while charging but thts normal I think.
  
  The people might not have yet noticed but I coudn't resist to note is the  vibration . Its very different and awesome. When u open the clock, there appears analog clock and with every tick tok of the second hang u feel mild vibrations so it feels like u r holding a small alarm clock actually. That's pretty interesting.
  
  The most important NEGATIVE point to consider is very less number of service centres across the country. I live in Gujarat and nearest service centre for me is 200Km away that too is non functional as someone said in previous review. So, basically It's kind of a gamble to risk ur 13,999/- and expect that u need not have to run to and fro to service centre. XIAOMI MUST REPIDELY OPEN UP NEW SERVICE CENTRES IF THEY WANT TO SUSTAIN THE SALE.
  
  Overall, in less than 14K price, this phone is worth buying and value for each penny u spend. Xiaomi has given premium quality & features at unbelievable price. And for me, Xiaomi is nothing less than a premium brand. I might have bought some sony or micromax phone costing >18,000 and specification almost half than what this is having. Xiaome has saved my 5000 Rs. Thanks a lot. Most welcome to India. We needed you. Please open more service centres, expand your sale, put adequate handsets in market and create a milestone in Indian smartphone history.

So i decided to find it out and after some hours of study found that the issue arises when i put the network selection mode to "Prefer 3G". I changed it to 2G network only or 3G network only..... Perfect it worked (Atleast in my phone)
  

  So guys just try this:- go to settings > mobile network > Preferred network type> Make the selection to either "2G network only" or else "3G network Only" > Restart the Phone.

I was using Xperia mid range phone for 2.5 years, and it is unnecessary to say that it was disgusting to use after just 1 year of use simply because it was slow and it was not smooth any more. So my requirement was simple, no brand fascination, should be fast or smooth (UI and navigation of day to day apps), reasonably priced and should go for at least 2-3 years (bad thing with smart phones these days generally they don't last longer - either for hardware or software no longer supported).
  

  With Moto E/G we saw that low end/cost mobiles can give better performance. So I was looking to buy one Moto (mostly G). It is a coincidence that Xiaomi launched same time I am looking for a new phone. And it ticks all the points I have with some plus points of having a impressive hardware and MiUI. Using it for just 2 days, it is difficult to judge some of the aspects of a new phone (think of reliability), but here are my opinions about the phone:
  

  (+)ve
  
  + Fast, smooth UI, no wonder MiUI is world renowned. Lots of customization option
  
  + Apple iOS like UI feel (transitions are smooth, not too fast or laggy)
  
  + MiUI's many small but good things - torch from home screen, security and permission things many more.
  
  + battery in my average use is good to go for 1 day and some hours without worry (mainly mails, social n/w, whatsapp and whatsnot! 30min call, 1hr of music, some 2D games - its after first full charge, should be better after couple of charges)
  
  + big and bright screen
  
  + hardware is top notch, no heat up issue or freeze so far - using it like maniac (after all new toy :) )
  
  + Though not my regular thing, played Asphalt and some other 3D games, super smooth, and not much heating up.
  
  + Camera has decent details in proper light condition, in low light it is just ok.
  
  + Price
  

  (-) ve
  
  - No memory expansion slot? Fine for me at this moment, but if need arises I have no option inbuilt
  
  - too much fingerprint on screen
  

  Some points to note:
  
  > 5" screen, bezel is not thin, so little bigger than many nicely designed 5" phones out there in market
  
  > No headphone bundled, considering the budget, I can't complain
  
  > No customer service history for Xiaomi India.
  
  > No reliability history for MI phones in India.
  
  > SAR level little higher side than some flagship phones of other brand (if that matters to you), though it is very much within limit.
  
  > Limited accessory available in market at this moment
  

  All in all, a recommended mobile. Only thing is to look out for reliability of the brand and its product.

column6: Tips, Tricks Solutions: a review after receiving MI3
column7:
Till date there have been many reviews and almost everything has been discussed. I will bring on here what issues I faced and how I resolved them.
  
  I received my MI3 on 1st august 2014 after placing the order on 29th May 2014 which is by 3 to 4 days as in between there was a holiday. Even though i registered, it showed me unregistered the first time  sale started, then with help of  Filpkart customer care service, I could get assistance and was able to bring MI into my cart, after which i could place order. Now, coming to post delivery, I found Manual to be missing which actually makes life of  new bee in MI  like me  little hard. But there are plenty of solution too. Let me discuss straight way problems and solutions in my case. Hope it helps solving your problems  too if any.
  

  1. Sim Card tray: As no pin has been provided with the phone in the box i received , I couldn't get how to open the tray. For help, Please refer video tutorial there are online videos avalabile demonstrating how to open tray. But as I did , please do use paper pin to push it a little hard, and the tray will eject and once you get to know no further problem.
  

  2. Apps could not connect to internet: I have already have a 3G pack installed in my sim but apps were not atall able to come online, neither crome, whatsapp, nor skype or even browser. Surprisingly, playstore was going on well and download speed was lighting fast.
  
  For this problem, the solution is factory reset.
  

  settings> backup and reset> turn on back up my data> turn on automatic restore> and then go for factory data reset. All app settings will be deleted but not the downloaded files, apps or cam pictures, nothing to worry.
  
  Just reinsert the sim and violaaa!! you are done.
  

  3 All the users if you are struggling with MI user interface then there is MI community and forum for help. You can even download custom ROM and make use to cutomize whatever you want.
  
  here is the user guide
  
  use http ---> en.miui.com/thread-31199-1-1.html
  

  4. This phone is a power user. Lighting fast and no lagging. Please turn off all unnecessary apps and 3G or wifi if not required. Also keep in battery saver mode  to get the maximum.
  

  5. There is a cover on the screen which comes with the delivery of the mobile. Make sure you remove it and then use otherwise the screen will black out. There is also instruction given on the right top side to  Tear off the so called screen guard. So make sure you follow that.
  

  6. Camera: Put the camera on HDR mode and use, you will definitely be satisfied. Yes in dark, the quality is in question. But still very happy considering other features.
  

  7. Storage: Although no external card slot and only recommended 16GB, you will get 11.35 GB usable. This is the area i think could have been a bit better. But for users like me with moderate game freak and music, and app lover, I think 11 GB is still enough to be filled. (at least for me) so no complaints.
  

  My Verdict: The phone is a wonderful product, and there is no doubt about that. Samsung and other brands will have to think now with new marketing strategies. The configuration is as such that it qualifies  with the price range of 25000 to 30000 in INR if you choose HTC SONY or SAMSUNG or any other.  Another noticeable fact is user interface can be considered to be a copy of Iphone (IOS). Most features of Iphone Interface has been broadly implemented. So that becomes a Iphone feeling when you use this Android.
  

  Flipkart reviews did help me too, so while you go for purchase  or even post purchase do search and try find out in what ever you have confusion. Please people don't complain as many people who like spoon feeding want a very easy user friendly GUI. The fact can be considered as using windows XP vs Linux or Apple Macintosh Operating Systems. Windows can be very friendly GUI but not as efficient and stable as Linux or Mac
  
  MI comes will bundle of settings and customization at all levels which when you understand, you will love it most.
  
  So keep exploring and keep loving it. It is definitely a  must buy.
  

  Last but not least another trick for you guys how to make purchase in Flipkart so that you can get it in your cart. Open flipkart and register  yourself for the sale. On the day of sale  be online on the site atleast half an hour before sale starts, and exactly the time  when the sale starts and the counter begins count 5,4,3 2,1,0 hit refresh button on the buy page. Definitely you will be able to grab one on that very day of sale. (This strategy worked for me and also recommended by Flipkart Customer Executives)
  

  Caution: Please do check the box contents you receive and check if anything is missing. In my case Pin for opening the tray and user guide is missing. If you find them missing please report to Flipkart, I have raised this issue too.
  

  Finally,  Thanks for your time friends..
  
  Thanks Flipkart as well.
  

  BR, Aparajit

Got my Mi3 on Aug 24'th so its been One month since I got my phone. I have been testing this phone a lot and I am happy to say that we have got a knockout champion here which will defeat any device in its price range or even double the price. I will not go into specs as everybody knows it.
  

  Pros.
  

  1.DISPLAY
  

  Big beautiful 1080p display ( out of the box the display looks yellowish even after setting the colour temperature to cool but by gradual use you will notice a difference. It will not go completely but after one month of use this dont bother me at all compared to the initial stage)
  

  2.SOUND
  

  Loud and balanced sound output from the external speakers ( Not upto HTC one level but sound output is more than you would expect from this device.)
  

  3. PERFORMANCE
  

  As you all know this is a performace beast. Throw it anything and will eat it for breakfast. It does heat up a little while playing heavy games like Asphalt 8 for more than 15-20 mins but heat is not a major issue. Still I would not suggest extensive gaming for 1-2 hours without any break. Play games for 20-30 mins then give it some time to kool down ( 10-15 mins)
  

  4.BATTERY
  

  This is where I was blown away completely. My battery lasts almost 2 days with light usage and 1.5 days with medium usage. Battery lasts almost 1 day with medium to heavy usage.( data or wifi full on. All day whatsapp. Occasional facebook and twitter. Some casual gaming and 1-2 hours of video playback and 2-3 hours of music playback).
  
  Battery will last only 7-8 hours in extreme usage( Wifi or data on all the time. Heavy face book,twitter and youtube. All day whatsapp. 3-4 hours of video and music. And 1-1.5 hours of heavy gaming like Real racing 3, Dead trigger 2 and Asphalt 8)
  
  Out of the box I was really disappointed with the battery life as I was only able to get 12-14 hours with medium usage but after fiddling with the settings and proper charging and discharging routines now my Mi3 is champ in this reign.
  
  Here are my battery saving tips.
  
  a) Dont use any battery saving apps from playstore( Trickle charging is already present in Mi3)
  
  b) Charge your device without any breakage. I mean put your phone for charging when your battery reaches 15-20 percent and let the device charge up to 100 percent without any usage. After 98 percent phone will take approx. 30-40 min to fully charge.
  
  c) If possible put your phone to aeroplane mode while charging ( this will result in quicker charging also). Never use your phone while charging as it will result in simultaneous charging-discharging. Besides using Ur phone while charging is never safe with any device
  
  d) Discharge your battery completely once in a month for extended battery life
  
  e) Turn the auto brightness on and keep your device to 60-70 percent of the brightness level( Trust me this and the next step will make your battery life really longer even double the time  what you are getting now)
  
  f) If possible don't sign into Xiaomi cloud storage and turn off auto sync. ( You can turn on auto sync for face book and whatsapp seperately)
  

  To conclude I am really satisfied with the device more than I thought I would. for 13999 this is the bargain of the century. Though I am little worried about the lack of service centers and parts availability the build quality of the device gives me some relief that I wont be needing a service center as long as I use my Mi3 with proper care.
  

  PS: Also bought the Mi3 flipcover and Powerbank. Great quality products. Though at first I thought the flipcover was overpriced @ 559 but after using it for more than 10 days I can guarantee you its totally worth the money. At 999 powerbank is a deal to steal.
  

  Thanks for reading my review.

column6: Leaving the Price Behind. (Plus comparison with HTC One M7) ( 1 week usage review)
column7:
My review won't focus on how this phone is the best below 15K but will really focus on the phone itself. I will also compare it with my HTC One M7.
  

  1) Packaging : The Eco Friendly box that it comes in,holds just the phone and charger-cum-data cable. No surprises as I was expecting this since I got Moto G.
  

  2) Gaming Performance : No doubt the specs scream that it's blazing fast. throw any game at it and it plays without breaking a sweat. Adreno 330 in Mi3 is significantly better than Adreno 320 on my HTC One M7.
  

  3) Browsing : The stock MIUI browser is really fast, you wont need to use Chrome after that, but that's stiil a user's preference. Stock Browser has very simple interface and is a joy to use.
  

  3) Design : Even after being Silver color, it never looks or feels like a cheap Chinese phone. The build quality is comparable to Lumia 900 and the fit and finish is also great. This phone feels very solid to hold and everyone who held it was surprised that it was so light in spite of it's large size. However it cannot be compared to HTC One in design as HTC is much better designed has the metal feel which nothing can beat.
  

  4) Screen : I am not impressed by this screen and there are a few reasons for that. Firstly, the screen doesn't feel that sharp for a 1080p display. you can see some grains on the screen (No, it's not the theme!!) when you look closely making it feel like a Pentile display. Secondly, the display gets heat up quite easily and this heat is only only felt when you keep the phone in your pocket. Thirdly, it's not that power efficient, but the large 3050Mah offsets it completely. Apart from these, the display produces very nice colors and saturation levels are not that high. The viewing angles are also very great. HTC One's screen beats it in every segment hands down.
  
  The touch is very responsive albeit a bit too sensitive for me. The screen is NOT a fingerprint magnet as suggested by some. The glove mode is not at all helpful for me as it failed to register touches when i had my gloves on.
  

  5) Camera : This one is really a surprise for me. I never liked the Low-light performance of Exmor sensor used in Mi3. But if you know how to take low light photos then you are in for a treat. Some low light samples were really impressive and had very less grains as compared to Sony phones which uses the same sensor. But I still feels that this sensor lacks the dynamic range that it's competitors offer.  In good lighting conditions the photos were nice as expected and it just crushes the camera of my HTC One. However in low light, HTC One is the clear winner as it can take better pics even when on Auto Mode.
  
  Video quality is a bit underwhelming as the videos looked highly post processed and lacked sharpness.
  

  6) Audio Quality : Tested using Klipsch Image S4. I am used to the sound of HTC One which is the best in business (if you know how to tweak the equalization). When I first listened to Mi3, I was a bit disappointed.With DiracSound enabled, the soundstage is great but the music lacks the warmth which HTC provides. Overall, the sound is very flat (good for audiphiles) but lacks the loudness as well as the fidelity of HTC. I love the sound of HTC anyday even if it is a bit colored.
  

  7) Speaker Quality : The speaker soung is great and never feels like a cheap unit, it provides a good soundstage as well as bit of sparkle. But again it doesn't even come close to HTC One's Boomsound Stereo Speakers. No explanation needed.
  

  8) Battery : The best part about this phone. I used the phone fairly heavy and still the battery lasted for more than 15 hours ( including 45 mins gaming, 1 hour 3G surfing, 30 mins calling and about 50 photos without flash). In normal daily use the battery will easing last for 24+ hours. Kudos to MIUI for it's lightness and efficiency.
  

  9) UI : MIUI v5 feels a bit restricted for an Android ROM at first sight, but underneath there are a ton of customizations waiting. The MIUI themes are the most advanced themes, it changes many things from icons to locksreen unlocking styles. MIUI is made to feel like iOS with the absence of app drawer and it actually makes the OS to be easy to use. Plus, there is almost zero lags in the UI. So overall a refreshing UI.
  

  10) Conclusion : While reviewing this phone I didn't give it an advantage of it being a cheaper phone (as we all know that Xiaomi sells it nearly at manufacturing cost and all flagships are manufactured at about the same cost). It is a flagship device and justifies it's title. Go for it even if you are about to buy a phone worth 35K. As with service centers, even HTC service is quite pathetic so if you can buy a HTC then no. of service centers shouldn't be an issue.

  The phone is lightning fast in all transitions. Even if you are playing heavy graphics games or play HD video, pressing the Home screen takes you instantly to App drawer. Downloaded games/Apps and watched youtube video simultaneously while having whatsapp, gmail running and found no performance issue.
  

  Screen:
  
  Screen is lively and colours are crisp. Have watched movies in 720p and seen full HD videos on youtube and found it impressive.
  

  Call quality:
  
  the sound quality is good and i found no issues while taking calls.
  

  MIUI:
  
  This is the one I want to talk a lot about as I was most skeptical about this initially. I should say I was completely wrong and MIUI is much better than stock android. It is simple, fast and has lots of customisations that can be done and privacy protection at individual app level. All usual things that you may want to do on your phone have a shortcut in notification bar. You can assign functions to different buttons. It automatically merged duplicate contacts and rearranged them for me. Having said that, As always with software, there is always room for better.
  

  Connectivity ( Wifi/3G/GPS):
  
  The phone shows good Wifi signal reception at distances where my old Samsung Galaxy ace used to show weak signal. NO issues in download over Wifi. have downloaded Gbs of data till now.
  
  Have verified Skype video quality on 3G and it indicates good 3G reception.
  
  GPS was able to lock easily while at home. But still have to verify while travelling.

  Rear camera is good. The low light performance is not great. Also, the picture is darker when taken with a light source in background which is a common problem with almost all cameras even in 20K range. Xperia Z2, Galaxy S5 might be better in this segment.
  
  Front camera is good for skype video calls but not that great for selfies.
  

  Battery:

First of all, let me tell you the basics: This smartphone has Qualcom Snapdragon 820 processor with Adreno 530 GPU with 32GB Internal and 3 GB RAM. Considering price, everybody is like why not add 4000-5000 more and buy One plus 3. Let me tell you that One+ 3 and One+ 3T currently have heating issues which goes upto 50 degree and you can check that out on youtube. MI 5 also had heating issues but it got resolved after updating from MIUI 7 to MIUI 8. Many people reviewed that it gets heated a lot while charging. It did not happen for me. There are other phones which offers even more RAM. But remember RAM is only for Multi tasking and not for the application speed. Your application speed depends on your Processor which is the latest in this phone though under clocked but even then faster than all other Qualcom chipsets. Coming down to phone:
  
  Pros:
  
  1. Great Build. Very sleek. Elegant and beautiful.
  
  2. Touch Response rate is very fast and amazing.
  
  3. Fingerprint sensor is very accurate.
  
  4. Rear camera quality is awesome. You can record video at 4K or slow motion which captures everything with clarity.
  
  5. Front camera though it is just 4 MP but click great selfies. I just love this. Its far better than my previous HTC 826 camera which was 13 MP.
  
  6. Battery goes upto 1.5 days with internet, gaming, music, videos, capturing photos and calls. So now I am happy and relieved.
  
  7. Though this phone supports quick charge 3.0 but in the Box you will get quick charge 2.0 but even with that, I am able to charge from 20% to 100% in less than an hour which goes for 1.5 days. I feel so great. No need of powerbank for this phone. :)
  
  8. Sound quality of the loudspeaker as well as earphones are good. Lot of people complaint that audio quality is pretty bad and when I used for the first time, even I thought so. But there is setting within this MIUI8 where you can tweak with equaliser, MI Sound Enhancer and kind of earphones selection to get better output. I am using Sennheiser earphones and the quality is pretty good. You can say that its not that loud, but seriously, if you want to listen to loud music, you can buy a Home Theatre. I have F&D F6000U and it got great bass. Overall, I did not feel any need for even louder loudspeaker or in-ear sound output.

Short review:
  
  Mi5 is perhaps the best phone for less than INR40k. It certainly is a case of  you get more than you pay for. 
  
  If you want a phone that does all and then some, just get Mi5. Yes, there is no brand assurance like Apple and Samsung, but then Xiaomi is no obscure Chinese and certainly Mi5 is no slouch. It definitely feels and behaves like a flagship phone, and only loses out by a whisker to the likes of iPhone 7 and Google Pixel.
  

  Detailed notes:
  

  Exteriors: Mi5 is beautiful. Yes, that's the word. The moment you hold it in your hands, you realize that its beautiful with those curved edges, near bezel-less display and gorilla glass 4 back panel. While the phone has solid unibody design meaning that you can't remove the battery, it is surprisingly light at 129g.
  

  Performance: Mi5 uses top of the line chipset married with fast RAM and ROM, optimized to deliver exceptional performance. All this translates to buttery smooth user experience. While the detailed performance metrics can be found on review sites, I got Antutu score in excess of 120k.
  

  Software: MIUI 8 running on Mi5 is one of the best interfaces that I've used thus far. The software optimizations run deep and the Mi5 engineers have done a stellar job to customize the whole UI with great attention to detail. Just to give you a perspective, I tried Touch Wiz UI and it felt downright ugly and inconsistent compared to MIUI. Yes, MIUI is that good. And all those android purists can go buy those utterly disappointing Moto phones, for everyone else, MIUI just about does the job.
  

  Multimedia: Mi5 has a 16MP (Sony 298 sensor) rear camera with 4 Axis OIS. The rear camera performs well, has fast PDAF coupled with capable OIS. The image quality is excellent with high DR and low noise. The front camera is 4MP (ultrapixel technology) which allows it to keep noise levels low, and bumps the DR. All of this translates into selfies which can put the likes of Oppo F1 and Asus Zenfone Selfie with their 13MP selfies to shame. I conducted a real life shootout with Sony C5 Ultra (which has one of the best selfie cameras in the market) and was pleasantly surprised to find that Mi5 selfie stood its ground with lower noise and more mature image processing.
  

  Battery: Mi5 has 3000mAH non-user removable battery. The software optimizations allow Mi5 to easily handle a day's use. With light use, the battery can last more than 2 days.
  

  Afterthoughts: Special mention to that lovely display. Mi5 has a colour calibrated 5.15in display which is extremely bright at 600nits and deep blacks. It certainly comes very close to AMOLED experience. For the discerning users (photography enthusiasts) who care about true colour reproduction, the screen would be a delight. While the display is smallish by 2017 standards, the addition of home button and soft keys at the bottom free up that much needed screen space.
  

  PS: And if some of you might be thinking this is a paid review, I'd suggest get the Mi5 to experience echo of thoughts :)

So I am a Nexus 6 user. And I got a JIO sim. Nexus 6 not being a dual sim handset my search for one started. I was lucky twice in the one plus 3 T flash sale. But somehow i didn't felt like spending 29k. So I started looking for an alternate option. My criteria was a dual sim handset having a snapdragon 820 processor. Saw Xiaomi Mi5 being used by a friend and got good feedback. It fit bid perfectly (got it for 18,453 after the offers applied in Flipkart sale). I placed the order on December 21 11am, and I was holding the handset on December 22, 5pm. EXCELLENT job in fast delivery without paying extra for one day delivery. So coming to the point: How's the phone. Here's my review/experience so far:
  

  1. It feels premium in terms of styling as well as feel. It's very slippery (imagine holding a bar of wet soap and try flipping it by holding it in one hand, that's how the phone is slippery), so it feels fragile. Back cover is MUST. Black looks more premium over white.
  
  2. I upgraded to MIUI8 the moment I saw an update. Installed all applications along with GOOD for enterprise (GFE) which is is a corporate mandate for office emails. To my horror GFE identified my device as jail broken/rooted. I carried a test using root checker and it said the device is partially rooted. I was surprised. I spent a day researching on how I can get GFE working. Per the forums, the culprit is TWRP 3+ that gets flashed with MIUI8 update and to get GFE working i had to flash TWRP2.8.7.0 without changing the ROM. I couldn't find this version for download and also I couldn't boot the device in fast boot mode (recovery never loaded, only he fast boot image was displayed). So I was stuck and was contemplating to return the device. But decided to give a final try by doing a factory reset. I did it. After that I was still on MIUI8. Tried GFE again and luckily it worked. PHEW! I was happy to not return the phone was i was sold for its styling and just wanted to keep it now as GFE was working.
  
  3. Performance is amazing for general use (i am not a gamer). Full charge needs around 90min. Battery lasts for a working day 7-8hours over heavy use: Constant online 4G/Wi-Fi, voice calls, and other messaging applications, email usage. Otherwise it will easily last 9-10hours. Even on battery saver I found the device fast (unlike Nexus 6 which seemed exhausted). I verified the device on Antutu officer. In terms of Antutu score the device didn't appear in first 10. Again no complaints. I didnt want to buy a device burning a hole in pocket and see it rank in first three ranks on benchmark.
  
  4. I found the phone warning a bit on top right part in the initial two days. But there's absolutely no heating  given my pattern of heavy usage.
  
  5. Finger print sensor works perfectly (once a while experience a glitch but no complaints). Double tap on it and it behaves like a home function which is very cool feature of MIUI. So is double tap to wake the screen. On power turn on, somehow the finger print sensor never works and you will have to unlock the device using pattern/password. MIUI also let's you switch the function of left and right buttons back versus app list. Google search will reveal more cool MIUI features.
  
  6. Camera takes excellent pictures in day light. Of course low light pictures might not have all those details, but again no complaints as low light photography is rare. Videos have enough detail. I have read online that it shoots 4k but might be a lower fps (30) compared to my earlier Nexus 6 which shoots 4k at 60fps i believe. So Mi5 videos were played on my 4year old LCD TV  but Nexus 6 videos couldn't be played on same TV. So the lower fps on mi5 is a blessing in disguise for me.
  
  7. MIUI has cool themes so I am not missing the stock android experience on Nexus 6. It took time for me to get used to the 'home screens only' mode of MIUI versus the 'home screens + apps view" of Nexus 6. There's a little room on the first home screen to place your frequently used app, so you will have to organ ize a bit.
  
  8. Audio quality is acceptable at full volume. I didn't test the headphones as I never use them much.
  
  9. Bluetooth paired perfectly with my car's audio system.
  
  10. I was used to rooting devices and flashing custom ROMs on Nexus 6. I won't be doing that on mi5 as I cannot afford to stop GFE from working. Rooting and flashing MI devices doesn't seem to be that easy (at least from what I have read, but there would be still users who are adept to it).
  
  11. Display is full HD. And it serves the purpose.
  
  Overall an excellent VFM phone, would have given it 5 stars had it not been the glitch with getting GFE working.
