column7:
NOTE: I have purchased Redmi Note4 4GB-64GB version in very first Flash sale and using it since then.
  
  After getting the desired Results, I Purchased 3GB-32GB version from Flipkart for my Father.
  
  Following are the Observations,
  
  Pros:
  
  1) All 3 versions have Qualcomm Snapdragon 625 64 bit Processor(2ghz Octa core).
  
  # This Processor perfectly balances the Battery life & Performance.
  
  2) Screen is 5.5inches 2.5d slightly Curved at the edges.
  
  3) Has memory expansion option upto 128GB ( Hybrid slot).
  
  4) Most Importantly Battery Life is 20% Better than Note 3, beause of Snapdragon 625 Processor.
  
  ( Check the Genuine Battery Perfomance stats below the Cons )
  
  5) Built Quality is Improved over Redmi Note 3.
  
  6) Finger Print sensor is Lightening Quick.
  
  7) Phone Handles Heavy games like NOVA, Modern Combact 5, Ashpalt 8, etc Smoothly.
  
  8) With heavy multitasking NO LAGS Detected yet.
  
  9) Also NO Substantial Heating Noted.
  
  10) Camera Quality is reasonable for the Price and Better than Note 3.
  
  11) Has Lots of sensor like accelerometer, gyro, Infrared Blastor, etc.
  
  12) Supports Dual Sim.I am Using JIO Sim with it and I get good Performance.
  
  13) Device gets Regular Software Updates.
  
  Cons:
  
  1) NO Quick Charging Supported.
  
  2) Video Recording Quality is Not that Good.Honor 6x & Moto g4+ has Better camera Quality.
  
  # I certainly Not Recommend it for Vloging.
  
  3) Back is bit Slippery.
  
  4) Can't Get Same Performance with 2GB Ram version (my friend has one).
  
  5) No Earphone Inlcuded in Package.
  
  6) Display is NOT Corning Gorila Glass, which makes it vulnerable to Damage.
  
  7) 4GB version gives 2.2GB max. Ram even if All Apps are closed.
  
  8) Design is Very Similar to Note 3.
  
  Battery Performance Stats:
  
  # Charging from 0 to 100% takes 2hrs 30mins. with 2Amp stock charger.
  
  # Battery Performance is Better than Note 3 & Redmi 3s Prime, even if Battery is Same(4100mah).
  
  Usage Mode ---> Battery Performance(Avg.)
  
  =============================================================================
  
  @ Mobile Data(3g/4g) Used Continously ---> 9 Hrs.
  
  @ Mobile Data ON + GPS ON + Normal Calling ---> Roughly 1.5 Days.
  
  @ Normal Calling Only + Standby ---> Almost 2 Days.
  
  @ Normal Calling + Music Playback( Continuous ) ---> 9 Hrs.
  
  @ Internet Usage on WiFi Only( No Calling ) ---> 12 Hrs.
  
  @ Gaming ( Wifi) ---> 7-8.5 Hrs.
  
  @ Gaming ( without WiFi ) ---> 8-9.5 Hrs.
  
  @ Video Playback ---> 13 Hrs.
  
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  VERDICT:
  
  If you Already have Redmi Note 3 or 3s Prime, then Don't Buy it.
  
  If you are purchasing your 1st MI phone, then Definitely Go For it.
  
  DO NOT Purchase 2GB Version, you won't get Best Performance out of it.
  
  Atleast Purchase 3GB Version.
  
  Finally, for Battery Hunters. If Not satisfied with this Beast, then they can go for Lenovo P2.
  
  It will give you 4+ Hrs of Performance compared to Redmi Note 4.
  

  If you find this review Helpful, then Please Hit YES/Helpful Button.
  
  Thank You for reading this Review.

column7:
I was taken by all the hype and publicity around Xiomi Redmi, so I didn't really properly read the reviews before deciding to buy. I trusted Flipkart and ordered the phone. And, I sorely regret it.
  

  After using Redmi Note 4G for 3 weeks now, I can tell from my experience that this handset has some serious quality issues and shame on Flipkart and Xiomi to push such defective products on gullible customers who fall for such tactics of creating artificial scarcity.
  

  The premise of online shopping is that the customer trusts the online seller, and the customer trusts that the product that he/she is ordering will be free of defect and provide a reasonable service as expected/advertised of the product.
  
  Because when ordering online the buyer cannot touch, see and hold the product.
  
  When we buy from a physical store we can operate the handset, see its feature, see the camera etc and then make the buy or not buy decision.
  
  But on online site we just trust the online seller.
  
  If the product is not good then the online seller should take it back and refund you.
  

  This is the review of the second handset I received after the replacement of the first handset.
  
  The first handset I had received had display issues and the display used to go off randomly.
  
  I was advised to do soft reset and then hard reset of the handset, but after trying all of that the problem persisted and I was sent a replacement.
  
  I ended up wasting significant amount of time doing followup and reset business.
  
  Also after the hard reset I had lost all my app, including the google apps, office apps and Mi tools, even the Google play store app.
  
  Overall it was not so pleasant experience.
  

  I received the second handset and has been using it for few days now.
  
  Unfortunately, the second handset is not great either.
  

  The phone heats up significantly some time when I have kept it in pocket while driving or even during meetings.
  
  I realized this after the phone heated up a lot couple of times.
  
  This is a major cause of concern because the phone can catch fire of explode.
  
  This is a health hazard.
  
  This might be a rare case, but it speaks very poorly of Xiomi quality because there other issues with the phone.
  

  Another problem that I am seeing now after using it for 2 weeks is that some times the display
  
  goes off immediately after I have disconnected a call, this happens randomly and even after I have set a time-out of 30 seconds
  

  The phone camera is no good. The images taken under flash come out dark.
  
  Are there any settings to change that?
  
  Why is it that other cheaper phones have cameras which work perfectly fine with flash?
  

  What is even more hilarious that the setup exe in the phone is in Chinese language,
  
  that shows that they have not done proper testing and quality check.
  

  Redmi Note 4G sucks.
  
  And, Flipkart, is this your best, pushing such shoddy products on your trusting customers?

The phone is unbelievably good for the price it charges. You can spend about 2-3 times more on another phone and there is a good chance that this phone will beat it in specs and performance. My review here is not based on any benchmark tests but pure user experience. Some of these points are already covered in online reviews, but let's just say that I had to say them.
  

  Pros:
  
  Fast & Responsive: I tried a variety of apps from office and sound hound to games like subway surfer and fruit ninja. There was no noticeable lag in responsiveness. I even played a few high-def movies in the in-built video player. No problemo.
  

  Impressive Display: The display is amazing. Looks great at varying angles. Retains a bit of visibility at extreme angles. I felt that the colors were not 100%accurate but it's not too noticeable.
  

  Fantastic Music: This was a surprise. The sound through the 3.5mm jack is good (even with lowly corded nokia headphones), but the real winner were the in-built speakers. They are not too loud but the audio quality is superb. And the phone provides a few audio customization options (in addition to the equalizer) depending on the type of headphones used.
  

  Android Kitkat: Android users know what it means.
  

  Really flexible UI: I have read that the only UI better than MI's is Cyanogen. Basically, the UI on the phone gives you a bunch of customization options available that you wont find on other android phones (except the nexus, and those running cyanogen). And trust me you will notice AND use them.
  

  Amazing battery backup: Enough has been said about it. Again, dont expect your phone to run for hours if you keep playing games, or watching videos. Suffice to say that any other phone with a similar display would typically have 50-60% of the battery life compared to this phone.
  

  Cons:
  
  Camera: This was the biggest disappointment. The 13-MP camera really is a joke. It seems to have trouble focusing (which could be a software issue). And low-light images are really bad...if I had to compare, I would say they were as good as a 3.2 megapixel camera without focusing capabilities. I even tested it side-by-side with a REDMI 1-S, and the 1-S beats this one in hands down. It does a better job in day-light, however, it still doesn't justify the 13-MP tag. The front camera though is surprisingly better.
  

  Moving Apps to SD: It restricts moving apps to SD-card. It means you would be limited to saving your apps to internal memory, instead of the 64-GB external memory. But it's not a big issue. The internal memory is sufficient for a number of small apps. But if you are a fan of big games, try to limit yourself to few games at a time.

column6: A good value for money Phablet.
column7:
Rather than tell everyone about the hardware specs and features again, as i'm sure everyone is familiar with it, I'll post some observations from a real world usage scenario.
  

  1.The screen is gorgeous and vibrant with adequate brightness and good viewing angles. A tempered glass screen protector is must as this phone is very slippery.
  

  2.Screen on time is amazing. More than 4 hours on cellular and close to 6 on wi fi.
  

  3.The phone came with 4.4.2 KK out of the box with Miui v5. Immediately you'll get OTA update to KK 4.4.4 with stable miui v6.
  

  4.MIUI 6 is nice and lot of new features are added. Its smooth and fast enough and has the much needed one handed use mode. But in this iteration,its missing lock screen music controls.
  

  5. Camera is just good enough in low light although photos are a bit grainy. Front cam isnt the greatest for selfies but good for video calls. HDR mode is quite good. A much needed manual settings mode is also present.
  

  6.Speaker is loud enough and sounds full. Headphone audio quality is also really nice. Call quality is very very good and noise cancellation works perfectly.
  

  7.Remember to put the phone into performance mode before playing games. by default it is in Balance mode to conserve battery. Really heavy games like gta:sa and modern combat 5 will lag at highest settings. Simple games like temple run,angry birds will run just fine.
  

  8.Miui 6 has a lot of hidden features, be sure to check out the mi forums to get to know all of them.
  

  9.The internal memory is only 8gb out of which just 4 or so gb is free. Apps cannot be moved entirely to sd card without rooting.Camera shots and other downloads can directly be stored to sd.
  

  10.Overall i feel for this price its a great deal. The comparison of this phone should be done keeping the other brands in the same price bracket. Its way more durable and of better build quality than brands like Micromax,xolo,karbonn etc. Just go for it.

column6: Xiaomi's budget phablet, Redmi Note :  Cheapest 4G device around.
column7:
1. Build & Design :The phone is pretty wide at 78.7mm. The  4G variant is lighter at 185gram compared to the 3G version that weighs 199gram. The back cover is rounded at the edges and is white in colour, sporting a glossy finish. The right edge features metallic keys for volume and power.
  
  2.Display :Xiaomi Redmi Note sports a 5.5-inch IPS display with a resolution of 1280x720p. The display is protected by Gorilla Glass 3 and looks bright and vibrant. While the display doesn't look as sharp as 1080p (full-HD) display, it offers wide viewing angles and decent sunlight legibility. In brief use, the display panel is very responsive to touch.
  
  3.Hardware specifications : The 4G version is powered by a 1.6GHz Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 quad core processor. It is a single sim phone. The phone supports both FDD-LTE Band 3 (1800 MHz) and TD-LTE Band 40(2300MHz) 4G bands. Most 4G networks deployed in India are on TD-LTE.
  
  4.Software : The 4G version of the Redmi Note runs MIUI 5 over Android 4.4 KitKat. Xiaomi plans to update the Note to KitKat and MIUI 6 which is due for release in the first quarter of 2015.The software experience was smooth and we did not notice any stutter while navigating through home screens, launching and switching between apps.
  
  5.Camera : Xiaomi Redmi Note sports a 13MP rear camera accompanied by an LED flash and a 5MP front facing camera. The rear camera supports 1080p video recording while the front camera supports 720p recording. I  tried clicking some pictures and found them to be pretty decent. There was no shutter lag and the Camera app is similar to the one found on Xiaomi Mi 3. The front camera also did a decent job.We'll need to spend more time with the phone to assess the capability of its camera.
  
  6.Pricing : The Redmi Note is better than most budget phablets available in the market, when it comes to hardware specifications. The camera resolution is higher and the processor, more powerful. The 4G variant of the phone is the cheapest 4G device around.
  

  Interestingly,I also expect it to make an impact on the sales of phones like the Asus ZenFone 5, which comes with decent specifications and costs the same. Indian handset vendors will also feel the heat and need to come up with better devices to keep up.

column6: THE BEST BUDGET 4G PHONE IS NOW EVEN BETTER !! THE ONLY HONEST REVIEW YOU NEED !
column7:
I Ordered Redmi 2 Prime on 10th Monday .Delivered on 14th Friday packing was good , Flipkart Rocks!.
  
  Here is the review ---
  
  DESIGN-
  
  On the first glance, the Redmi 2 Prime looks like a pretty good device for its price. Right away, the 4.7-inch 720p IPS display with 312 ppi pixel density is clearly the highlight of this device. The Redmi 2 Prime features a laminated LCD panel reducing the gap between the display and the glass which feels more fluid and offers better viewing angles. The display is bright and vivid and the color reproduction is pretty good. The sunlight legibility has improved as well, and the display sports AGC Dragontrail (manufactured by Asahi Glass Co. JAPAN )protection almost same as Corning Gorilla Glass.
  

  The design of Redmi 2 Prime is not remarkable, but it's a solidly-built phone and quite utilitarian. The curved edges and the matte finish makes for a great grip, although it tends to get slippery at times. Overall, the phone looks like a great, compact package, and exudes a feeling of durability.
  

  PERFORMANCE -
  
  Xiaomi has endowed the Redmi 2 Prime with a comparatively modern chipset. Performance wise, the new processor is much better.Powered by a 1.2GHz Qualcomm Snapdragon 410 64-bit quad-core processor with 2GB RAM and Adreno 306 GPU, it comes with 16 GB internal storage out of which around 12 GB is available to the user. The phone also features a microSD card slot that supports storage cards of up to 32GB.
  
  The performance of Redmi 2 Prime is better than Redmi 2 in everyday usage. I did not notice any lags even when I had 15+ apps open in the background. I played Asphalt 8 did not notice any lags. or frame drops . Also, the device does not heat very much. Overall, the phone has an awesome performance. Also, browsing on Chrome is also very smooth and snappy. 3G and 4G also work excellently, and there are no network drops. Also, 4G can be enabled on both sims. The call quality is also good and the dual- microphone cancels the background noise. So no complaints here also.
  
  The sound through the speakers and headphone is really good and crystal clear.
  

  BATTERY -
  
  The phone packs a 2,200mAh battery (removable) and will last you a full working day (15-16 hours) if you put the screen brightness at the highest level and use 3G data all the time. You'll be able to make about 1-2 hours of phone calls, play some casual games and browse the web in this time period. It lasted more than 20+ hours with light to medium usage.Your mileage may vary with different usage patterns. The phone offers two power modes Performance & Balanced , you can choose the balanced mode to save some battery. The phone supports Quick Charge 1.0 that speeds up charging.
  

  CAMERA -
  
  The Redmi 2 Prime sports an 8MP rear camera with an LED flash that is easily the best in the price segment. The photos in daylight are quite good and vibrant with decent level of details and accurate color reproduction. Indoors, the photos have a little bit of noise but still better than other phones at this price. Photos taken at night has a yellow tint .The rear camera can capture 1080p video and the output is decent enough.The 2MP front camera has a wide-angle to accommodate more people in your group selfies, although the photos are a little noisy but what more can you ask in this price?
  

  UI -
  
  The MIUI 6 is one of the best skins out there. Prime handles it very well and the overall performance is snappy. It is colourful and simple to use. There are many preloaded apps like cleaner, security, compass,scanner etc. There are also a whole load themes which can change the look of your phone. However one thing to note here is that the apps are spread all over the home screen and there is no app drawer.
  

  HOW TO GET PUSH NOTIFICATION FOR WHATSAPP
  

  I read many people saying that they are not able to get push notifications for Whatsapp, Messanger,etc. This happens because MIUI security app doen't allow them to publish notifications.
  
  Follow the steps to solve the Whats-app, etc. push notification problem-
  
  1. Go to the Security app which is pre- installed on the device
  
  2.Click on Permissions.
  
  3. Click on Auto-start.
  
  4.Select Whats-app and turn it on for whats-app.
  
  5. Now Reboot your device .
  
  Do the same thing for all the apps whose notifications you want to receive.
  

  VERDICT -
  
  This is the best phone in the market for Rs.6999. It has all the features you will need. Also, 2GB of RAM and 16GB ROM are welcome additions which makes this phone the best. I would recommend you to buy this over Yu Yuphoria or Lenovo A6000 Plus.
  
  If this review helped you in any way, please click the "YES" Button. Thank you.

  I bought this phone for my Dad. It's his first android device and he loves it. It more than meets all his needs. The cons mentioned often are the heating issue and battery drain, which are in my opinion, not severe enough to worry. It heats up only if you are multi-tasking more than 3 apps or under heavy gaming. Even then, not too much. It is more of a warming up than heating up.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Display
  
  The display is on par with devices from higher category. Beautiful colours on screen.
  

  2. UI
  
  The MiUI looks very elegant and classy. Great for people who want a simple UI. I personally use a Nexus 5 on CM 12.1 which my Dad hates.
  

  3. Sound
  
  The sound quality is rich and audible enough and feels premium.
  

  4. Ease of handling
  
  The phone is just the right size for single hand usage. It is neither too big nor too small. Feels great to hold in the hand thanks to the backpanel's matte finish.
  

  5. Performance
  
  The phone offers good performance, be it gaming or multi-tasking. On par, if not better than it's competitors in the price range.
  

  6. Light-weight
  
  The phone feels very light to hold unlike other devices in the range. You wonder if the battery is removed at times.
  

  7. Dual Sim
  
  Not many smartphones offer Dual Sims. There are people who need a dual sim facility and this phone does it very well indeed.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. No app drawer

First things first. We cannot expect an iPhone or iPhone specifications in 9K price range.
  

  I decided to write this review after seeing lots of negative reviews for this phone. I have been using this phone for almost two weeks now.

  Coming to the phone, we cant expect everything to be great on a 9K phone. We have to be realistic.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Biggest plus for me in this phone is the 4100 mAh  battery - It lasts for me two complete days with moderate internet/data usage and substantial call usage. I charge this phone only on alternate days.
  
  2. Finger print sensor for 9K phone - It works like a charm. Opens the phone in a second. You can also set fingerprint for locking applications. Amazing.
  
  3. 3GB RAM - very useful when doing multitasking. You dont see any lag whatsoever in performance.
  
  4. 32GB storage space - Huge storage space which can hold many of your apps on the phone avoiding the need to move the apps to memory card, which also helps in improving the performance.
  
  5. Metallic body - Looks awesome and stunning. Though i missed out on the Gold color and settle for a silver color, it also looks good.
  
  6. Display - Colors are nice, pictures and videos look great on this 720p 5 incher screen, though the pixel density is only 294 ppi.
  
  7. More than anything else, the usability in one hand is so easy. It really feels good to use this device.
  
  8. I havent faced any sort of heating until now.
  
  9. This model comes preloaded with Android Marshmallow (6.0), but we may not get a future upgrade. But Marshmallow preloaded is really great for this price range.
  

  If we would have to talk about the negatives, we would have to really get very picky. though there are few.
  
  1. Camera performance though is fast, picture clarity is not great for a 13 mp camera. Low light pictures look pretty average.
  
  2. The second sim slot getting merged with a hybrid memory card slot might not go well with many, but i am fine with using a single sim on this phone.
  

  Hope this clarifies and helps buyers.

column7:
I ordered this phone on 31st august on wednesday sale and got it delivered on 2nd september(friday). It was very well packed and was delivered early in the morning. I've been using this phn for past 7 days and this phn is just awsome.
  
  PROS :
  
  1. Fingerprint Sensor
  
  The main reason behind choosing this variant (3s prime) over 3s is fingerprint sensor. this sensor works perfectly, unlocks phn in just a fraction of seconds and gives a cool feeling that you hv a fingerprint sensor in your phn.
  
  2. 3GB RAM + 32GB ROM
  
  a phn having a fingerprint sensor and 3 gigs of ram then what else you want, this phn can handle heavy apps as well as games. I have been using this phn for past 7 days and have never encountered any lags or hanging. Redmi 3s prime offers a massive storage of 32gb out of which only 25-26 gb can be used. I don't know why people are complaining that they are cheated as their phn doesn't hv storage as stated in specs, guys you can't get a full of 32gb usable, I know that mi should hv offered 28-30gb usable but yes we hv to compromise on that.
  
  3. Body
  
  Its metal body is so classy, gives a premium look and the gold finishing at front is so beautiful.
  
  4. Camera
  
  I don't know why people are complaining about the camera quality I found its camera good especially the front one. I'm very much satisfied with the front facing camera.
  
  5. Compact
  
  If you have a mindset of using a compact phn then this phn is for you. Believe me guys, this phn is even more compact than other 5" phn and is very handy and can be used with one hand only.
  
  6. Battery Backup
  
  After buying this phn you don't need to carry your charger or power bank. Having 4000mAH battery is just like carrying a power bank itself. This phn lasts for 2 days of moderate use(playing games and surfing on net using wifi).
  
  7. Other sensors
  
  Its sensors are not only limited to fingerprint but it also hv IR blaster as well as gyroscope sensor. I think everybody knows about IR, if not then it is used for tv and ac remotes etc, in other words you can use this phn as your remote and gyroscope helps you to view 360 degree videos and much more.
  
  8. CPU+GPU
  
  This phn has a decent cpu and works perfectly with adreno 505. I've played asphalt 8, sniper 3d and gangstar 4 and all of these games run without any lag.
  
  9. Value for money
  
  Finally, at last this phn is a beast at this price range.
  

  CONS :
  
  1. Screen is average
  
  The picture quality of this phone is just average. It is neither too bad nor too good. My previous phn which was also 720p, has much good looking picture quality than this.
  
  2. Heating issue
  
  This phn heats up only while playing heavy games which is a little bit annoying. However, doesn't heats up very much but does a little bit.
  
  3. No blacklit
  
  This phn doesn't offer backlit in navigation keys. However, there is no need for them as the navigation keys are very much visible.
  
  4. No earphones
  
  This is a bitter true, this phn doesn't comes with an earphone and you hv to buy a separate one.
  
  5. Hybrid system
  
  Both variant has hybrid sim, which means one can insert micro sim + nano sim or micro sd card. For some users, this may be a reason for buying redmi 3s prime not redmi 3s, as redmi 3s offers only 16 gigs internal while 3s prime offers 32 gigs.
  

  Verdict:
  
  I think this is a very nice phn under this price range having many features, nice looks and much more. This phn has many pros. and a little cons. which can be neglected. So, this a must buy product.

Atleast if you were looking to buy the phone with good battery, this is not the one.

I Ordered Redmi 2 Prime on 10th Monday .Delivered on 14th Friday packing was good , Flipkart Rocks!.
  
  Here is the review ---
  
  DESIGN-
  
  On the first glance, the Redmi 2 Prime looks like a pretty good device for its price. Right away, the 4.7-inch 720p IPS display with 312 ppi pixel density is clearly the highlight of this device. The Redmi 2 Prime features a laminated LCD panel reducing the gap between the display and the glass which feels more fluid and offers better viewing angles. The display is bright and vivid and the color reproduction is pretty good. The sunlight legibility has improved as well, and the display sports AGC Dragontrail (manufactured by Asahi Glass Co. JAPAN )protection almost same as Corning Gorilla Glass.
  

  The design of Redmi 2 Prime is not remarkable, but it's a solidly-built phone and quite utilitarian. The curved edges and the matte finish makes for a great grip, although it tends to get slippery at times. Overall, the phone looks like a great, compact package, and exudes a feeling of durability.
  

  PERFORMANCE -
  
  Xiaomi has endowed the Redmi 2 Prime with a comparatively modern chipset. Performance wise, the new processor is much better.Powered by a 1.2GHz Qualcomm Snapdragon 410 64-bit quad-core processor with 2GB RAM and Adreno 306 GPU, it comes with 16 GB internal storage out of which around 12 GB is available to the user. The phone also features a microSD card slot that supports storage cards of up to 32GB.
  
  The performance of Redmi 2 Prime is better than Redmi 2 in everyday usage. I did not notice any lags even when I had 15+ apps open in the background. I played Asphalt 8 did not notice any lags. or frame drops . Also, the device does not heat very much. Overall, the phone has an awesome performance. Also, browsing on Chrome is also very smooth and snappy. 3G and 4G also work excellently, and there are no network drops. Also, 4G can be enabled on both sims. The call quality is also good and the dual- microphone cancels the background noise. So no complaints here also.
  
  The sound through the speakers and headphone is really good and crystal clear.
  

  BATTERY -
  
  The phone packs a 2,200mAh battery (removable) and will last you a full working day (15-16 hours) if you put the screen brightness at the highest level and use 3G data all the time. You'll be able to make about 1-2 hours of phone calls, play some casual games and browse the web in this time period. It lasted more than 20+ hours with light to medium usage.Your mileage may vary with different usage patterns. The phone offers two power modes Performance & Balanced , you can choose the balanced mode to save some battery. The phone supports Quick Charge 1.0 that speeds up charging.
  

  CAMERA -
  
  The Redmi 2 Prime sports an 8MP rear camera with an LED flash that is easily the best in the price segment. The photos in daylight are quite good and vibrant with decent level of details and accurate color reproduction. Indoors, the photos have a little bit of noise but still better than other phones at this price. Photos taken at night has a yellow tint .The rear camera can capture 1080p video and the output is decent enough.The 2MP front camera has a wide-angle to accommodate more people in your group selfies, although the photos are a little noisy but what more can you ask in this price?
  

  UI -
  
  The MIUI 6 is one of the best skins out there. Prime handles it very well and the overall performance is snappy. It is colourful and simple to use. There are many preloaded apps like cleaner, security, compass,scanner etc. There are also a whole load themes which can change the look of your phone. However one thing to note here is that the apps are spread all over the home screen and there is no app drawer.
  

  HOW TO GET PUSH NOTIFICATION FOR WHATSAPP
  

  I read many people saying that they are not able to get push notifications for Whatsapp, Messanger,etc. This happens because MIUI security app doen't allow them to publish notifications.
  
  Follow the steps to solve the Whats-app, etc. push notification problem-
  
  1. Go to the Security app which is pre- installed on the device
  
  2.Click on Permissions.
  
  3. Click on Auto-start.
  
  4.Select Whats-app and turn it on for whats-app.
  
  5. Now Reboot your device .
  
  Do the same thing for all the apps whose notifications you want to receive.
  

  VERDICT -
  
  This is the best phone in the market for Rs.6999. It has all the features you will need. Also, 2GB of RAM and 16GB ROM are welcome additions which makes this phone the best. I would recommend you to buy this over Yu Yuphoria or Lenovo A6000 Plus.
  
  If this review helped you in any way, please click the "YES" Button. Thank you.

  During the first few hours of use, I used to get frequent  No service available  error, which was abnormal. Looking through the SIM Card settings, I found that Preferred Network type is set by default as LTE (4G) and my service provider has not started 4G in my area. It seems that, in the effort to locate a non-existent 4G service the device had some hick-ups and dropped the signals. Changing the setting to 3G solved the problem. I have seen some other customer reviews where the signal problem was mentioned. I would suggest everyone to choose the  Preferred network type  correctly. In case you are travelling out of town, the best bet would be to choose 2G!
  
  Overall:
  
  Excellent value for money. I like the fixed price, no-nonsense approach of Xiaomi.   First of all, my moto g3 order got cancelled and i had to order some phone so i choose this for a while.But, irrespective of my Xiaomi image (as a local chinese phone..!) this phone has shattered all my doubts and the bad image i had of MI series.
  
  Talking about the phone, i always wanted a phone which can handle my hard multitasking with many apps running at a time all around. Also i needed a phone with a minimum 1 day or long usage battery with moderate 3g and multitasking being done. Screen size is also a matter for me as i can't buy a smartphone of more than 5" screen. All these specifications are fully and well fulfilled by redmi 2 prime. I am just in love with this phone. Phone UI is attractive and very very light so don't bother about hangs on this device.
  
  Selfies are good but i am not satisfied with the back camera because my earlier galaxy core of 5mp camera used to take sharper images than this 8mp .
  
  Call quality is excellent and music is very loud n crystal clear for music lovers.
  

  PROS :
  
  Excellent Multitasking.
  
  Light weight and very easy interface.
  
  Very fast processor and you get approx. 1gb ram always free even if 10-12 apps r running.
  
  Long lasting battery backup.
  
  Feasible screen size..easy one hand operation.
  
  Excellent sound and screen 720p is worth it.
  
  CONS :
  
  I found a big disadvantage that inspite of having 3g connectivity, networks switch to 2g automatically and retains it which is very embarassing. But i tried a solutiion and it worked. Download Phone Testing app from google play and set data network to ONLY WCDMA/HSDPA instead of PREFER 3G.
  
  Back camera is okay but not upto the mark
  
  All around i don't find any crucial cons as this revice kills them all.
  
  Superb REDMI 2 PRIME.

  I bought this phone for my Dad. It's his first android device and he loves it. It more than meets all his needs. The cons mentioned often are the heating issue and battery drain, which are in my opinion, not severe enough to worry. It heats up only if you are multi-tasking more than 3 apps or under heavy gaming. Even then, not too much. It is more of a warming up than heating up.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Display
  
  The display is on par with devices from higher category. Beautiful colours on screen.
  

  2. UI
  
  The MiUI looks very elegant and classy. Great for people who want a simple UI. I personally use a Nexus 5 on CM 12.1 which my Dad hates.
  

  3. Sound
  
  The sound quality is rich and audible enough and feels premium.
  

  4. Ease of handling
  
  The phone is just the right size for single hand usage. It is neither too big nor too small. Feels great to hold in the hand thanks to the backpanel's matte finish.
  

  5. Performance
  
  The phone offers good performance, be it gaming or multi-tasking. On par, if not better than it's competitors in the price range.
  

  6. Light-weight
  
  The phone feels very light to hold unlike other devices in the range. You wonder if the battery is removed at times.
  

  7. Dual Sim
  
  Not many smartphones offer Dual Sims. There are people who need a dual sim facility and this phone does it very well indeed.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. No app drawer
  
  Some people, like my Dad, like this UI with all the icons on the screens. Apple users might like this too. But many people out there, like me, will sorely miss the app drawer.
  

  2. Resource intensive UI
  
  Of course, it doesn't make any difference to Redmi 2 Prime with it's 2 GB but for Redmi 2, this is a major issue.The UI looks great but consumes too much of the RAM. Nearly 700MB is taken up by the UI.
  


  The battery is rated at 2200 mAh though the company claims it holds a little more juice. This should last you one full day of mixed use without an issue. On video loop, it lasted about 11.5 hrs which is pretty great. Using mobile data with a normal usage might give a battery life of about 10 hrs.
  

  I personally think the grey colour looks much classier and substantial than the white one. I had ordered a grey one for a cousin while Dad opted for a white.
  

  Overall a great device for the price paid. If you are looking for a smartphone with great display, pretty good camera with dual sim facility, this is the one for you. Don't go in expecting performance of a 15+k phone and you shall not be disappointed.

Redmi Note 4 is the first smartphone from Xiaomi to sport a 2.5D curved display. Moreover, the company will be rolling out Android 7.0 Nougat update for the handset pretty soon.
  

  So does the Redmi Note 4 live up to the expectations? We find out in our full review.
  

  Design and display
  

  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 comes with a matte-finish metallic design that gives it a premium appearance. The phone has a metallic unibody that makes it look and feel much better than what its price may suggest. The rounded edges make for a comfortable and non-slippery grip in the hand. The volume rocker and power button are placed on the right, while the hybrid dual-SIM card tray is on the left.
  

  The front panel is largely dominated by a 5.5-inch Full HD display and there are three capacitive keys at the bottom. The top edge has a 3.5mm audio jack, along with an IR blaster for controlling TVs and other appliances. A micro USB charging port is placed at the bottom. As for the rear panel, it's home to a 13MP primary camera with dual LED flash, along with a fingerprint sensor.
  

  All in all, we found the overall design of the Redmi Note 4 to be pretty good, especially given the price.
  
  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 comes with a 5.5-inch Full HD 2.5D curved display of 1080x1920 pixel resolution. This is the first Xiaomi smartphone to sport a 2.5D curved display.
  

  In our testing, we found the display to be pretty decent with appreciable viewing angles. It's fairly visible under direct sunlight and the phone also has a setting to tweak the colours, allowing users to switch between warm and natural colour tones.
  

  Performance and camera
  

  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 Prime is powered by an octa-core Qualcomm Snapdragon 625 SoC paired with 4GB of RAM and 64GB of internal storage. It also supports memory cards of up to 128GB in size. The company has also launched two other variants - 2GB RAM/32GB ROM and 3GB RAM/32GB ROM.
  

  During our time with the device, the Redmi Note 4 delivered an overall smooth performance with no visible lag. The large display makes gaming and media consumption pretty enjoyable. We played games like Asphalt 8, Mini Militia etc. and the phone handled them very well.
  

  That said, the Redmi Note 4 does get a little hot during extended gaming sessions, primarily because of the metal body.
  

  Apart from that, multitasking works as it should. The phone manages to run multiple apps and switch between them without suffering from any performance drain.
  

  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 sports a massive 4,100mAh battery, which easily lasted us up to a day with heavy usage. Call quality of the device was also fine during our testing. We used a Reliance Jio SIM with the smartphone and it handled VoLTE calls without any issues.
  

  As for the software, Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 runs Android 6.0 Marshmallow topped with the company's MIUI 8 UI layer. The interface itself is pretty clean and user friendly. However, there is no app drawer and all apps are placed on multiple home-screens.
  

  MIUI is very colourful and offers nicely designed themes, app icons and wallpapers. The device offers some interesting modes such as a Reading Mode, which reduces the display's background glare to help in reading. Along with this, the device offers a second space, which essentially enables users to have different profiles each with separate wallpapers, apps, files and photos. Users can also assign different fingerprint and passcode to access them.
  

  Redmi 4 Note comes equipped with an IR blaster which can be used to control home appliances such as TV and ACs easily. The pre-installed 'Mi remote app enables users to add multiple remote controls for different appliances and use them from the phone itself.
  

  For imaging duties, the Xiaomi Note 4 sports a 13MP rear camera with dual LED flash and a 5MP front camera for selfies. During our testing, we found camera performance of the device to be pretty decent. The smartphone uses a noise-eliminating CMOS sensor with backside illumination (BSI) and larger pixels to provide good shots even in low light conditions.
  

  The camera itself is pretty fast and has a user-friendly interface. Users can apply live filters at the time of clicking photos and can also access various shooting shooting by tapping on the button above the shutter button.
  

  The smartphone's cameras produced some really nice pictures during our testing. Focus is good and colour reproduction is accurate as well. There's a burst mode included as well.
  

  Verdict
  

  Priced at Rs 12,999, the Xiaomi Note 4 is a good option in its price segment. The smartphone offers premium features like metallic body design and good camera at a competitive price. Those looking for alternatives can consider buying Moto G4 or the Samsung Galaxy J7 Prime.

column6: A small counter to negative reviews
column7:
1) Battery Life:
  
  It's important to note that it's a Lithium Ion battery, so the 1st time you turn on your phone, you should immediately charge it until it is fully charged and then for 6 additional hours. This will not only increase your battery life, but make sure that the natural decline in battery life over the months is mitigated. Although I agree with many people that theoretically this problem should be absent with Li. Batteries, but from a practical standpoint it does matter.
  

  My battery lasts almost 2 full days, with moderate use (wifi/data is always on).
  
  My charging is also phenomenal. If I'm not mistaken, the phone has Quick charge (ver2.0) upto 80%. No complaints here.
  

  2) Low lighting pictures:
  
  I agree that if you just focus and snap the picture, it comes out grainy in a low-light setting. However, after tapping to focus, you will notice there is a little dotted/lined circle which you can rotate. By rotating this clock-wise or anti-clockwise, you can change the light exposure. Set it higher than 1.0, but no more than 1.5 - 1.7.
  
  There is also a dedicated mode for night-time shots, but I have not checked it out yet.
  
  I've taken a few great photos in pitch-darkness.
  

  3) Heating issue:
  
  First of all, keep in mind that given these specs crammed into the phone and due to the metal body, it has a natural propensity to generate heat and conduct it effectively to the surface. However, I do agree that this phone runs hot after extended-moderate to heavy use. After talking to a few reviewers on youtube, it seems that the mi4 on miui v5, did not have this issue, to this extent. So this appears to be a software optimization problem. Hopefully, Xiaomi releases an update to help alleviate this. Just make sure that you are not downloading the developer roms; stick to stable releases.
  

  4) Back panel is slippery: I agree, it is. But no one in this day and age keeps a premium phone without a case. Just get the Nillkin black case, Has great traction.
  

  Now, I just want to add a few small notes.
  
  The 8MP front-facing camera: For all you selfie-lovers, it's one of the best I've seen in the market in this price-bracket.
  
  Also, there are a lot of hidden features, that some of you might like, so just check it out on youtube. Look for MiUi tips and tricks, or hidden features, or some variation of that.
  

  All in all, great specs, great build quality, great support by the company. And now that the 64Gb version is out in India, all that's missing for me is the black version of this phone. :P

I am writing this review exactly after 2 weeks of use of my Xiaomi MI4.
  

  I'm sure all of us are aware of the specifications and pros & cons of this phone. All I want to share is my personal opinion on this phone.
  

  I have used several android phones in the past starting from the rugged Motorola Defy to my last phone, the brilliant LG Optimus G e975. I have also rooted all my phones and used several custom roms on all the phones that I have used so far.
  
  I can say without doubt that this MI4 is the best android phone that I have used till date. Once again this is my personal opinion based on the phones that i have used so far. Others could have difference of opinions.
  

  Since getting this device in hand I had one OTA version update that I installed. It still is on MIUI 6.7.1.0, based on 4.4.4 KitKat. It's a personal choice that I prefer a stable KitKat rom than an unstable latest rom.
  

  I am an above average user of the phone with my phone always on 3g and or Wi-Fi with regular usage of WhatsApp, Gmail, and Facebook with all notifications always on. I have a couple of decent games installed, a few important apps for banking, online shopping, sports updates and so on.
  

  Some observations of mine are -
  

  Battery - With all these on use, i get great battery backup. Sometimes i can stretch it to a couple of days. I just feel good looking at my phone going to sleep in the night and waking up with almost the same percentage left in the morning. I haven't experienced this in any of my android devices so far.
  

  UI - I like the UI as I had installed MIUI long time back, based on gingerbread on my Motorola Defy and found it interesting. Again it is a personal choice. I like the customizations on MIUI. CyanogenMod also has great level of customizations which I like too. This MIUI version is very fluid and I found it great to use.
  

  Camera   Awesome in daylight, one of the best I've seen so far. Low light photos may not be satisfactory considering the 13mp Sony Camera. The front camera shoots some great selfies in daylight while in lowlight not so great. Still, I'm thrilled with the camera.
  

  OS   Is still on Kitkat with a stable Lolipop (hope it doesn't suck the battery much) may be around the corner. Am very happy with the current one though.
  

  Gaming   I have not installed too many games but games like subway surfer, stick cricket, real racing which my kids play, run without any issues on balanced mode. Given the hardware, I'm sure all high end games will run flawlessly on this. There is a performance mode too which will enhance the gaming experience.
  

  Display and Size   The display is great with good viewing angles. I may not be able to differentiate between full hd and quad hd screens so you may want to consider other reviews for this. The size is ideal for my preference as it fits very well in my hands and in my pockets. My wife has a One Plus One which is in all ways a similar phone with CM but a bit bigger in size which made me lean over to the MI4.
  

  I've never experienced any kind of heating issues so far. I have the 64 GB version so space is also not a constraint. It has an IR blaster which works well on my Samsung TV. For my Airtel set top box, I had to rely on third party apps from the play store. Sound output on the loudspeaker may be a bit on the lower side (not that it is feeble), however the quality and the output on headphones are great. Signal quality was very good and so was the data connectivity and call quality.
  
  I bought the original MI4 Minimalistic Back case from flipkart along with this and the combo gives good looks without compromising on the size.
  

  To say that I'm happy with this purchase of mine, is an understatement. I would recommend this phone to anyone who needs a phone that can give apart from the basic phone features, great battery backup, good pics on the camera, beautiful ui (personal choice), performance and all these and more at a decent size and price.

column6: Value for money phone, but don't compare it to high end flagship devices.
column7:
I had a Mi3 before buying this phone, Mi3 was a good phone and i was expecting same value for money out of mi4, but this is not the case. All the people who compare this phone to an iPhone 5s,6 or HTC one, Sony Xperia Z series and high end Samsung phones and call it better are highly mistaken and most probably have never used or even held a high end phone in their hand.
  
  All the websites with reviews proclaiming it to be a flagship level device are either paid for or the reviewers are out of their silly minds.
  

  Compared to any flagship, this phone is way behind in respect to the following.
  

  1. Glass. This phone has Corning concore glass and not gorilla glass. I had to get a tempered glass screen protector as on the 4th day 2-3 scratches were visible on the screen. A very poor choice of material.
  

  2. Display. Colors are not accurate, whites appear to be a greenish blue when compared to other high end phones or even my old Mi3.
  

  3. Build quality: Keep this phone next to a white iPhone and you will understand the difference between white and blue. Mi4 looks like a pale blue phone when compared to iPhone, Also the shiny metallic part of the metal frame is full of scratches within 2 weeks. Same goes for the plastic back.
  

  4. Loudspeaker. Extremely poor, old mi3, nexus 4, iPhone 5,6 easily outperform it in speaker department. Not at all good.
  

  5. Camera performance. Don't care about what all tech jargon Xiaomi is throwing to promote the camera, that is, Sony sensor, 6 element lens, chroma flash etc, Camera is slow to operate, i.e launch time and shot to shot time, focus accuracy is poor, slow motion video is nothing more than a gimmick and end quality is just okay but nothing exceptional.
  

  6. Apps/Software performance. Again this thing has more ram and processor compared to mi3, but it is slower. Basic apps like youtube take 5-6 seconds to open, music player also takes about 4-5 seconds. I believe miui 6 is the culprit here as even Mi3 performance came down after the update.
  

  7. Software updates. For all those people who crib about software update timeline of HTC, Sony etc, Xiaomi is not any better, this is an 7-8 month old phone and has no Android 5.0. and the miui 6 update for Mi3 came after 4-5 months of being available in other regions.
  
  But this phone does has its pros as well, battery life is really impressive, so is the front facing camera , these are the only 2 things which come to my mind when i compare it to a flagship.
  

  Final words: Anyone planning to buy this do keep in mind you get what you pay for, this is no flagship killer. An excellent display, speaker, camera and build quality are missing. If you are using an xperia z3 or HTC one M7/M8, don't think that your phone is over priced and that your next phone will be a xiaomi where you will get the same features for half the price.
  
  It is a good phone but there might be better value for money propositions (one plus one). This phone should have been prices at 17-18 range. 20 is just a little too much for this phone and brand. Value for money factor has come drastically down considering my experience with Mi3.

column6: A Great Phone for a Great Price
column7:
I am in love with this phone from the moment I have held it in my hands.
  
  Most of the reviews here has helped me decide to buy this phone so many thanks to all the reviewers.
  

  I feel it is better to get the 64GB version though as you don't get expandable storage.
  
  Most of the reviewers have listed all the good and bad things about the phone, so I will try not to repeat it, and list down my experience so far with the phone after 2 weeks of usage:
  


  1) Battery heating is not an issue while normal usage, but it does heat up a little bit while charging, nothing alarming, as the power brick provided is a fast charging one, hence it will heat up the phone, its normal.
  

  2) The front camera is awesome. I am not a person who used to take selfies, but after I laid my hands on this phone, 70% of all photos taken with this phone is a selfie. Big thumbs up!
  

  3) It does have occasional glitches, and apps tend of crash every now and then, but it has not created any problem yet
  

  4) MiUi is great, with lots of customization options. MiUi keeps sending OTA updates, however after the recent update, the video player is crashing and is not playing videos, probably it will be fixed in the next update.
  

  5) 3 GB RAM is enormous, and multi tasking works like a breeze. I have not experienced a slowdown yet, and I am a power user.
  

  6) Battery is GOOD, but not GREAT! Yes, for power users, it might just last up till the evening. I am not sad with the battery but definitely there are phones with better battery backup. As the phone supports fast charging, it really helps a lot. But you need to have a fast charging adapter as well.
  

  7) Overall feel of the phone is great in the hand, just the perfect size, as I had been using Note 2 for more than 2 years now, the stainless steel frame really feels great. However, the plastic back is still slippery and Samsung-y, hence a case would be nice to have!
  


  To be honest, I was confused between OnePlus One and Xiaomi Mi4 (which are both great phones with almost similar specs), and ended up with this for the below reasons which are as per personal preference:
  

  1) The size of the phone, 5 inch vs 5.5 inch (plus bezel)
  
  2) Better camera performance
  
  3) Better in-hand feel with metal chamfered edges
  
  4) 1080P in 5" is better than 1080P in 5.5" (nothing noticeable, but still better)
  

  All in All, a great phone to have for the price at which it is being offered.

column6: Great Phone | Cool UI | Lovely Design | Superb Performance
column7:
I got my hands on the Mi4 the day after the sale went live. I'm an iPhone user and needed an Android phone for app development and testing purposes and I was delighted with what I got. I've tried to break my experience in parts and make it useful for you guys. I've used the product for 4-5 days now and one thing's for sure, Xiaomi is here to stay.
  

  1/ Design: The phone looks really great and the design is crafted to perfection, although it seems inspired from the iPhone 5S, they've done a pretty good job. The phone is a bit on the thicker side which is the only slight drawback as far as design and size is concerned.
  

  2/ Performance: The phone has a very responsive touch and performance even on very heavy games like FIFA 2015 is superb. There is not a single moment of lag. However the 3GB RAM is for a reason, almost 2GB is always occupied by the phone even when no apps are running in the background. This does not impact the performance as you still have 1GB of free memory.
  

  3/ UI: Probably the best part of the phone is the user interface (MIUI, as they call it). It's surprisingly fresh and beautifully designed to enlighten the user's mood every time you use the phone. They have taken the best from both worlds (Android and iOS) and built something which is a delight for the eyes. To complement the great UI design they have beautiful interactions and a brilliant crystal-clear display which is the best I've seen on any Android phone so far. You'll fall in love with it instantly. (I'm appreciating it so much being an iPhone user says a lot)
  

  4/ Camera: Superb rear camera with a really fast auto focus and a brilliant flash. The 8MP front camera is also excellent and probably the best secondary camera in the market.

column6: One of the best smartphones under 15K budget!
column7:
So I have been using mi4 for about 5 months now and here's my complete unbiased review
  

  1. Design - Beautiful! The look and feel is really good. But the back case is too glossy and tends to slip out of your hand so I'd recommend a hard back case or a flip cover for it. The 1080 resolution screen looks really nice, no laggy touch whatsoever. So for design I give it a 9/10.
  
  2. Performance - Smooth! 3 GB of RAM with 2.5 ghz quad core processor makes your experience with your phone very enjoyable. Incidents of lagging was extremely rare. All high end games run without any lag too so I would give 9.5/10 for its performance.
  
  3. Camera - Beast! In all honesty, I fell in love with photography thanks to mi4 camera. Rocking a 13 MP back camera and 8 MP front camera, this phone will in no way disappoint you in terms to capturing some of your favorite moments thanks to a large part to the Sony sensor installed in the camera. So without any hesitation I give it a 10/10 for camera.
  
  4. Battery - On paper it says 3000 mAh battery but I'd say it's good but not great. I don't play high end games but do use 3G or Wi-Fi all day  and plus a 1080 resolution screen has a lot to do with the battery usage. With this usage, it lasts a whole day for me and would be around 15-20% at the end of the day. And about the charging, it takes around 2 hours to go from 0-100% with the quick charger xiaomi provides. So I'd give 8.5/10 for battery.
  
  5. Audio - I'm not overly impressed by its audio quality. I'd say slightly better than average audio quality but I mostly use my sennheiser earphones which clears up my audio issue. So for the audio, I'd give 7/10.
  

  Now let's talk about something that everybody's talking about - Heating issue. Yes, it does heat up a lot if I keep using my phone for let's say 30 minutes or an hour without any break. It also heats up if you are playing any kind of game. Now I might not feel the effect as much as other mi4 users as I'm using a flip case which prevents my hand from a direct contact with the glossy back case but I do feel the heating issue to some extent. About the heating issue while charging, that's not a problem. Phones charging under a quick charger heats up a lot and that's pretty normal so nothing to worry about there. Another disadvantage about this phone is the memory storage. A 16 gb phone with no SD card slot does raise some eyebrows. Personally I don't have any problem as I don't play any games or store HD movies so this issue shouldn't really apply to everybody.
  

  To sum it up, it's a great smartphone. It's definitely one of the best phone under 15K budget and honestly I got use to the heating issue so I ain't complaining about it. Considering all the points mentioned above, I give it an overall 8/10 and would definitely recommend to others too.

I'd definitely suggest this phone to those who wants to buy. Before buying it myself, I had read a lot of rantings and whining about heating issues, which made me a little concerned. Never the less, I bought it and have been using it for the past 2 months.
  

  YES, the phone heats up quite often. But my question to all those people who are crying about it - Why wouldn't it heat up?
  

  1. It's using a quad - core 2.5 ghz processor.
  
  2. It's using a 4GB RAM.
  
  3. It has a display of 441 ppi Full HD
  

  And when you're utilizing all those resources at the same time - with multiple apps open, or playing HD games, it's pretty normal for ANY phone to heat up, UNLESS they have a METAL cover. So, if you really feel this phone is putting you up on flames with it's overheating issues, then please search your pockets and get hold of 40-45K INR and buy a flagship from renowned companies with metal bodies.
  

  For a 20K phone, the experience is awesome!
  

  Note - I've used flagship phones from Sony before (been a Xperia Z user for a long time). It used to heat up worse than this.
  

  That being said, there is still some scope for improvement from Xiaomi. They can enhance the memory management system of MIUI, thus reducing heating issues to some extent, but for a phone with a plastic body using such extreme resources, I don't think it'd be much use.

column6: Excellent phone in the 9K price range
column7:
First things first. We cannot expect an iPhone or iPhone specifications in 9K price range.
  

  I decided to write this review after seeing lots of negative reviews for this phone. I have been using this phone for almost two weeks now.
  

  I ordered this phone on 11th Aug and got it delivered on 12th Aug. Awesome delivery by Flipkart. Hats off.
  

  Coming to the phone, we cant expect everything to be great on a 9K phone. We have to be realistic.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Biggest plus for me in this phone is the 4100 mAh  battery - It lasts for me two complete days with moderate internet/data usage and substantial call usage. I charge this phone only on alternate days.
  
  2. Finger print sensor for 9K phone - It works like a charm. Opens the phone in a second. You can also set fingerprint for locking applications. Amazing.
  
  3. 3GB RAM - very useful when doing multitasking. You dont see any lag whatsoever in performance.
  
  4. 32GB storage space - Huge storage space which can hold many of your apps on the phone avoiding the need to move the apps to memory card, which also helps in improving the performance.
  
  5. Metallic body - Looks awesome and stunning. Though i missed out on the Gold color and settle for a silver color, it also looks good.
  
  6. Display - Colors are nice, pictures and videos look great on this 720p 5 incher screen, though the pixel density is only 294 ppi.
  
  7. More than anything else, the usability in one hand is so easy. It really feels good to use this device.
  
  8. I havent faced any sort of heating until now.
  
  9. This model comes preloaded with Android Marshmallow (6.0), but we may not get a future upgrade. But Marshmallow preloaded is really great for this price range.
  

  If we would have to talk about the negatives, we would have to really get very picky. though there are few.
  
  1. Camera performance though is fast, picture clarity is not great for a 13 mp camera. Low light pictures look pretty average.
  
  2. The second sim slot getting merged with a hybrid memory card slot might not go well with many, but i am fine with using a single sim on this phone.
  

  Hope this clarifies and helps buyers.

  a phn having a fingerprint sensor and 3 gigs of ram then what else you want, this phn can handle heavy apps as well as games. I don't know why people are complaining that they are cheated as their phn doesn't hv storage as stated in specs, guys you can't get a full of 32gb usable, I know that mi should hv offered 28-30gb usable but yes we hv to compromise on that.
  
  3. Body
  
  Its metal body is so classy, gives a premium look and the gold finishing at front is so beautiful.
  
  4. Camera
  
  I don't know why people are complaining about the camera quality I found its camera good especially the front one. I'm very much satisfied with the front facing camera.
  
  5. Compact
  
  If you have a mindset of using a compact phn then this phn is for you. Believe me guys, this phn is even more compact than other 5" phn and is very handy and can be used with one hand only.
  
  6. Battery Backup
  
  After buying this phn you don't need to carry your charger or power bank. Having 4000mAH battery is just like carrying a power bank itself. This phn lasts for 2 days of moderate use(playing games and surfing on net using wifi).
  
  7. Other sensors
  
  Its sensors are not only limited to fingerprint but it also hv IR blaster as well as gyroscope sensor. I think everybody knows about IR, if not then it is used for tv and ac remotes etc, in other words you can use this phn as your remote and gyroscope helps you to view 360 degree videos and much more.
  
  8. CPU+GPU
  
  This phn has a decent cpu and works perfectly with adreno 505. I've played asphalt 8, sniper 3d and gangstar 4 and all of these games run without any lag.
  
  9. Value for money
  
  Finally, at last this phn is a beast at this price range.
  

  CONS :
  
  1. Screen is average
  
  The picture quality of this phone is just average. It is neither too bad nor too good. My previous phn which was also 720p, has much good looking picture quality than this.
  
  2. Heating issue
  
  This phn heats up only while playing heavy games which is a little bit annoying. However, doesn't heats up very much but does a little bit.
  
  3. No blacklit
  
  This phn doesn't offer backlit in navigation keys. However, there is no need for them as the navigation keys are very much visible.
  
  4. No earphones
  
  This is a bitter true, this phn doesn't comes with an earphone and you hv to buy a separate one.

  Both variant has hybrid sim, which means one can insert micro sim + nano sim or micro sd card. For some users, this may be a reason for buying redmi 3s prime not redmi 3s, as redmi 3s offers only 16 gigs internal while 3s prime offers 32 gigs.

I am not the one to write reviews often. But this piece of phone has compelled me to write one. I have been using this for over two months now and I have been very disappointed with it.
  
  My reasons for purchase were simple: this phone claims to pack a good battery, RAM and a decent camera. Unfortunately, I have had a terrible experience on all these three fronts:
  

  a. Battery: In theory, the phone claims to have a super battery in this price range. However, the battery is nothing extraordinary. In fact, it hardly lasts for a day - even on an average use. The battery also diminishes at an accelerating pace. Once its <20%, you can bet that it will switch off in half an hour! And I have tried battery saving techniques, plugging off data connections, wifi etc. So I suspect that perhaps battery is not as strong as they claim. Atleast if you were looking to buy the phone with good battery, this is not the one.
  

  b. RAM: The 3GB RAM should work like a butter, right? Well, wrong. The phone hangs often. The first time it hang - and that was in the first two days of use itself - I ignored it. But then to my horror, it just kept hanging regularly. And mind you, I don't use more than say 3 apps at any given time. So a 3GB hanging with such avg use is something that is very weird.
  

  c. Camera: Well, the camera is very very average. And no, price range doesn't justify it as I have seen better cameras at this price range. The camera is terrible in low light. And quite avg even in daylight.
  

  Additional drawbacks:
  

  d. Heating issues: The phone's front surface heats up quite a bit on charging and during a call! If you happen to speak for more than ten minutes, the phone gets unbearably hot to hold on the ear!
  

  e. Network Connection: Now as if that other problems were not enough, you have the mother of all problems: poor network detection and connection. You see, I can live with a phone which doesn't deliver on battery as it claims, or a phone which hangs now and then or a phone which heats up and has an avg camera - BUT I cannot live with a phone where I can't even have a smooth connection! The voice keeps breaking and the damn signals keep fluctuating. It is this which is most frustrating and has compelled me to write a review. Believe me, the connection issues are something I have never faced before (and I have used about 10 phones so far of brands such as lenovo, sony erricsson, motorola , nokia even spice). I'll be honest: there are times when I am on a call when the voice just breaks down and I want to smash this phone on the ground and crush the damn thing. May be one of these days, I will do it.
  

  Bottomline: Don't get fooled by the specs and don't justify to yourself that these specs are great at this price point: because a terrible phone is a terrible phone and it will come back to haunt you and then you'll regret of buying this.

I am Reviewing this product after 2 weeks of use. Overal, the device is very good.
  

  PERFORMANCE: The performance is extremely good. It has Snapdragon 650(The same processor which you get on Xperia X priced at    45000). However, under heavy gaming, it may show small lags.
  


  BUILD & DESIGN: The design is truely amazing. It looks very good and is very nice to hold. But the Aluminium  Back is quite slippery. If you're getting this device, do invest in a Case.
  

  DISPLAY: The 1080p panel is very sharp. The display quality is very good. But the display doesn't have Gorilla Glass protection. So you will have to buy a Tempered Glass.
  

  AUDIO: The speakers are very loud and good. The sound from audio jack is also very good.
  

  CAMERA: I saw a lot of users complaining about the camera. But in my opinion, it might not be the best but it is good. I don't have any complaint about the front or back camera. The dual LED flash is very bright and enhances the shots in low light.
  

  BATTERY: The battery on this device is extraordinary. I can easily get a Screen On Time of around 8 - 10 hours on single charge. It will easily get you through the day. If you a light user, it can even last up to 2 days.
  

  SOFTWARE: I personally don't like the MiUi. It has a lot of bloatware. At present, the autorotation doesn't work sometimes. Hopefully, this issue will be solved with a software update very soon.
  

  HEATING: On normal usage and gaming, it will show mild heating which you can neglect. Under heavy usage( like 360   videos or VR Videos more than 15 min), the can get very hot. But one hardly watches those videos, so I guess heating won't be an issue.
  

  SERVICE: THE Xiaomi's after sale services aren't good. The PickMi service takes a lot of time. Service centers are not present everywhere. I live in Chhattisgarh. There is no Xiaomi Service Center in the whole state.
  

  Under    10,000; It is THE BEST.
  

  If you have a budget of    12000, you might be confused between Le 2 and Redmi Note 3. Le 2 outperforms Redmi Note 3. But Le 2 has a hollow cavity under the display which often bends and is not a good sign. So, if you can be very cautious with the device, buy the Le 2. Otherwise buy Redmi Note 3.
  

  If you can spend some more cash, you can take a look at Zuk Z1.

Redmi Note 3 is an awesome smartphone with only the LeEco Le 2 as a competitor in the price segement. I have used both of them, so I am gonna compare the two to give you a better view to choose between them.
  

  Design: Personally I loved the design of Le2. Both phones offer a nice build quality but Le2 looks more premium and slimmer.
  

  Display: Redmi offers a sharp Full HD screen. No noticible difference here.
  

  Performance: Redmi offers a powerful Snapdragon 650 SoC coupled with 3GB RAM which handles daily tasks and moderate gaming without any issues. LeEco has a slightly better 652 SoC but normally you won't notice a lot of difference.
  

  Storage: Redmi offers 32GB storage just as LeEco but additionally one of its SIM slots can be used as SD card slot and hence it gains the edge over Le2 in storage.
  

  Camera: This is where I feel both phones could have done better. That being said, the Camera's are almost equal on paper and in actuality. Although, some shots felt better on Le2.
  

  Battery: Redmi Note 3 has  a huge 4000Mah battery compared to 3100Mah in Le2. Expect a lot better battery backup in Redmi. However, Le2 features quickcharge support and comes with quick charge adapter, so it charges a lot quicker.
  

  LeEco Le 2 and Redmi Note 3 are good phones. Both has their own advantages and disadvantages. Based on requirement, the device can be selected.   If your priority is battery life and support for microSD card, then Redmi Note 3 is better. I have been using this phone for over a month now and I could not find much to dislike about this phone. This is one of the best budget smartphone available with so many features to offer at such a lesser price when compared to other brands. Below I have written my own observation and experience with this phone within a short span of one month (although I know it might be too early ;p )
  

  1. First things first, the look of the phone is amazing (Gold color). The shade of the gold color is neither too loud nor too low. Although the self declaration sticker at the back of the phone might be upsetting at first, but you can always get rid off them anyway.
  

  2. The second feature for which I purchased the phone was the camera. The front facing camera (5MP) is excellent. It captures light and color in perfect balance and performs decently under bright light. However, the absence of the front flash is disappointing about this phone and don't expect it to capture better selfies and pics under low light.
  

  The rear camera which boasts 16 MP camera at 11,999/- doesn't actually delivers pics like a 16 MP camera. But it is not disappointing either. The camera gives a high resolution picture even under moderate light conditions. For better clicks under low light conditions, you may try switching to HDD mode.
  

  3. The display is very bright and clear. I can bet no one can keep maximum brightness level on this phone.
  

  4. The phone is compatible with variety of headphones and earphones. The sound quality is excellent.
  

  5. I have loaded more than 30 apps on my phone and usually like to do multitasking. I faced no problem in doing so.
  

  6. Only one Caution: The phone might start heating up while playing high graphics game.

This phone was delivered in a day's time, which was good.
  

  Following things I've noticed after using my phone;
  

  HEATING - This phone heats up normally like every other phone, it has no extensive heating issues like every other person has been complaining about in their reviews. If you play heavy games continuously for like 10 minutes or so, the phone heats up a little bit, but that is completely normal. Even while charging or talking on the phone for quite sometime, the phone will heat up, but in a normal way like almost every other phone. I had updated my phone almost immediately after opening the package, so I don't know about the heating issue before the update, but as of now, its completely fine.
  

  CAMERA - The camera in this phone is freaking brilliant. If you're getting blurred photos from your Mi4i camera, then you're just not focusing it properly because it has a manual focus as well (tap on the screen where you want to focus). None of my photos have come out blur (what I had focused on came out crisp clear). The front camera is also equally good. Sometimes the photos do come out a little (just a little) grainy, but remember, sometimes even digital cameras and dslrs' produce a little grainy photos and that is not the fault of the camera. Grainy photos are produced due to low light.
  

  RAM - 2gb RAM helps a lot. The phones barely lags and when it does, its for barely a second and that is totally manageable. I've noticed that the phone lags only when I switch from app to app very quickly, like when you open one app by mistake and realize that's not the app you wanted to open and then you click the home button and then quickly click on the other app, that's when the phone lags. That's not even the right way to operate a phone I think, so I'd take the blame for that. There is a shortcut button for task messenger (left bottom, feather touch button) which shows what all apps are running in the background and you have the option to kill those apps instantly. After the first update, the free memory after killings all apps would be around 400mb. I got a third update (one day before writing this review) and after that the free memory goes up to 700mb. No worries about the RAM in this phone and no lag issues.
  

  INTERNAL MEMORY - Of course, an external memory card slot would have been a major plus point, but quite frankly 16gb memory is enough. You get to use almost 10gb only because the system also uses a lot of memory. If you think you're running low on phone memory, then please check the photos that you've clicked from your phone and the music list. I had low memory issues with my previous phone only because of excessive and unwanted photos and music in my phone. Otherwise, the memory issue should not be there.
  

  SPEAKER/HEADPHONES - The volume of the sound is actually less, even at full volume. Sound quality is not bad. People have been complaining about poor sound quality and that isn't the case. Sound quality is definitely not great, but it's definitely not bad. Sad thing is, earphones were not provided along with this phone. So pair up your phone with some really good earphones and enjoy the music.
  

  BATTERY - Though the battery capacity is really good, I don't get a very good backup as I use too many things on the phone and some heavy apps. If you play a lot on this phone (or any other phone also), the battery will die faster. Internet browsing, facebook, whatsapp, games, etc do drain the battery, but there are certain apps which run in the background which also helps in draining the battery. The default security app scans the phone at times without your notice, but I'm not sure if that does too much damage. Otherwise, the battery backup is good. Lasts properly for a day and a half with heavy usage of the phone.
  

  DESIGN - The phone has a very beautiful and a minimal design, nothing unnecessary on the front or the back. The back panel is a little slippery, but it ain't a problem. The interface of this phone is simply amazing with a lot of customizing options, just love it.
  

  VOLUME/POWER BUTTON - A little sharp, but you'll get used to it. So far no cuts on my finger and it will not even cut your finger.
  

  SIM CARD SLOT - The pin to open the sim card slot was not provided with this phone. I had to use a paper clip for this. The slot does not open instantly once you insert the pin in the hole. I had to literally force the pin inside and was scared of damaging it, but it finally came out. Just be careful on this one.
  

  Verdict - Amazing phone, seriously no complaints. Go for it. If you do have complaints, then you're probably not using it right. Cheers!
