Redmi Note 4 is the first smartphone from Xiaomi to sport a 2.5D curved display. Moreover, the company will be rolling out Android 7.0 Nougat update for the handset pretty soon.
  

  So does the Redmi Note 4 live up to the expectations? We find out in our full review.
  

  Design and display
  

  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 comes with a matte-finish metallic design that gives it a premium appearance. The phone has a metallic unibody that makes it look and feel much better than what its price may suggest. The rounded edges make for a comfortable and non-slippery grip in the hand. The volume rocker and power button are placed on the right, while the hybrid dual-SIM card tray is on the left.
  

  The front panel is largely dominated by a 5.5-inch Full HD display and there are three capacitive keys at the bottom. The top edge has a 3.5mm audio jack, along with an IR blaster for controlling TVs and other appliances. A micro USB charging port is placed at the bottom. As for the rear panel, it's home to a 13MP primary camera with dual LED flash, along with a fingerprint sensor.
  

  All in all, we found the overall design of the Redmi Note 4 to be pretty good, especially given the price.
  
  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 comes with a 5.5-inch Full HD 2.5D curved display of 1080x1920 pixel resolution. This is the first Xiaomi smartphone to sport a 2.5D curved display.
  

  In our testing, we found the display to be pretty decent with appreciable viewing angles. It's fairly visible under direct sunlight and the phone also has a setting to tweak the colours, allowing users to switch between warm and natural colour tones.
  

  Performance and camera
  

  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 Prime is powered by an octa-core Qualcomm Snapdragon 625 SoC paired with 4GB of RAM and 64GB of internal storage. It also supports memory cards of up to 128GB in size. The company has also launched two other variants - 2GB RAM/32GB ROM and 3GB RAM/32GB ROM.
  

  During our time with the device, the Redmi Note 4 delivered an overall smooth performance with no visible lag. The large display makes gaming and media consumption pretty enjoyable. We played games like Asphalt 8, Mini Militia etc. and the phone handled them very well.
  

  That said, the Redmi Note 4 does get a little hot during extended gaming sessions, primarily because of the metal body.
  

  Apart from that, multitasking works as it should. The phone manages to run multiple apps and switch between them without suffering from any performance drain.
  

  Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 sports a massive 4,100mAh battery, which easily lasted us up to a day with heavy usage. Call quality of the device was also fine during our testing. We used a Reliance Jio SIM with the smartphone and it handled VoLTE calls without any issues.
  

  As for the software, Xiaomi Redmi Note 4 runs Android 6.0 Marshmallow topped with the company's MIUI 8 UI layer. The interface itself is pretty clean and user friendly. However, there is no app drawer and all apps are placed on multiple home-screens.
  

  MIUI is very colourful and offers nicely designed themes, app icons and wallpapers. The device offers some interesting modes such as a Reading Mode, which reduces the display's background glare to help in reading. Along with this, the device offers a second space, which essentially enables users to have different profiles each with separate wallpapers, apps, files and photos. Users can also assign different fingerprint and passcode to access them.
  

  Redmi 4 Note comes equipped with an IR blaster which can be used to control home appliances such as TV and ACs easily. The pre-installed 'Mi remote app enables users to add multiple remote controls for different appliances and use them from the phone itself.
  

  For imaging duties, the Xiaomi Note 4 sports a 13MP rear camera with dual LED flash and a 5MP front camera for selfies. During our testing, we found camera performance of the device to be pretty decent. The smartphone uses a noise-eliminating CMOS sensor with backside illumination (BSI) and larger pixels to provide good shots even in low light conditions.
  

  The camera itself is pretty fast and has a user-friendly interface. Users can apply live filters at the time of clicking photos and can also access various shooting shooting by tapping on the button above the shutter button.
  

  The smartphone's cameras produced some really nice pictures during our testing. Focus is good and colour reproduction is accurate as well. There's a burst mode included as well.
  

  Verdict
  

  Priced at Rs 12,999, the Xiaomi Note 4 is a good option in its price segment. The smartphone offers premium features like metallic body design and good camera at a competitive price. Those looking for alternatives can consider buying Moto G4 or the Samsung Galaxy J7 Prime.

Hey guys , Review of the Redmi 1s, Any questions can be asked under our Youtube Channel 'Nitty Gritty Reviews', where we have posted our review & we can answer your questions.
  

  Build Quality
  

  Quite good.. one of the better handsets at this price range.. The removable back leaves some space in between which makes it feel a bit hollowish
  

  Dragon Trail Glass for the front panel is an amazing plus at this price point.
  

  No backlit Keyboard... hard to use in it in the dark... but this is something you'll get used it.
  

  Display
  

  720p IPS display.... Biggest reason to consider this phone... Colors are good... and brightness is fine under sunlight.
  

  4.7" display makes it really good for watching movies... Overall phone build quality is quite good.
  

  UI
  

  Quite different from other Android Skins, There is no app drawer...Everything is in the Homescreen like with IOS.
  
  The Multi Tasking is also slightly different... where you get icons instead of  small screenshots.
  

  The music player is really nice and it offers specific settings for the Xiaomi Pistons(also reviewed) and it definitely makes quite a big difference.
  

  The messaging app allows you to reply to messages without having to quit any app you already are in.. which is a real nice addition.
  

  The phone runs 4.3 which and Xiaomi has not mentioned anything about an udate to 4.4 Kikat.... so thats a small setback
  

  Camera
  

  The daylight performance is quite good...and the 8mp is more than what most phones offer at this price point.
  

  The low light performance isnt great, but that should be expected considering its just 6k.
  

  The phone has difficulty in focusing on close objects, but pics are clicked really fast with little to no delay.
  

  Storage
  

  8gb Internal ... Expandable with microSD.
  

  Problem is apps cannot be installed on MicroSD, this limits your apps storage to 5gb of free internal.
  

  Battery Life
  

  Average battery life, Heavy usage means you'll be looking for the charger by 5-6pm... Normal usage should give you a day's of battery life.
  

  Handling Heat
  

  The phone gets quite hot while using 3g for web browsing or for any apps ... This is makes it uncomfortable to pick calls etc during the such operations.
  

  Call Quality
  

  Softer than most phones i've used... Not that its unusable... But it isnt as loud as other phones.
  


  Purchasing Experience is horrible... and considering that Android One is coming out in a couple of days and the fact that Moto G 2nd Gen and the Zenfone 5 cost just a bit more with better build qualities and overall experiences and much higher avalablity... column6: Review which will make sense to everyone
column7:
Dear people crying foul, I understand your pain.
  

  This phone was not meant for everyone. The people who are pained to have such phone, please migrate to other awesome manufacturers of the likes of Karbonn, Micromax et al. You'll have a great time dealing with the pristine quality product they have on offer. This was sarcasm, in case you didn't get it.
  

  About the product. I have been using it for about a week now. Fiddled much around with it and now know how make it my pet.
  

  First thing first, the dreaded RAM issue. Yes people, the RAM is scant, I got only 340MB on first ever boot and I operate my whole day on mostly less than 200MB free RAM, but should that concern you? It should if you think you are some rocket scientist, which you probably aren't. I use three apps, WhatsApp, Opera Mini and Telegram throughout the day, with my corporate email synced in background. And I do have issues with Opera Mini closing every now and then. But not even once any app has crashed. I get all the pages of Opera where I left. People who have had any phone understand this particular problem. So, I don't think the issue is very glaring. It is an issue, but hey, it can be sorted with an SOFTWARE update. Remember people, software and hardware are different.
  

  Okay now the build quality.
  
  Forget HTC and Sony, this should be the quality standard at below Rs 10,000 mark. Some guy claiming to have come from Sony Xperia Z1 and then saying the design is not inspiring, you have my sympathies brother. The design is absolutely delightful. The plastic is polycarbonate and not el cheapo polythene. The curves make it comfortable to hold and the phone is dense, like really dense, thus making it heavier too, which is a good thing; speaks volumes about the detailing. One issue, the flash unit on my device wobbles a little. Hmm. Never mind that. The buttons are great and soft to press, which is bad for me but good for most others I have talked to as they find softer buttons, better. For them, "softer buttons are easy to press in pocket". I, with my small hands, tend to press them every now and then.
  

  The display.
  
  The display has tweaks my grandmother can't remember the same number of rotis she made for dinner. Apart from usual brightness, it also has tweaks for saturation, temperature and option to disable sensitivity in pockets (this feature first appeared in Nokia N9. How do I know, I have that phone) so your pocket doesn't dial the number for you. The viewing angles are great and there is no chromatic aberration whatsoever. Which also brings in the fact that like most phones, the display is extremely glossy and reflective. I-can-see-my-own-face reflective. Use a matte screen protector if you are not happy with this. But it is with every phone, so this isn't really a downside. The capacitive buttons are not back-lit, which enables you to become Sherlock Holmes while using the phone in dark, as you have to guess where exactly you have to tap to perform navigation. The notification light is non-intrusive and glows very softly, me likey.
  

  The camera.
  
  OMG! Dis camera zz soo kewl! Literally. The camera is one of the best you can get in under 15,000 bucks. The autofocus is spot on and it creates a nice bokeh effect on its own. It is fast, time taken from one snap to ready to take another is so quick, you won't even realize that the picture has already been taken. It also has HDR, low-light mode, 12 different scene modes, photo filters, ISO upto 1600 (did they actually go crazy?) and a speak-to-click mode (wherein you speak 'click' and the photo is captured, nice for snaps over tripod), apart from the usual camera tweaks you find on a smartphone camera. The Exmor-R sensor made famous by Sony has found home here and dare I say the quality of the pictures. They give a tough run for money to the camera centric mid-range Lumias.
  

  The battery.
  
  Disappointments galore. The battery lasted me 5 and a half meagre hours of constant gaming, videos, surfing, texting and picture snapping while connected to WiFi all the time. This is the standard test as it gets, because this is all what anyone does. and the screen was on all the time for those 5 and a half hours. This is sheer disappointment. Keep your chargers ready people, winter is coming. Oh, sorry, battery warning is coming. It will last for not more than 12 hours of standard office usage time. This is sad. I understand this *might* be why the Mi power banks are available so cheap.
  

  Continued in next review.

Hi All,
  

  I have been using this phone since 10 days now which seems like a decent time to post my review. I am a Techie with a keen interest in computers & cellphones. Below are the Pros & Cons of the Xiaomi Redmi 1s MIUI v45 based on my review.
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Nice & sleek design
  
  2. Firm fitting of exterior parts which gives a good feel while holding the phone
  
  3. Good specs - Snapdragon quad core processor with 1GB ram, 8MP rear & 1.6MP front camera, big 4.7 inch display.
  
  4. MIUI (Xiaomi developed custom ROM) gives an iphone-like feel to the interface
  
  5. 2 Amp charger for superfast charging. The phone gets fully charged from 0 to 100 in about 100 mins when switched off or in Airplane mode. (My brother's Moto G2 takes 3 hours to charge with Moto official 550 mAmp charger)
  
  6. All usual games work just fine. I experienced occassional frame drops on Asphalt 8 (with low graphics setting) & Subway surfers. But I think its to do with the heavy JellyBean OS and MIUI eating up RAM. The hardware is pretty good for these games to work properly.
  
  7. Tons of accessories available on Flipkart and few other online sites
  
  8. Good for elders due to the "Lite mode" feature which makes all options on the screen big for easy viewing. If no 2G/3G data or WiFi is used, then the battery should easily last 3 days or more.
  

  Cons:
  
  1. Battery capacity of 2000 mAh is a little less for a phone with this kind of specs. Capacity should have been at least 2500 mAh. No option in Flipkart to buy a spare battery yet.
  
  2. MIUI could actually be irritating at times & there is no offical/easy option to disable it (unless you root the phone). MIUI takes a lot of RAM typically leaving about 300MB for the user
  
  3. Device is still on 4.3 Jelly bean, hope kitkat/lollipop update comes out soon
  
  4. No option to install/move apps to Micro SD card
  
  5. The Xiaomi sync application for Windows is in Chinese. There is a need for Official English version
  
  6. The phone (not the battery) tends to heat up while on my Office WiFi and the battery drains like water from a tap from 90% to 0% in about 2 hours. However, this does not happen with my home WiFi where a full charge will last about 1.5 days (with WiFi, GPS, cellular network on full time) with moderate use of about 6-7 hours.
  

  Contrary to a lot of reviews where people say that the battery is heating up very often when kept ilde in pocket, I haven't faced that issue with MIUI v45. This is a good phone at a good price. Total value for money for the Indian consumer.

column6: Powerful hardware but issues with Software
column7:
I could manage to buy this one during the 2nd flash sale and have used this phone for over 20 odd days before writing this review. But, sadly lost it on a busy bus a few days ago. Here are my observations after a brief usage :
  

  Pros:
  
  1) Amazing hardware- quad core  Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 coupled with Adreno 305 /1GB RAM which supports high end graphics and HD videos/ games. Even 1080 p video playback is supported.
  
  2) 312 ppi 720 p  LCD Display is the best you can get in this price range. The colours are crisp and accurate too. The dragontail glass is really scratch resistent. I have infact used the unit without applying screenguard for a week commuting on dusty roads and coins in my pocket.
  
  3) Amazing primary 8 MP sony camera module  + 1.6 MP Front facing camera captures good quality pictures. The video recording also supports 1080p recording.
  
  4) The notification LED at the bottom of the screen can be configured to glow with 5 different colours for different notifications.
  
  5) Built in call recording facility.
  
  6) Supports dual sim with 3g support for the first sim slot
  
  7) Expandable storage upto  64 GB micro sd slot with inbuilt 8 GB flash memory.
  
  8) Great call clarity with dual mic noise suppression
  
  9) Amazing sensors unit. You even get the Gyroscope and digital compass along with the proximity, accelerometer and ambient light sensor at this price point.
  
  10) Great audio quality, good for listening to music and sound (when using earphones) is loud enough to be heard even in noisy traffic.
  
  11) some great inbuilt apps like call recording/antivirus/data access management/tasks killer are very useful.
  


  Major Cons:
  
  1)  Too hot to handle -  It is true that this device heats a lot, even after normal use i.e without playing any games or recording videos. After a few charge/discharge cycles heating has bit reduced but it is still on the higher side. The device heats up a lot near the camera module on the back side and the screen area near the earpiece on the front even after using internet for 10 min or a long call lasting more than 5 min and is unbearable. This is the biggest con of this device making this amazing hardware almost unusable. Heating also has adverse effects on performance. Though I have not encountered any reboot problems, apps start crashing when the battery temperature rises over 40 deg C. Even Antuntu scores reduce to below 15K when the temperature rises which is otherwise 20K + when the device is cooler. Surprisingly, the device doesnt heat a bit when using the earphones for conversations.
  
  2) RAM optimization is very poor. Apps get closed in the background without your notice. Available RAM is always less than 30% even on idle and mostly occupied by system processes. This makes multitasking a pain on this device. You cannot play music and browse internet at the same time as music player crashes which is irritating.
  


  Minor Cons:
  
  1) The in call voice volume could be have been higher. At the highest volume there is some vibration in the ear piece causing disturbance in hearing which might be resolved by software update, not sure.
  
  2) The capacitive keys below the screen could have been backlit. It is difficult to use it in the dark unless you get used to it.
  
  3) The  power button is too close to the volume keys and sometimes get accidently pressed. May be it depends on the user as I have got used to the volume keys which is on the left on my previous device v/s on the right side on this device.
  
  4) The device is too bulky and bit large to carry considering it is a 4.7 inch unit. It gets even bulkier on applying protective case on it.
  
  5) Device runs on Android 4.3 Jellybean currently though most of the devices getting released recently run on Kitkat (v4.4).  Android 4.4 is expected to arrive with MIUI6 on this device by end this year which should resolve this con. But you will need to wait till then.
  


  This phone has the best possible hardware at this price point including the camera module. But the software (MIUI) is quite buggy and not able to utilize it well. Just assume that you have bought the h/w and you are getting the MIUI as a freebie with this device when you are buying it. Hope, that the upcoming software updates will resolve most of these issues giving it 5 stars in future and making it the best device under 15 K. But, for the moment you have to live with them. Good Luck !

  Of the 1GB RAM minimum free space is 450 MB, and it will reduced as you start using the phone. Clean the memory as often as you can for better performance. The free RAM available could drop to as low as 120MB.
  

  There is 8GB storage of which about 6.14GB is allocated as internal storage (4.12GB available). OTG is supported. There is micro SD slot that supports up to 64GB cards. Apps are installed on internal storage and there is no option to move to external storage.

The feature to automatically save data to SD Card has been released in the next MIUI update (Version 37) but that's released in China as of now and is yet to be released in India.
  

  2. The phone cannot be used if you want to sync your corporate email to it. Most of the corporate email accounts have a policy of device encryption which is available in all android devices but it is not available in any of the Xiaomi devices. I got to know it post purchase and hence had to switch back to my older device (Moto G).
  
  My friends who had purchased MI3 are also facing similar issues.

column6: Wow, its an amazing phone. Everything you need to know about Redmi 1s
column7:
I bought Redmi 1s last month and have been using it till date. I am very happy with the phone. Thanks to all the advanced users who reviewed the phone already. Their reviews gave confidence in me going for this model in spite performance and heating issues mentioned by other users. My battery lasts easily for more than a day with moderate usage which includes 1 hour calls, 1 hour of gaming, one hour of 3g data, 4-5 hours of 2g data. I am sharing what I've done with phone after the purchase. If you are not clear with the steps I followed, please google in Miui forums and there are plenty of posts with proper steps on each of the points.
  

  Tips for Basic Users
  

  1. Charge the phone overnight for at least 8 hours with mobile switched off. Do it before the first use
  
  2. Upgrade the phone firmware to V45 with updater tool available in the phone
  
  3. Always set the sim1 mobile network to 2G mode only. Switch to 3G only when needed. Always on 3g network drains battery fast even though you don't use 3G data. 3G networks signal strength are the cause. 2G signal strength is stable with most mobile operators
  
  4. Disable continuous Sync of your Google and other accounts. Sync on demand
  
  5. Disable automatic Brightness, set brightness to 50% or slightly less according to your need. Setting to 100% will drain battery fast
  
  5. Use toggles to enable/disable Data, Brightness, Wifi, Bluetooth, GPS for quick
  
  access
  

  Tips for Advanced Users.(Search Miui Forums for details steps)
  

  1. All tips mentioned for basic users above holds good here as well
  
  2. Root the phone. For steps just google in Miui forum for native rooting. (Unrooting is possible too if you need to revert)
  
  3. Install No Frills Cpu from play store
  
  a) Set the minimum Freq to 300Mhz. Maximum to 1.1 Ghz for moderate usage, 1.4 for heavy graphics intensive gaming usage like ashphalt 8)
  
  b) Governor - Ondemand
  
  c) I/o Scheduler - cfq
  
  d) Apply on boot to be ticked
  
  e) Go to app settings and ensure you tick "Disable safety valve" and "Prevent changes from other app"
  
  4. Install Greenify. Greenify apps which are not needed to run in background when the phone is not used by you. Don't Greenify apps like Whatsapp, hangouts if you want instant notifications
  
  5. Install MinFree Manager and set "Mild" from the presets for optimized RAM usage
  
  6. Install auto reboot and set the auto reboot of your phone every day defined time. My phone reboots everyday at 3 AM. Android performs better when rebooted in regular intervals
  

  Optional tips
  

  1. Install Link2sd or similar app to freeze apps not in use
  
  2. Install folder mount to move apps to SD card. In Redmi, we can't move apps to SD in Miui
  
  3. You can also install custom CM 11 roms from available in XDA or Miui forums too.
  
  Hope this will help some existing users as well as new users who want to buy Redmi.
  

  After doing the above the things, now
  

  1. Battery last for one and half days for my usage. You should see a 30% improvement in your battery stand by based on your current usage. One and half days for my usage not guaranteed for everyone
  
  2. Phone temp hasn't gone up above 38 deg after gaming(Real racing and Crazy Taxi tested)
  
  3. No lag issues or random crashes or reboots
  
  4. No worry about running out of space in internal memory
  

  Redmi is truly value for money. Try to make use of what its capable of, don't expect it too perform like a flagship phones sold over 20k or 30 K. Be realistic and be happy...

column7:
Not a full fledged review, as I am sure plenty of details are already there on other reviews, hoping to bring you what you want by now. And these are just first impressions, as I got the phone just yesterday
  

  Good stuff first:
  

  * Flipkart delivered it 5 days earlier to the scheduled date of 25th. Got it yesterday. That was impressive considering the festive time
  
  * I unboxed it and within few minutes started to feel the burn around the camera area - and realized hell yeah I understand what the guys are talking about (heating issue). So, performed the firmware update V45 and such a dramatic BEFORE - AFTER. The heating issue is gone. Just half a days' use. Will update this review with more details
  
  * Did a lot of stuff (fidgetting), and did not feel much lag or force closing issues (I am not a gamer guys. Everything else seems OK with this phone)
  
  * The camera - its the speed of eye blink. Crazy speed focus, shoot and ready for next shot. Even with SD card on.
  
  * Display is yes reflective. Do not expect to watch HD movies in burning summer days (I am sure you wouldnt do that anyways), but you should be able to get around seeing who is calling and sending that text messages
  
  * Did almost everything on the phone - Firmware update, watching videos, browsing, setting the phone up (means hell a lot of sync), emails, music, et al. I got close to 2 3/4 hour screen time and 5 hours of usage time, with 50% until death. Not bad for an un-calibrated battery. Expecting 6hr screen time, which seems decent at this point
  

  Other usual pros:
  
  * 8MP camera with flash and 2 MP selfie cam
  
  * 4.7inch HD 720p screen
  
  * Quad core processor clocking 1.6Ghz
  
  Though there are complaints on lag, I went with the specs and pretty happy with what I see so far
  

  * Build quality is very impressive for an ultra cheap phone
  

  Cons:
  
  There is a flipside to buying stuff online - you are not sure unless you actually feel the stuff in hands. I expected a 4.7 inch screen to be slightly smaller, but this one weighs heavier and is even bigger to my 5" Micromax.
  

  By now I guess you can see someone in the neighborhood flaunting the 1s. Try feeling it before you buy
  

  Overall, I was WOW-ed for a 6K phone. No major gripes as the V45 seems to have fixed the ones that existed. Huawei Honor holly is competing at 7K with a larger screen and availability! But if you are lucky to get this one (and 6k is all you got!), do not look beyond!
  

  Cheers, and Happy Diwali!

column6: Don't Blame the phone's performance just Customize your setting
column7:
I can see many negative review for this phone but we have to remember its a only 6K phone and I bet it's performance is better than all the 10K range phone available in market. All you need to do is to customize the setting.
  

  1. Battery Issue: Go to Security > Power > Battery Configuration > select Marathom mode if you want long battery backup. It will disable wifi/mobile data while phone is locked and save battery. I tested and having almost 14hrs backup with 2G on and normal use without gaming.
  

  2. RAM issue: Redmi 1s is already heavily preloaded...if you want to add more application issue can happen. Thats why they took 6K not 16/26K for the phone :-) Please remove all the unnecessary apps ( as I removed google book,video,play,swiftkey,flipkart apps etc - please do it as per your requirements). Keep freeing RAM(by pressing option key longer) before starting game and also RESTART YOUR SET ONCE IN 2 DAY if you are a heavy gamer or internet freak.
  
  I have installer TemplerunOZ,Subwaysurfer,RealRacing,Fronline Commando1,D-Day,Prince of Percia and I am getting always 200-300MB free mem which is good.
  

  3. Enhance Performance Further: Go to Security > Cleanup > Clean Cache frequently.  You can also schedule a cleanup.
  

  4. Heating issue: I am agree that its there but if you follow all the above mentioned tips you can minimized it.
  
  - Try to refrain gaming with wifi/3G on, this will heat the cell and also drain the battery.
  
  - Please remember very high end games are made for device with higher CPU/RAM, if you play those games here device will support nicely but performance degrades and start get heating
  

  At last I can say no phone below 10K available in Indian market can beat its performance. If you still not happy with that, please go for a high end Android phone and please not blame Redmi.
  

  Good Luck!!!!

column6: Near Perfect device with few niggling issues
column7:
1.Got the product much before the promised date and the first impressions of the phone was simply jaw dropping. The screen protector and adaptor are not generally provided with the box so it was a pleasant surprise.
  

  2. I dont bother about specification because they hardly have an implication on real time performance of the device. I rate the performance of this device purely based on experience.
  

  Display : 9/10. 1280 * 720 resolution does what is expected of it and IPS retina display is not something you will not find in this price range. Above par for the course.
  

  Gaming : 8/10. Hardly any lag on simple games likes Traffic Racer, Wings of fire & Temple run 2. Graphics output is very very good. Above par. Highly satisfied.
  

  Camera : 10/10. Show me a better camera from a phone below 15000 than the redmi and i will give you a treat. It is that good. Took photographs in pitch dark with flash on and still no grains found. Daylight photography is easily best. Some of my friends thought the photos were taken in digital camera. Level of details in the photographs is very sharp and ...(I can keep talking but i will stop)
  

  MIUI : 7/10. The MIUI 5 in the phone is very userfriendly and thoughtfully designed. The practical nature of the UI is commendable. It was heavily inspired (not copied) from IOS so the overall user experience is very smooth. Again the graphical design of tools and display of apps etc is fantastic and the feel good factor is always there. (Graphic output when Recorder/compass is running are examples). Wide variety of themes available to play with, this is something very unique for a mobile phone
  

  MI Cloud : I am against storing anything in cloud i dint use it and so i cannot comment.
  

  Multi tasking : 2/10. At first i dint believe that the phone was actually hanging then i realised that it was hanging almost everytime i open 3 or more apps. RAM management is very sluggish. I was using a Lumia 520 before and trust me with nearly 40 % of and processor and RAM capacity the 520 was still faster and better equipped for multi tasking. I have reached level 10 in Temple Run 2 with 520 while continuously keeping several apps open at the same time. The way Windows manages the meagre 512 RAM is a lesson to other smartphone makers. You simply cant beat 30 years of OS experience that they have got. This niggling issue really irritates a lot and regardless of the ridiculously low price of 6000 you cannot live with the hanging problems. MIUI looks great and the graphic processing for general stuff is so high that you end up with hardly 200 mb for your use. That is very low for such a quality display et all. So cannot forgive the designers on this aspect. I dont want more RAM, but should have reduced the MIUI customisation for this phone to improve workability. But have to make do with it.
  

  That is why despite taking into consideration the price and the other performance parameters i give only 2 stars because at the end of the day multi tasking is one of the most fundamental aspects of a smartphone these days. Secondly the exclusivity and mad rush created by lack of handsets is maddening. If is continous people will soon lose interest and move to ASUS zenphone ( a close competitor, but i have not used it yet).
  

  Thank u hope it was useful.

  Redmi not the snappiest phone in market, but it is not visibility slower than my friends MotoG. Also Xiomi runs numbers of additional background process and MIUI take some processing.

  I agree with most of the user, that 1GB is not enough memory.   5. UI -
  
  Lot of people find UI unintuitive. I think MIUI it rather simple and features are nicely copied from iOS6. If you don't like it, you can root it always. CyanogenMod is now available for Redmi 1S.

I bought the phone on the first sale of Xiaomi Redmi 1S using my Flipkart first priority pass. When I received my phone with complimentary Screen guard and Micro Sim sleeve on 11th of September, I realised, it was a steal at the price. I started using the phone without updating the OS and tweaked some basic settings and was mesmerised with quality of the phone and MIUI. I installed many apps and all apps worked like a charm.
  

  Later when I went to post a review after about a week of use, I found there was lot of negative reviews about Xiaomi Redmi 1S. So I decided to wait for some time to read the user reviews and complaints before and come out with solutions for them.
  

  The following were the main concerns mentioned:
  

  1. The phone heats a lot.
  
  Slight heating is normal for any smartphone on heavy use but it should not overheat. This phone comes preset with CPU usage in "Balance mode". Change it to "Battery saving mode" (setting explained in Custom Battery configuration below). This will not only reduce the CPU usage but also reduce battery drain. I tested my phone on AnTuTu stability test and the maximum temperature went up to 45 degrees which is quite acceptable.
  

  2. The phone uses an overclocked CPU.
  
  I have come across many posts claiming Xiaomi to mislead customers by providing false information about the CPU being a 1.2Ghz Qualcomm MSM8226 instead of 1.6Ghz Qualcomm MSM8228 as mentioned in their specifications. This is the human mind trying to justify the heating issues. A strip down review of the phone is available on MIUI forum by Robin Ghallasi which confirms the genuinity of the CPU.
  

  3. The phone is weak at memory management and multitasking.
  
  This phone comes preloaded with MIUI which provides the best user experience on Android. But this comes at the cost of higher memory consumption. So it is better to free memory by starting the in-built memory manager by long pressing the menu button before starting high end games needing very high RAM. Moreover MIUI have come with a solution for this by implementing ZRAM memory compression in their latest update v41.1. Just update with the latest OTA update and enjoy smooth multitasking.
  

  4. Apps frequently crash on this phone.
  
  The apps crash when CPU temperatures rise beyond limits. When the heating issues are coupled with low free RAM, the CPU temperatures rise beyond limits when the CPU tries frantically to clear memory on one hand while trying to run the app at full performance on the other. Resolve the above issues and this issue is resolved automatically.
  

  5. Data can't be stored in SD card.
  
  This is a total myth. Using the Explorer app, the data can easily be copied or moved from internal storage to SD card or to any external storage device connected via USB OTG. Moreover the new OTA update v41.1 allows you to store images and videos captured from camera directly to SD Card. Avoid using low quality SD cards which generate more heat.
  

  6. Battery drains out fast
  
  This phone has a 2000 mAh battery and is very decent for its price. Tweak the battery configuration to get the best use of battery. With heavy usage of 3G and wi-fi, I'm able to use the whole day and put it on charge at night. Lithium batteries do not have charging memory and can be charged any time and can be used while charging. However if you need to use it while charging, use a low amperage charger or charge using a PC or laptop's USB port as high amperage charging produces heat in batteries.
  

  7. Display not visible under direct sunlight.
  
  This phone has the best quality of display in its price range comparable to phone double its price. The default setting has brightness set to Automatic 50%. If you find this brightness not sufficient under direct sunlight, adjust the brightness to your liking by opening the quick toggles menu by swiping down at the top of the display.
  

  Custom Battery configuration:
  
  To setup custom battery configuration select Security -> Power -> Battery configuration -> Add configuration.
  
  Give the configuration some name of your choice and set the following
  
  CPU usage: Battery saving
  
  Clean memory: After 1 mins
  
  Brightness: Automatic 33% (or set it up as low as per your liking as screen drains most battery)
  
  Sleep: After 1 minutes of inactivity
  
  Airplane mode: Off
  
  Wi-Fi: Off
  
  2G/3G: Off
  
  Vibrate: Never vibrate
  
  Bluetooth: Off
  
  Sync: Off
  
  GPS: Off
  
  Vibrate on touch: Off
  
  Sound notification on touch: Off
  
  You may also tweak the settings to suit your liking
  

  Overall the phone has the best processor, best display with scratch resistance, and best camera in its price range. The other specs are all above average and quite decent for its price range. MIUI comes with a backup app with which you can backup and uninstall unwanted/unused apps and move them to the SD Card. However for those who want to store apps on SD Card, you will need to root your phone. Best of all rooting does not void warranty.
  

  5 stars for the phone, 5 stars for Flipkart / WS Retail / Delhivery Service.

I read many reviews of this product on Flipkart and I believe most the negative reviews are born out of unreasonable expectation from a phone costing 6K currently. My expectation was not to play Asphalt-8 kind of games on this device. Mid range games like Temple Run-2, Subway surfers etc. are fine. Another observation on available RAM, many people are complaining about the amount of available RAM for other applications. The available RAM is around 400MB. Moto E with latest Kitkat version has also around the same amount of RAM available for user applications. It is advisable not to keep more than 4-5 applications running in the background at any time.
  

  Pros -
  
  1. Better than average build quality.
  
  2. Good screen (though highly reflective when its off).
  
  3. Simplified version of Android (good for those who are not interested in tweaking their phones on regular basis and want a smooth smartphone experience minus high-end gaming).
  
  4. Good for watching online videos.
  
  5. Good back camera.
  
  6. Support for micro SD card up to 64 GB, provides ample storage for multimedia contents.
  
  7. Excellent stand-by battery life.
  

  Cons -
  
  1. Top half heats up considerably on moderate usage, though not very uncomfortable if you are not used to rest all your fingers on top. I have seen similar heating issues with most of the high end phones as well.
  
  2. Battery drains very fast while the phone is in use. However the stand-by time is excellent and almost unmatched in Android world. I have observed similar battery behavior with MIUI with Kitkat 4.4.2 on my Nexus 5 as well. Xiaomi needs to work on this.
  
  3. Below average front camera. It captures very less light and hence you need good lighting conditions for video calls or selfies.
  
  4. Form-factor and weight of this phone are not very comfortable for a 4.7 inch device with 2050 mAH battery.
  

  Overall a very good option for those who want a reasonably good smartphone with reasonable expectations.

Before I bought this phone, I wasn't really convinced that Xiaomi would provide me with a handset of decent quality. But after using this phone for nearly 2 weeks, I have been pleasantly surprised with the quality of the handset.
  

  ****Unboxing****
  
  The box contains nothing but the essentials:
  
  1. The handset and the removable battery
  
  2. A charger with a detachable data cable
  
  3. A quick start guide
  

  ****Initial impressions****
  
  The phone feels solid...no creaking at all. The plastic feels premium, and the screen is incredibly smooth and for some reason, doesn't get smudged by fingerprints. Turning it on, you will be asked to sign in to your MI account, which you can skip.
  

  ****Pros****
  
  1. Solid build quality: The plastic cover is thick and rigid, the handset neatly fit into the hand. Panel gaps are consistently small, and the phone does not flex.
  

  2. Smooth and responsive screen: This phone has the best touch sensitivity of any phone I have owned yet. Ultra responsive, and the Dragon Tail glass is a bonus. No scratches even without a screen guard. Also, the display is a 4.7" IPS HD (not full HD, just HD). So videos and text looks crystal clear.
  

  3. Camera: The quality of the 8MP shooter in the back is just mind-blowing. This phone shares pretty much the same Sony Exmor sensor as the Sony Xperia L. But Xiaomi's software optimization is so good that they make better use of the hardware than Sony itself! Minimal noise, and excellent regulation of light are some highlights. Front camera is decent enough to take selfies, if so inclined.
  

  4. MIUI: This is what makes the phone so attractive. You can customize the UI to suit you, and download themes from the theme store. While stock Android is still the best, it could learn from MIUI in how to make app icons more consistent, so that the home screen looks elegant and organized instead of a jumbled mess.
  

  ****Neutral****
  
  1. Storage: 8 GB of internal storage translates to around 5 GB of usable storage. A decent amount to store apps, but you won't be downloading too many big games. You can insert an SD card to store music, pics and videos.
  

  2. Battery: Decent battery life. Lasts the entire day, so I'm satisfied.
  

  3. Audio: The external speaker seems to buzz when playing any media, but the call quality and headphone port provide high quality audio.
  

  4. RAM: 1 GB of RAM is currently sufficient enough, and I've not faced a single crash or restart even with heavy multitasking. It might be a bit less in the long run, though.
  

  ****Cons****
  
  1. The handset is slippery. You must buy the silicone case, otherwise holding the phone is like holding a bar of soap.
  

  2. The phone occasionally overheats when playing a heavy game, or playing a HD movie. But this is slowly coming back under control. I guess the hardware takes time to "break in", and the MIUI update supposedly fixes the problem.
  

  3. No headphones provided: While that is not a deal-breaker, headphones would have been nice.
  

  ****Overall verdict****
  
  I see why this phone is selling like hot cakes. The quality and features provided at this price point blows away all the competition, and makes Samsung and Sony products look horrible overpriced. There is so much potential in Xiaomi, I can see it become a major competitor in the world market if it continues to make products like these.

column6: Seeing is believing, nothing beats this under the 8-9k price range.
column7:
After going through tonnes of reviews and youtube videos I finally made up my mind and ordered this phone. And after thorough testing I've come to the conclusion that,
  

  What you pay for is definitely not what you get. This device supercedes everything else upto 8-9k range as of December, 2014.
  

  1. First of all I'm an out and out geek, and I want lots of headroom for tinkering with my devices. So first off, the kind of support that is available for this phone out there is amazing. Lots of new ROMS, tweaks and tutorials are posted every hour on XDA and MIUI forums. I straight away installed the MOKEE ROM which is a CM11 ROM based on KitKat 4.4.4. Have already received 3 OTA updates since I installed it a week ago, no bugs or glitches and is completely stable.
  

  2. Not much of a gamer, but I play games like PvZ2, The Room, Leo's Fortune and Prince Of Persia. Absolutely fine, no overheating or crashes. Runs pretty smooth.
  

  3. RAM management on Cyanogenmod has been proven to be very good, and on Redmi 1S I'm glad to say that the statement doesn't change. I always have 4-5 apps open in the background with 300-400 MB RAM always available. Going through apps, menus and everything else is a breeze with no lags or stutters.
  

  4. After 4 complete charging cycles, i.e. 100% to 1%, the average screen on time equates to around 4 hours, and 23 hours for the device overall.
  

  5. Call quality's great, speaker's volume is adequate and can be increased (Head over to the official MIUI Redmi 1S forum, loads of good stuff there) and I haven't had a single problem with WiFi at home and 3G (Airtel) on the go.
  

  6. Sound quality's awesome on the headphones. I use Signature Acoustics C-12 IEMs and Poweramp as my choice for a music app.
  

  7. Best of all, you don't void your warranty when you root your device or install any custom ROM. Infact, the moderators on official forums and the company itself promotes using the phone to its maximum potential.
  

  The only problem I have is with the proximity sensor of this phone which refuses to work 3-4 out of 10 times. It's a global problem with a lot of customers (as seen on the MIUI forums) but there are tutorials there on how to calibrate the proximity sensor again, which I did after which it works pretty well.
  

  Personally I think this phone will satisfy any techie out there at this price range with its plethora of customization options available and the hardware underneath. I don't prefer to buy the Android One/Micromax and other similar brand offerings just because of the lack of updates and lack of support/mods/ROMs for the device on prominent Android websites such as XDA. On top of that their after sale services are nothing to be proud of. Xiaomi straight replaces the device if there's anything wrong within the warranty period.
  

  Phew, I'm tired, but I hope it helps someone out there who's confused (I was) on whether to shell out money for this device or not.

column6: Excellent phone for the middle class Indian!!
column7:
I love this phone. I bought it on 6th Oct (Big billion day) and received the shipment very quickly. Loved the packing. I used a stanchart card so there was a 10% discount and also got a Rs.300 cashback voucher so effectively it cost me Rs.5149. I got screen guards and sim trays as part of the deal. I had a lot of trouble putting the screen guard on, I guess that was my fault. The phone was rocking, and it received the MIUI update to version 5 in the next 5-6 days. It did heat up quite a bit on playing games or charging and playing games/watching media at the same time. The battery, which was earlier rapidly, now was holding charge better.
  

  I installed an app called Snapdragon Batteryguru to make the battery last longer. In any case, if you are addicted to your phone then make sure you carry a battery bank because though the heating and battery drain problem was somewhat solved, the issues largely remained. I guess that's the cost of buying a cheap phone.
  

  This is one issue I never heard from anyone: When I played audio or video on the phone, it started shaking! Funny part is, this continued even when I played it on Bluetooth! It felt like there is some insect inside the phone trying to get out. This was not a major inconvenience, but a drawback, nonetheless.
  

  So why did I give a 5 star rating? What Xiaomi is doing here is giving a slightly older technology in a not-so-stylish phone at ridiculously low prices while still maintaining a decent level of quality. My phone rarely hanged or dropped a call or showed lags in video or gameplay, although some games such as Plants Vs Zombies 2 give quite a few phones the jitter. But this one got a bit angry (heated up), but no lags. Now that's got to count given the price point. The picture and video quality of this one is leaps and bounds ahead of other phones in this price range. Of course as brand grows, I expect them to raise prices and become just like any other company, but till that time does not come, its party time for consumers. Remember what Reliance did to the Indian mobile phone industry in 2003 when it launched the Rs.500 phone. I think something similar is happening now. As long as I have my phones cheap while my work gets done, I am happy. I don't  have the intent of buying an expensive cutting edge phone and having it replaced it with another one 6 months later while I sell the old phone at a loss. I'm happy with a cheap, flawed-but-excellent-value-for-money phone
  


  Having had a brush with a Xiaomi phone, I decided to explore further. By default, random Chinese phones some 10 years back had a very bad name, so I was quite sceptical about Xiaomi as a company. But having read so much on the net about the feedback and having a first hand experience, I decided to trust this rapidly growing company. I sold it last week and purchased the Redmi Note on Dec 2nd. I am glad to say that till now, the Note has been just as I had expected, probably better.

  1) at the first step root the phone, (refer MIUI blog or simply google to find)
  
  2) install "No-frills CPU" from Play store.
  
  3) Under clock the CPU speed to Max - 1100 mhz or 787mhz  and set minimum speed to 300 mhz
  
  4) then "install Greenif"y app and hibernate the unwanted apps that is not in use.
  
  5) Install Titanium back app and remove some of unwanted MIUI apps (System apps)  which consumes more RAM. but be cautious in removing system apps bcoz it may lead to system instability. better remove unwanted themes.
  
  6) never use auto bright ness mode - bcoz, when I contacted flipkart technical team, they said light sensors may consume more battery life,, i personally checked this info also.
  

  by doing these above steps, definitely solves the heating problem and battery drainage. i have tested for three days after doing above steps and it worked fine for me.
  

  Rest of all Pros are already discussed by other users.
  

  As of now this is the only solvation as i found. The update version of V45 is not helped in Heating issues but it improved bugs fixes when compared to previous V 36 .
  

  I thought have giving five stars as a rating, since the issues i faced, i give 2 stars to device and five stars to flipkart (Delivery, Good response from Technical team)

column6: Excellent little toy turned out to be a cool phone
column7:
In no way could you pass up on this gadget. For 6 smackers you get the specs of a Motorolla G (spec 2). Coming from an iOS background the transition to MiUI was easy. Apps do not crash, games run well on medium settings, audio is the best part, it is on par with beats on HTC ONE and iPhone. Video quality is superior to the other competing 720p screens, with the exception of the retinas. The screen has a good layer of oleophobic coating, one swipe on your jeans and the smudges are gone. Like the iMessaging service these guys have a MiUI messaging app. And the cloud storage is good for contacts, notes and app data backups (which is free). The build quality of the device is not a replica but similar to nokia, very sturdy, yet light weight.
  

  UPDATE: After 2 days of usage, and customizations, I can frankly state this is an iOS killer. It is the best android experience I've had so far. Notification management is similar to iOS, even the default apps are similar to it. And talk about the screen its a premium HD IPS screen made by Sharp, I've played a ripped 1080P movie on the phone, and I was in for a surprise, no lag or frames missing at all. This too was from a class 4 storage card. And another cool feature is the led indicator, you can change the color for each type of notification, red is for messages, green is for calls and blue for the rest. Just like iOS you have an option to send messages to the callers without answering their calls. One thing I can't seem to figure out is the app names, being cut out. In terms of games this puppy can handle them all, at medium settings without losing frames. Real Racing 3 and Shadow Fight 2 are power hungry game apps, after 1 hour 27 minutes on Shadow Fight 2, neither the phone warmed up nor it crashed. Again if you're going to run it at high settings, instead of medium, you're going to lose frames, it'll warm up and perhaps shut down as it does not have the graphics or memory to support that task. Use the hardware as it is designed, if you throw over powering things at it, you'll be disappointed. I think that's what the rest of the users are doing, playing all the games at MAX, and running the screen too bright, letting multiple apps run in the background. Be it any device, if you try to out perform it by assigning 100s of tasks it'll fail.
  

  I'll keep posting updates, as and when something changes for the better or worse.
  

  --
  
  Numair Ali Aidroos

column6: Detailed review after testing and using the mobile for 1 week
column7:
I would definitely recommend this phone to customers having budget less than 12K and looking for a phone with latest hardware and very good performance. I would list out the pros and cons which i have felt after using the phone for over 1 week now :
  

  Pros :
  
  1) The display is very vivid and clear. 312 ppi is not disappointing at all. Full HD videos are very crisp and clear.
  
  2) Sound quality via the speakers is above average and loud. But the audio output via the earphones will beat almost all the phones available in market these days. If you have a nice set of earphones, then the audio quality will be the best with the Audio Enhancer available in stock music player. I have tested the audio output on Sennheiser MX170, Sony MDR-XB600 and Apple iTouch earphones. This phone is a must have for music lovers.
  
  3) Brilliant camera is what i can say. Both rear and front camera will surprise you with such a fine quality image generated. Very good quality lens used.
  
  4) The build quality is very good and simple.
  
  5) MIUI is very good with loads of features, utilities to play with. MIUI will almost cover all your needs, which earlier required many apps to be installed on the phone.
  
  6) Call quality is good and there is no issue in data connectivity via 3G or 2G SIM.
  

  Cons :
  
  1) The mobile heats up at the rear below camera lens when you use it heavily with charger connected. If you are browsing on 3G with charger connected, the phone heats up very much.
  
  2) RAM is at a bit of downside on this phone. The phone becomes a bit slow when you are using multiple apps. The cache can be cleared very easily though. I would recommend rebooting the device daily at least once for optimum performance.
  
  3) The battery stays hardly for a day when used only on 2G data. With 3G switched on the battery will stay only for 7-8 hours with normal usage. So for heavy users, the phone has to be charged twice daily.
  

  I hope xiaomi will look into this cons and get a better solution in their next update.
  

  Overall i had an awesome experience using this phone.
  

  -Aravind NS

column7:
First of all to all those people who are planning to buy this phone seeing the specs and watching all the reviews on youtube.......DONT!!!
  
  Seriously, the phone heats up like hell and I know heating is normal in a Quad core phone but trust me this phone doesn't just heat up it cooks up......also the battery is just pathetic and dont get me started on the RAM management even games like 'Subway Surfers' lags sometimes.
  
  All this happens only because of the greediness of Xiaomi, what they have done is.... to up the specs power of the phone they are using a processor that is optimum at 1.2-1.4 Ghz and clocking it at 1.6 Ghz.....this is the reason behind all the heating up and battery usage.
  
  What else would you expect if you try to make a donkey run like a horse. The result is Redmi 1S.
  
  There are many pros as well especially the screen and camera are top notch no doubt about that, at this price bracket such a camera is remarkable. Also the build quality is solid, something that really impressed me (considering its a Chinese brand). But all in all I think the cons outweigh the pros, the new "Android One" will be a much smarter choice.
  

  So this is it for the people who have not bought this phone, however I understand the agony we go through after buying it the heating, the battery, BUT there is a way around it, FIRST of all you HAVE TO root your phone, without rooting I'm afraid its just not possible. So after you root it, which is pretty easy according to me, you just have to download a zip file and then rebbot it in Recovery mode (refer Google for all the steps), you can downlaod 'No Frills CPU Control' and give it root permission, then set the maximum limit to 1.306 Ghz and minimum to 364 Mhz. This solved the heating and battery issue for me but not to a great extent.
  
  The RAM issue on the other hand was not solved and I could not find another solution either. You could try and uninstall all the unnecessary apps like 'Hindi Input' 'Pinyin Input' etc. But I dont think its going to make a huge difference. Hopefully when the KitKat update comes out it will be
  
  Also I read that some people had problems with their calls, since I've never had such a problem ( I've been using it for 15 odd days) I guess it will be solved once you update the MIUI.
  
  Well as a summary this is not a very good phone all because of Xiaomi, but it can be made into one.

I have been using this phone for a month for my regular day to day use, In past I have used (tested) other devices such as Moto G (1st Gen) & Xperia L, I didnt notice any big flaw in the Redmi 1s, compared with them [Note: Both these are above 12k].

  1. Primary Camera [The best compared with Micromax Nitro(13mp) ]
  
  2. Performance [ Smooth and Lag free Racing Games and 1080p Videos ]

  Now as for the performance yes, it has a few issues such as low RAM availability. You will have at most 350-400 MB available. But I feel that it is more than enough for normal usage. And of course Xiaomi has not made it a "Gaming Phone". Its a normal daily use phone.
  

  The MIUI interface is great. Better than the normal Android UI. But if you have used Android before, it will take time to adjust to a few things. The messaging app is great though. You can hide personal messages...
  

  The battery lasts for about a day, if you are using it normally with 3g connected. But drains away fast when connected to WIFI or playing games or videos.
  

  Camera is extremely good...of course a few people are saying that its average and all...but dude just tell me how much have you invested on the phone again...
  

  Display is charming...Try to watch high quality 720p and 1080p videos on this...you will start loving this phone.
  

  Overall lets be frank...by the time of writing this review...you will not get a better phone within this price range...So guys who are really price conscious just go for it...what are you waiting for???

This is a great device for it's price. If you like Xiaomi and love it's features, you'll like this phone. If you play a lot of games, watch a lot of videos, surf the internet a lot.. if you do anything which involves the screen a lot, you'll love this phone. I'm pretty sure that no one is here for a full review of this phone (if you want a full review there are dozens of them a 'Google' away).
  

  Still, I have to comment about the screen. It is HUGE. Maybe even a bit more than the Note series. And as is obvious, if you don't like big screens back off, this device is not for you. The phone does have a one handed mode where the display shrinks to 4 inches. But personally, I love big phones.
  
  The Xiaomi's 'skin' does give this phone a new life. The MIUI does it's job perfectly optimizing 3 GB of RAM. I have never had a single lag on this device,  and I use this device a lot. But I have seen that the fingerprint senson sometimes act odd and won't recognise my finger. But a software update can fix that.
  
  If you are a developer, this is not very much recommended. But still it has TWRP and LineageOS officially supported, so if you don't like MIUI and the Xiaomi crapware (which you probably won't if you're a dev ;)) you can always switch to Lineage.
  

  So, overall. It's a great phone to have. And yeah, I recommend it under 20k (after the Moto G5 Plus, of course)

column6: Just buy it without thinking but only from flipkart.
column7:
I bought this phone from flipkart, and got it delivered just in 2 days to my location.
  
  About the product -
  
  The best phone in this price range, I ordered the 2 GB RAM/16 GB variant, but there was no difference between this and 3GB variant in day to day tasks performed on the phone.
  
  Just dont think too much, no need to read the negative reviews, I used the phone, played games, used for hotspot, calls, pictures, used it as much as I can, and It never heated up other than while charging, as was mentioned by many other negative reviews. And its normal if a phone heats up to a particular level. I dont know why people don't understand that any electronics with a processing power will heat up while processing at high end, and while gaming any processor will be used to its maximum so its just pretty normal for the device to heat up.
  
  Battery lasts for 1 day with maximum usage, may last longer if used mildly, everything else is fantastic, just few cons are -
  

  1.Due to the back metal body and its design, it slips from hand as it is too slippery to hold, so get a case or cover for back right after u buy this phone
  

  2.Camera quality is below average, but that is due to software issue,as the other Mi phones with same camera have better quality, so it will be solved in the marshmallow update hopefully.
  

  About the flipkart service and seller(SuperComNet) -
  

  They are the best, I never had any problem with flipkart service, they take care of the customer too well, easy delivery, easy return, easy refund.
  
  I actually received a Mi phone with damaged screen which I couldn't notice from 2 days of the purchase as it was very small crack, so when I removed the screen cover that comes with the phone I saw it. It was scary to see a damage on my new phone, I was worried that flipkart will take the product back as they could have blamed me for the damage. So I requested a return, and I got informed that I will be contacted by their technician who was very helpful when I got a call from the tech, I told her my problem and she accepted the return, Return was accepted at 11:00 AM and the pick up was done at 11:30 AM the same day, I thought it will take days to get my refund back after the picup, but to my surprise the amount was initiated the very next day in my bank account early in the morning and I was able to order another phone from flipkart, I could't be any more happy from the service provided by flipkart.

column6: Excellent flagship for an unbeatable price
column7:
Overheating?: I was initially concerned about the reports of overheating from reviews on FK as well as from some reviewers. After using the phone for a few days I have not experienced any overheating. Like all phones, it gets a bit warm if you use it while charging and also for highly intensive games. But even during gaming, it never got too hot, just slightly warm. This is on Asphalt 8, Subway Surfers and Clash of Clans.
  

  Design: The device feels extremely great in your hand, even better than the Mi 3 and much nicer than the bigger phablets like Zenfone 2 and Honor 4x. The matte finish make the device feel premium. Every person I have shown my phone to has first commented on how light it feels, but also remarked how solid it is.
  

  Battery: The battery has been great, easily lasts me a day with some room to spare.
  

  Display: This is the main reason why I decided to buy the Mi 4i. The display is unparalleled in this price range and even in 20k+ devices. 1080p display just looks beautiful. The Corning OGS glass is same as GG 3 and makes me feel safe with my purchase. Also, I thought Sunlight Display was just a marketing gimmick, but it actually makes it easier to use my phone outdoors.
  

  Performance: Really love the performance of this phone. There are some minor lags after playing games for 30min+. Once the device cools down again it works as normal.
  

  Overall: Best phone since Mi 3. Don't believe the overheating reports until you actually use the phone. I was worried after watching a YouTube video showing really bad overheating, but he switched on performance mode. I have not seen any overheating in default mode and am still able to play all the games I want.

column6: Bang for the buck...with a catch
column7:
Here is what you need to know about the phone before you purchase:
  

  The good:
  
  1. Amazing display with display calibration and color gamut found in Apple Hardware. The sunlight readability works as advertised.
  
  2. Well built with anti-slip matte back and very light weight. Easy to hold and won't drop too often unless you are butter-fingered
  
  3. 'Flagship-grade' rear camera with quick focus, good HDR mode and great details and colors. Decent front cam, gets the job done but don't expect much detail in the picture
  
  4. Good battery life. Lasts a typical work day with about 20% battery left. Obviously depends on usage pattern. For better battery life, keep the phone in balanced performance mode and 40-50% brightness set on Auto
  
  5. Did I say, gorgeous display ;)
  

  The bad:
  
  1. Performance is middling at best and doesn't deserve a 'flagship' rating. App launches are slow, sometimes won't happen at all. Signs of an unoptimised OS running on decent hardware. Expect a Day 0 software update of 800 mb+ which is a must-have else the phone overheats and performance stays sluggish. There is an update in the works which should fix most of the issues though.
  
  2. Battery life could have been better. A problem possibly because of Lollipop 5.0.2. An update to 5.1 is needed to remove memory leak and battery life problems which should happen soon enough.

column6: Complete satisfaction and more than expected.
column7:
Hi,
  

  Bought this phone in the third flash sale because I was waiting to know the reviews about this phone from the previous customers. So far, this phone has been very impressive and I have no complaints (just a missing external memory card slot, which is not really a big deal). This phone was delivered in a day's time, which was good.
  

  Following things I've noticed after using my phone;
  

  HEATING - This phone heats up normally like every other phone, it has no extensive heating issues like every other person has been complaining about in their reviews. If you play heavy games continuously for like 10 minutes or so, the phone heats up a little bit, but that is completely normal. Even while charging or talking on the phone for quite sometime, the phone will heat up, but in a normal way like almost every other phone. I had updated my phone almost immediately after opening the package, so I don't know about the heating issue before the update, but as of now, its completely fine.
  

  CAMERA - The camera in this phone is freaking brilliant. If you're getting blurred photos from your Mi4i camera, then you're just not focusing it properly because it has a manual focus as well (tap on the screen where you want to focus). None of my photos have come out blur (what I had focused on came out crisp clear). The front camera is also equally good. Sometimes the photos do come out a little (just a little) grainy, but remember, sometimes even digital cameras and dslrs' produce a little grainy photos and that is not the fault of the camera. Grainy photos are produced due to low light.
  

  RAM - 2gb RAM helps a lot. The phones barely lags and when it does, its for barely a second and that is totally manageable. I've noticed that the phone lags only when I switch from app to app very quickly, like when you open one app by mistake and realize that's not the app you wanted to open and then you click the home button and then quickly click on the other app, that's when the phone lags. That's not even the right way to operate a phone I think, so I'd take the blame for that. There is a shortcut button for task messenger (left bottom, feather touch button) which shows what all apps are running in the background and you have the option to kill those apps instantly. After the first update, the free memory after killings all apps would be around 400mb. I got a third update (one day before writing this review) and after that the free memory goes up to 700mb. No worries about the RAM in this phone and no lag issues.
  

  INTERNAL MEMORY - Of course, an external memory card slot would have been a major plus point, but quite frankly 16gb memory is enough. You get to use almost 10gb only because the system also uses a lot of memory. If you think you're running low on phone memory, then please check the photos that you've clicked from your phone and the music list. I had low memory issues with my previous phone only because of excessive and unwanted photos and music in my phone. Otherwise, the memory issue should not be there.
  

  SPEAKER/HEADPHONES - The volume of the sound is actually less, even at full volume. Sound quality is not bad. People have been complaining about poor sound quality and that isn't the case. Sound quality is definitely not great, but it's definitely not bad. Sad thing is, earphones were not provided along with this phone. So pair up your phone with some really good earphones and enjoy the music.
  

  BATTERY - Though the battery capacity is really good, I don't get a very good backup as I use too many things on the phone and some heavy apps. If you play a lot on this phone (or any other phone also), the battery will die faster. Internet browsing, facebook, whatsapp, games, etc do drain the battery, but there are certain apps which run in the background which also helps in draining the battery. The default security app scans the phone at times without your notice, but I'm not sure if that does too much damage. Otherwise, the battery backup is good. Lasts properly for a day and a half with heavy usage of the phone.
  

  DESIGN - The phone has a very beautiful and a minimal design, nothing unnecessary on the front or the back. The back panel is a little slippery, but it ain't a problem. The interface of this phone is simply amazing with a lot of customizing options, just love it.
  

  VOLUME/POWER BUTTON - A little sharp, but you'll get used to it. So far no cuts on my finger and it will not even cut your finger.
  

  SIM CARD SLOT - The pin to open the sim card slot was not provided with this phone. I had to use a paper clip for this. The slot does not open instantly once you insert the pin in the hole. I had to literally force the pin inside and was scared of damaging it, but it finally came out. Just be careful on this one.
  

  Verdict - Amazing phone, seriously no complaints. Go for it. If you do have complaints, then you're probably not using it right. Cheers!

I must say this is one of those product, where a person is on a crossroad seeing Performance, Quality and Monetary satisfaction together. But before i move towards pros and cons of Mi 4i, i have being reading a lot about the heating issues from my other fellow users.
  
  The simple step to AVOID OVER-HEATING is to UPDATE YOUR SYSTEM to latest version. That's it.
  
  To do this, click settings < about phone < system updates. (make sure your are connected to a decent internet connection because you will be required to download a 806mb update)
  

  Before updating, the phone used to get heated within minutes of normal usage but now its running smoothly without giving me a tan.
  
  After updating i have been using this phone for 2 hours on a stretch, that too with wifi on, and I didn't find any over-heating issues. So before you start doing experiments with Mi 4i camera and other stuffs, make sure you have updated your Mi 4i system first. But still, a little Heads-Up from Xiaomi would have been better in this regard.
  
  Now the,
  

  Pros:
  
  1)Excellent Display screen (finally i can see in bright sunlight what on earth am i clicking)
  
  2)Strong Wifi receiver when you compare it with other phones (even the high end ones)
  
  3)No useless bloatwares
  
  4)Yes outer body is made of plastic but its nowhere near to being labeled as cheap. In-fact its very good, look-wise and the feel.
  
  5)The best part are its touch and user interface. Smooth and lag free.
  

  Cons:
  
  1)Average speaker
  
  2)Power and Volume Button could have been more sturdy
  
  3)Heating issues prior to System update(Yes, this nuisance went away after update)
  
  4)Only 10.83 GB available to users out of 16 GB(Considering there is no slot for SD card)
  

  Everything has two sides to it and overall am very satisfied with this product.

column6: Best Mobile in 9k (Review after 1 week usage)
column7:
Got this mobile in big billion sale in 9k (10k + 10% bank offer). Coming to the points about this phone
  

  1. MIUI 7 update has arrived to Mi 4i and it has solved all problems with phone. Dont believe anyone who says phone gets overheated. I have tested it using CPU-Z application, now temperatures remain within 38-43 degree limits and at the same time Xiaomi has enabled all 8 cores at the same time (earlier only 6 cores were enabled in normal mode to prevent overheating which resulted in lags , stutter and slow performance) but now phone gives better performance with all 8 cores On and almost no lags.   3. After update to MIUI 7, free Ram is also increased 850MB. And phone has become less laggy and faster.
  

  4. Camera is really class. Beautiful stunning pics captured. I actually bought it because of its camera.
  

  5. Storage is limited as you all know..but it does not bother me that much.

column6: Superb For Such A Small Price Tag
column7:
Before I go into my first week review, a little background on my smartphone experience. I started with Samsung S3 and then jumped up to HTC One M8 and finally landed on the Mi 4i. I gave away my HTC One M8 to my dad and I wanted to try something in the lower price bracket. I am not expecting at par performance with the M8 because few phones can match its performance but if the Mi 4i can even come 70% close to meeting the M8's awesome feel I will be grateful.
  

  A week has passed and I had ordered this on the 11th June registered sale. I got a defective piece on 12th June, the phone just did not start even after fully charging the batteries. Called up Flipkart customer care and they were prompt in replacing the set. I got my replacement on 14th June and now have used it for 3 days. I feel 3 days is enough to get a first impression of any phone and here's my take.
  

  Design: 7/10
  
  I loved the metallic design and the curves of the HTC One M8 and compared to that the Mi 4i is a bit plastic but for the price it sure does look glamorous. Just pair it with a good cover and it is sure to stand out from the crowd.
  

  Screen: 10/10
  
  Yup, the screen clarity is at par with the HTC One M8. In fact, the sharpness of logos and icons, text is just uncanny. Downside though is that notification top bar is tiny and at times so are other areas but at least very very clear. Videos in HD look beautiful.
  

  Camera: 9/10
  
  Back camera takes awesome pictures although low light pics leave a bit to the imagination. Overall though the camera is splendid with aperture control, real time effect control, HDR and other controls while you take a picture. Front camera is equally impressive and I feel that both cameras actually deliver above the price tag of the phone.
  

  Music: 10/10
  
  I don't really care for music from the built-in speakers neither do I ever use a phone to listen to music. Frankly phones can never come close to the quality you get from good music players or DACs. I use a Cowon D2+ with a E11K Amp paired with an AudioTechnica M50x to listen to music so trust me when I say this - this is the best damn sounding phone I have tried thus far with headphones on. Built-in equalizer does a wonderful job and it works even if you try it with internet radio apps such as Gaana, Murfie and more.
  

  Connectivity: 7/10
  
  WiFi I feel is a bit sluggish but it is ok, not something I can't live without. Mobile Data connection though feels more fluid. You get a 3.5mm jack and a data charging mini-USB port. No expansion slot to add a memory card, so beware if you think otherwise. What it does support is OTG so you can connect hard drives or pen drives directly and use data stored there to play videos and more.
  

  Heating & Performance: 7/10
  
  The phone does heat up when it charges battery, when you are on a call for long or doing something processor intensive such as multi-tasking or playing a game. It is not unbearable and similar to what I faced with the Samsung S3. As for performance, you have two modes, Balanced and Performance mode. In the balanced mode, it is sluggish and can at times hang on some apps, mine does on Murfie. In the performance mode, it is just slightly sluggish at times but most of the time fluent. Just remember to manually drop apps that you are finished using.
  

  Overall: 10/10
  
  Considering the price tag of the phone, you better not expect a 10 by 10 in all departments but overall for the areas where it does average, it has plenty more where it excels. So for just 13k this is the best damn phone right now in the market and I am comparing it to phones as high as 17 to 18k.
  

  PS: Get the Graphene Armor ULTRA HD tempered glass to protect your screen, it does not detract from the screen in any way and also remember to download the 800MB update the moment you get your phone setup, it does take care of many issues previously mentioned by other reviewers.
