column6: The ultimate beast of your home
column7:
Giving a clear and practical review after using for 3 weeks continuously.
  
  Firstly I would like to give the Tips for the existing and upcoming users as it will help you more than reading the reviews.
  
  1. If you get the phone with MIUI 6.5.3 update kindly update it to 6.5.4 asap. It will completely reduce all the heating issues. Otherwise you will feel the phone a fry pan.
  
  2. After receiving peel off the company fitted matte screen protector and place a 8-9H tempered screen guard as the phone doesn't have gorilla glass.
  
  3. Dont try to take pics with manual mode until you know it well.
  
  4.Use a hard back case for keeping away the phone form dust,oil. Still the phone has rubber washable nano finish back but it is recommended to use a back case.
  
  5.Don't access "permission manager". If you turn on the permission manager on many app features will be hidden.
  
  6. Try to off WIFI and mobile data as per your convenience for better battery backup and low heating of the phone.
  
  6.Dont use any launcher instead try to apply the themes available in MI themes.
  


  1. Look and comfortability
  
  Mi 4i is the slimmest phone in this range I can challenge. When you hold only the phone without any cover it will give you 1005 comfort to hold it for long times, When in call it is also very comfortable to hold the phone. Its trendy white and black combination gives an mind blowing stylish look.
  
  2. Performance
  
  I mainly do internet surfing,little bit gaming,photography,music and youtube. After doing all these things it gives a super 24 hour backup. I only charge once in a day. Coming to its octa core processor. Truly it has a superb speed of performance. It hardly gets hanged with the lucid combination of 2gb RAM and 8 core processor.
  
  3. Camera
  
  Its 13MP cam is truly 13MP. You can compare the images taken in daylight with A DSLR clicked image. Its front 5MP cam is just superb for taking selfies. Video quality is very good. But please don't click with manual mode untill you are not so accustomed to click picture in manual mode. It will give you a bad impression of the camera.
  
  4.Network
  
  Network reception is too good. It will give you the best 3g experience. Mobile data service is promptly switched on after you on the option.
  
  5.UI
  
  The MIUI 6 based on Android L is very good. Unlike the pure android versions you will get many more inbulit features for which you have to install 3rd party apps. Like-junk cleaner,app lock and many more.
  
  6.Sound
  
  The sound output is quite low but clear. You will get clear ans bass full sound in headphone. But if you listen songs only in phone then it is little bit low.
  
  7. Display
  
  The full HD IPS display will give you best out of your videos,movies. Display is very very clear. But it should have Gorilla glass 3.
  
  You will get much more than what you are paying. Go ahead for the phone if you are looking for a handy,sexy,performance mi-budget phone.

column6: Bang for the buck...with a catch
column7:
Here is what you need to know about the phone before you purchase:
  

  The good:
  
  1. Amazing display with display calibration and color gamut found in Apple Hardware. The sunlight readability works as advertised.
  
  2. Well built with anti-slip matte back and very light weight. Easy to hold and won't drop too often unless you are butter-fingered
  
  3. 'Flagship-grade' rear camera with quick focus, good HDR mode and great details and colors. Decent front cam, gets the job done but don't expect much detail in the picture
  
  4. Good battery life. Lasts a typical work day with about 20% battery left. Obviously depends on usage pattern. For better battery life, keep the phone in balanced performance mode and 40-50% brightness set on Auto
  
  5. Did I say, gorgeous display ;)
  

  The bad:
  
  1. Performance is middling at best and doesn't deserve a 'flagship' rating. App launches are slow, sometimes won't happen at all. Signs of an unoptimised OS running on decent hardware. Expect a Day 0 software update of 800 mb+ which is a must-have else the phone overheats and performance stays sluggish. There is an update in the works which should fix most of the issues though.
  
  2. Battery life could have been better. A problem possibly because of Lollipop 5.0.2. An update to 5.1 is needed to remove memory leak and battery life problems which should happen soon enough.
  
  3. The balanced mode takes the life out of this phone. Multitasking is a pain, app launches slow down further and you can notice the stutter in animations.
  
  4. Continuous camera usage can overheat the phone to the point that the camera app starts to lag a lot and the focus struggles. You will have to let the phone cool down to go back to smooth performance.
  
  5. Severe CPU throttling when phone heats. Don't know if its the OS or the Snapdragon 615 problem. We will know after the Software update for sure.
  
  6. 16 GB non-expandable storage with about 11GB of user available memory. If you keep a lot of media or love to take pictures, you might wanna wait for the 32/64gb one
  
  7. The OS uses a lot of RAM. 1.5Gb out of 2 is usually taken by MIUI. This is not a deal breaker but definitely a drain on performance and battery life. Lots of other bugs which need a fix.
  
  8. Only white option. If you've got to give only 1 option, make it black. seriously.
  

  NOTE to Buyers:
  
  If you see a lot of heating in general use or a light bleed below the backlit buttons, ask for a replacement right away. The heating problem is mitigated by the update so do that before you ask for replacement. The light bleed problem is due to poor panel lamination and replacement is the only option.

column6: Complete satisfaction and more than expected.
column7:
Hi,
  

  Bought this phone in the third flash sale because I was waiting to know the reviews about this phone from the previous customers. So far, this phone has been very impressive and I have no complaints (just a missing external memory card slot, which is not really a big deal). This phone was delivered in a day's time, which was good.
  

  Following things I've noticed after using my phone;
  

  HEATING - This phone heats up normally like every other phone, it has no extensive heating issues like every other person has been complaining about in their reviews. If you play heavy games continuously for like 10 minutes or so, the phone heats up a little bit, but that is completely normal. Even while charging or talking on the phone for quite sometime, the phone will heat up, but in a normal way like almost every other phone. I had updated my phone almost immediately after opening the package, so I don't know about the heating issue before the update, but as of now, its completely fine.
  

  CAMERA - The camera in this phone is freaking brilliant. If you're getting blurred photos from your Mi4i camera, then you're just not focusing it properly because it has a manual focus as well (tap on the screen where you want to focus). None of my photos have come out blur (what I had focused on came out crisp clear). The front camera is also equally good. Sometimes the photos do come out a little (just a little) grainy, but remember, sometimes even digital cameras and dslrs' produce a little grainy photos and that is not the fault of the camera. Grainy photos are produced due to low light.
  

  RAM - 2gb RAM helps a lot. The phones barely lags and when it does, its for barely a second and that is totally manageable. I've noticed that the phone lags only when I switch from app to app very quickly, like when you open one app by mistake and realize that's not the app you wanted to open and then you click the home button and then quickly click on the other app, that's when the phone lags. That's not even the right way to operate a phone I think, so I'd take the blame for that. There is a shortcut button for task messenger (left bottom, feather touch button) which shows what all apps are running in the background and you have the option to kill those apps instantly. After the first update, the free memory after killings all apps would be around 400mb. I got a third update (one day before writing this review) and after that the free memory goes up to 700mb. No worries about the RAM in this phone and no lag issues.
  

  INTERNAL MEMORY - Of course, an external memory card slot would have been a major plus point, but quite frankly 16gb memory is enough. You get to use almost 10gb only because the system also uses a lot of memory. If you think you're running low on phone memory, then please check the photos that you've clicked from your phone and the music list. I had low memory issues with my previous phone only because of excessive and unwanted photos and music in my phone. Otherwise, the memory issue should not be there.
  

  SPEAKER/HEADPHONES - The volume of the sound is actually less, even at full volume. Sound quality is not bad. People have been complaining about poor sound quality and that isn't the case. Sound quality is definitely not great, but it's definitely not bad. Sad thing is, earphones were not provided along with this phone. So pair up your phone with some really good earphones and enjoy the music.
  

  BATTERY - Though the battery capacity is really good, I don't get a very good backup as I use too many things on the phone and some heavy apps. If you play a lot on this phone (or any other phone also), the battery will die faster. Internet browsing, facebook, whatsapp, games, etc do drain the battery, but there are certain apps which run in the background which also helps in draining the battery. The default security app scans the phone at times without your notice, but I'm not sure if that does too much damage. Otherwise, the battery backup is good. Lasts properly for a day and a half with heavy usage of the phone.
  

  DESIGN - The phone has a very beautiful and a minimal design, nothing unnecessary on the front or the back. The back panel is a little slippery, but it ain't a problem. The interface of this phone is simply amazing with a lot of customizing options, just love it.
  

  VOLUME/POWER BUTTON - A little sharp, but you'll get used to it. So far no cuts on my finger and it will not even cut your finger.
  

  SIM CARD SLOT - The pin to open the sim card slot was not provided with this phone. I had to use a paper clip for this. The slot does not open instantly once you insert the pin in the hole. I had to literally force the pin inside and was scared of damaging it, but it finally came out. Just be careful on this one.
  

  Verdict - Amazing phone, seriously no complaints. Go for it. If you do have complaints, then you're probably not using it right. Cheers!

column6: Superb For Such A Small Price Tag
column7:
Before I go into my first week review, a little background on my smartphone experience. I started with Samsung S3 and then jumped up to HTC One M8 and finally landed on the Mi 4i. I gave away my HTC One M8 to my dad and I wanted to try something in the lower price bracket. I am not expecting at par performance with the M8 because few phones can match its performance but if the Mi 4i can even come 70% close to meeting the M8's awesome feel I will be grateful.
  

  A week has passed and I had ordered this on the 11th June registered sale. I got a defective piece on 12th June, the phone just did not start even after fully charging the batteries. Called up Flipkart customer care and they were prompt in replacing the set. I got my replacement on 14th June and now have used it for 3 days. I feel 3 days is enough to get a first impression of any phone and here's my take.
  

  Design: 7/10
  
  I loved the metallic design and the curves of the HTC One M8 and compared to that the Mi 4i is a bit plastic but for the price it sure does look glamorous. Just pair it with a good cover and it is sure to stand out from the crowd.
  

  Screen: 10/10
  
  Yup, the screen clarity is at par with the HTC One M8. In fact, the sharpness of logos and icons, text is just uncanny. Downside though is that notification top bar is tiny and at times so are other areas but at least very very clear. Videos in HD look beautiful.
  

  Camera: 9/10
  
  Back camera takes awesome pictures although low light pics leave a bit to the imagination. Overall though the camera is splendid with aperture control, real time effect control, HDR and other controls while you take a picture. Front camera is equally impressive and I feel that both cameras actually deliver above the price tag of the phone.
  

  Music: 10/10
  
  I don't really care for music from the built-in speakers neither do I ever use a phone to listen to music. Frankly phones can never come close to the quality you get from good music players or DACs. I use a Cowon D2+ with a E11K Amp paired with an AudioTechnica M50x to listen to music so trust me when I say this - this is the best damn sounding phone I have tried thus far with headphones on. Built-in equalizer does a wonderful job and it works even if you try it with internet radio apps such as Gaana, Murfie and more.
  

  Connectivity: 7/10
  
  WiFi I feel is a bit sluggish but it is ok, not something I can't live without. Mobile Data connection though feels more fluid. You get a 3.5mm jack and a data charging mini-USB port. No expansion slot to add a memory card, so beware if you think otherwise. What it does support is OTG so you can connect hard drives or pen drives directly and use data stored there to play videos and more.
  

  Heating & Performance: 7/10
  
  The phone does heat up when it charges battery, when you are on a call for long or doing something processor intensive such as multi-tasking or playing a game. It is not unbearable and similar to what I faced with the Samsung S3. As for performance, you have two modes, Balanced and Performance mode. In the balanced mode, it is sluggish and can at times hang on some apps, mine does on Murfie. In the performance mode, it is just slightly sluggish at times but most of the time fluent. Just remember to manually drop apps that you are finished using.
  

  Overall: 10/10
  
  Considering the price tag of the phone, you better not expect a 10 by 10 in all departments but overall for the areas where it does average, it has plenty more where it excels. So for just 13k this is the best damn phone right now in the market and I am comparing it to phones as high as 17 to 18k.
  

  PS: Get the Graphene Armor ULTRA HD tempered glass to protect your screen, it does not detract from the screen in any way and also remember to download the 800MB update the moment you get your phone setup, it does take care of many issues previously mentioned by other reviewers.

column6: Normal users review - 1 review that sums it up all for you.
column7:
Hello,
  

  I got this product within 3 days of purchase and I have been using it since 02nd May 2015 till date (13th May 2015). Personally, I am not feeling so happy owning a Mi 4i phone for the following reasons. However, there are some pros as well. I will list out both:
  

  Pros:
  

  1. I noticed that the battery life is excellent. I start my day (09:00 AM) by charging my phone for an hour (approx.) It gets charged from 20% - 85% within an hour. I use whatsapp for 3 hours in total, games for 0.5 hrs, calls for 1 hour and others apps for 0.5 hours in total. By 23:00, the battery life will be 30% still.
  

  2. The looks & design of the phone is good. It cannot miss anybody's attention while passing by and everybody opens up camera immediately and they say "wow". They call it even light weight. Its just 130gms against Moto g2 149gms and redmi note 4g 175gms.
  
  Its plastic back cover isn't too strong but it looks sturdy. It has however passed drop tests (Check out some videos in youtube).
  

  3. Primary camera is good and secondary camera is good. However, if there is low light, say night shots under tubelight condition has pixels. But if its good lighting, people ask "Can I will borrow your phone for taking some pictures". Its that good. Also it comes with time lapse and slow motion video camera. However shutter is slow and quick moving objects are blurred.
  

  4. 2gb RAM is fast enough and good for all gamers. Asphault 8 looks stunning and there is not even a single lag. I just faced 0.5 seconds lag once till date.
  

  5. You get constant updates from MI on the software and it will keep coming in as long as lollipop is evolving better. So no need to worry about small small complaints.
  

  6. Phone is handy to hold and to operate and the resolution of the screen is rich.
  

  Cons:
  

  1. The most concerned issue - heating. Yes, even I face it. Right from starting to play asphault 8 and upto half an hour, the phone heats up mild (say upto 30 degrees celcius). However, it is comparitely mild and you will definitely ignore it. Same was the case if you were taking pics for half an hour. However if you are charging your phone, it heats up till 40 degrees and you cannot keep the phone on your pocket immediately or can you switch on internet data immediately as this will further heat up the phone. After making 1 hour call, the phone was still cold. But to console you, even iphone heats up and you may expect some updates in the future for this.
  

  2. The plastic back cover case is not so sturdy and there are no cases available in the market till date. So use it carefully until market opens.
  

  3. The volume keys and lock key are strong and is difficult to press. Don't know if it can last for a long time.
  

  4. The touch of the screen is in general good, but at times it changes sensitivity on its own and can open up some apps on its own or type something which you never typed.
  

  5. The screen is fixed to set brightness yet I see that the brightness changes on its own. This is really disappointing. Within seconds of me operating, the brightness increases or decreases.
  

  6. The 16gb internal memory although might look big enough space for some normal users like me. Its only 10gb that finally reaches on hand and downloading games such as asphault eats away 1.5gb of space. So if you are a heavy gamer, its not recommended considering the memory constrainst.
  

  7. Finally, don't know if its my set's problem. The videos I shoot and upload on the internet has a green bar on the left hand side of the screen whereas the shot video is crystal clear in the gallery. I have to check on mi 4i forums about it or directly call customer care about it.
  

  Decision: My personalized opinion is you can buy this phone if you are fine to change your phone within a year and also you are fine with the above mentioned concerns. However, you do not get a phone of this price for the specs they offer. Moto g2 or leveno A7000 has its own cons and the decision to compromise is on your own choice. Also I have mentioned all criteria as far as possible. Do not read all the comments and confuse yourselves further :-) I don't feel proud buying Mi 4i for other phones.

column6: The ultimate beast of your home
column7:
Giving a clear and practical review after using for 3 weeks continuously.
  
  Firstly I would like to give the Tips for the existing and upcoming users as it will help you more than reading the reviews.
  
  1. If you get the phone with MIUI 6.5.3 update kindly update it to 6.5.4 asap. It will completely reduce all the heating issues. Otherwise you will feel the phone a fry pan.
  
  2. After receiving peel off the company fitted matte screen protector and place a 8-9H tempered screen guard as the phone doesn't have gorilla glass.
  
  3. Dont try to take pics with manual mode until you know it well.
  
  4.Use a hard back case for keeping away the phone form dust,oil. Still the phone has rubber washable nano finish back but it is recommended to use a back case.
  
  5.Don't access "permission manager". If you turn on the permission manager on many app features will be hidden.
  
  6. Try to off WIFI and mobile data as per your convenience for better battery backup and low heating of the phone.
  
  6.Dont use any launcher instead try to apply the themes available in MI themes.
  


  1. Look and comfortability
  
  Mi 4i is the slimmest phone in this range I can challenge. When you hold only the phone without any cover it will give you 1005 comfort to hold it for long times, When in call it is also very comfortable to hold the phone. Its trendy white and black combination gives an mind blowing stylish look.
  
  2. Performance
  
  I mainly do internet surfing,little bit gaming,photography,music and youtube. After doing all these things it gives a super 24 hour backup. I only charge once in a day. Coming to its octa core processor. Truly it has a superb speed of performance. It hardly gets hanged with the lucid combination of 2gb RAM and 8 core processor.
  
  3. Camera
  
  Its 13MP cam is truly 13MP. You can compare the images taken in daylight with A DSLR clicked image. Its front 5MP cam is just superb for taking selfies. Video quality is very good. But please don't click with manual mode untill you are not so accustomed to click picture in manual mode. It will give you a bad impression of the camera.
  
  4.Network
  
  Network reception is too good. It will give you the best 3g experience. Mobile data service is promptly switched on after you on the option.
  
  5.UI
  
  The MIUI 6 based on Android L is very good. Unlike the pure android versions you will get many more inbulit features for which you have to install 3rd party apps. Like-junk cleaner,app lock and many more.
  
  6.Sound
  
  The sound output is quite low but clear. You will get clear ans bass full sound in headphone. But if you listen songs only in phone then it is little bit low.
  
  7. Display
  
  The full HD IPS display will give you best out of your videos,movies. Display is very very clear. But it should have Gorilla glass 3.
  
  You will get much more than what you are paying. Go ahead for the phone if you are looking for a handy,sexy,performance mi-budget phone.

I have been using this phn for past 7 days and have never encountered any lags or hanging. Redmi 3s prime offers a massive storage of 32gb out of which only 25-26 gb can be used. I don't know why people are complaining that they are cheated as their phn doesn't hv storage as stated in specs, guys you can't get a full of 32gb usable, I know that mi should hv offered 28-30gb usable but yes we hv to compromise on that.

  I don't know why people are complaining about the camera quality I found its camera good especially the front one. I'm very much satisfied with the front facing camera.
  
  5. Compact
  
  If you have a mindset of using a compact phn then this phn is for you. Believe me guys, this phn is even more compact than other 5" phn and is very handy and can be used with one hand only.
  
  6. Battery Backup
  
  After buying this phn you don't need to carry your charger or power bank. Having 4000mAH battery is just like carrying a power bank itself. This phn lasts for 2 days of moderate use(playing games and surfing on net using wifi).
  
  7. Other sensors

I think everybody knows about IR, if not then it is used for tv and ac remotes etc, in other words you can use this phn as your remote and gyroscope helps you to view 360 degree videos and much more.
  
  8. CPU+GPU
  
  This phn has a decent cpu and works perfectly with adreno 505. I've played asphalt 8, sniper 3d and gangstar 4 and all of these games run without any lag.
  
  9. Value for money
  
  Finally, at last this phn is a beast at this price range.
  

  CONS :
  
  1. Screen is average
  
  The picture quality of this phone is just average. It is neither too bad nor too good. My previous phn which was also 720p, has much good looking picture quality than this.
  
  2. Heating issue
  
  This phn heats up only while playing heavy games which is a little bit annoying. However, doesn't heats up very much but does a little bit.

  This phn doesn't offer backlit in navigation keys. However, there is no need for them as the navigation keys are very much visible.
  
  4. No earphones
  
  This is a bitter true, this phn doesn't comes with an earphone and you hv to buy a separate one.

I am not the one to write reviews often. But this piece of phone has compelled me to write one. I have been using this for over two months now and I have been very disappointed with it.
  
  My reasons for purchase were simple: this phone claims to pack a good battery, RAM and a decent camera. Unfortunately, I have had a terrible experience on all these three fronts:
  

  a. Battery: In theory, the phone claims to have a super battery in this price range. However, the battery is nothing extraordinary. In fact, it hardly lasts for a day - even on an average use. The battery also diminishes at an accelerating pace. Once its <20%, you can bet that it will switch off in half an hour! And I have tried battery saving techniques, plugging off data connections, wifi etc. So I suspect that perhaps battery is not as strong as they claim. Atleast if you were looking to buy the phone with good battery, this is not the one.
  

  b. RAM: The 3GB RAM should work like a butter, right? Well, wrong. The phone hangs often. The first time it hang - and that was in the first two days of use itself - I ignored it. But then to my horror, it just kept hanging regularly. And mind you, I don't use more than say 3 apps at any given time. So a 3GB hanging with such avg use is something that is very weird.
  

  c. Camera: Well, the camera is very very average. And no, price range doesn't justify it as I have seen better cameras at this price range. The camera is terrible in low light. And quite avg even in daylight.
  

  Additional drawbacks:
  

  d. Heating issues: The phone's front surface heats up quite a bit on charging and during a call! If you happen to speak for more than ten minutes, the phone gets unbearably hot to hold on the ear!
  

  e. Network Connection: Now as if that other problems were not enough, you have the mother of all problems: poor network detection and connection. You see, I can live with a phone which doesn't deliver on battery as it claims, or a phone which hangs now and then or a phone which heats up and has an avg camera - BUT I cannot live with a phone where I can't even have a smooth connection!   Camera: Camera is a weak link here. Low photography could have been better. HDR mode is a little slow and takes some time. Full light photography is good and works well. (7/10)

Just to be clear.. my 3 star rating is as compared to all the phones currently in the market irrespective of their price. So considering its price, it's a very good phone. I'm writing this after using the phone for over a week.
  

  The phone has a spec sheet which is almost too good for its price. But it does indeed live up to it and the benchmarks show that. It has an amazing gpu and cpu so it can run almost any app. I'll explain the 'almost' later. The camera is average. Still quite better than its competitors. It even has an IR blaster, which is a nice little bonus.
  

  The battery life is amazing. I'm a very heavy user and it doesn't last a day, but I plug it in whenever I'm in my room and it hasn't died out on me yet. Easily provides over 7hrs SOT. There is slight heating on the top half only when playing games.
  

  Screen is good, brightness levels go from very low to very high, and colours look nice. My previous phone was Moto x2 so i do miss that infinite contrast of amoled though.
  

  Hardware wise this phone easily deserved a 4star, but MIUI. It's such a pain. It is still not polished to perfection. This is my first Xiaomi phone, so i expected miui to be running flawlessly on it. I actually loved the OS and used it 2 3 years ago on some samsung devices. There i could accept some bugs. But when it comes pre-installed, it's very disturbing. I have compatibility issues with quite a few apps. On one occasion i switched on Google voice's detect ok Google from any screen, and that resulted in muting my voice on all incoming phone calls. This was so unexpected that it took me a couple of days to find the cause of the problem.
  

  Apparently Xiaomi knows this and has provided an official method to unlock the bootloader. I wouldn't be complaining even if that worked. I get verification errors on it. And the phone still runs lollipop, how can a company this big not be able to debug it's skin in two years?
  

  Software restricts this phone from being as good as the impression its spec sheet creates. But it won't bug an average user too much. It still is an amazing phone for the price.

  The rear camera which boasts 16 MP camera at 11,999/- doesn't actually delivers pics like a 16 MP camera. But it is not disappointing either.   3. The display is very bright and clear. I can bet no one can keep maximum brightness level on this phone.
  

  4. The phone is compatible with variety of headphones and earphones. The sound quality is excellent.

First of all thanks to Flipkart & WS Retail, actually I was trying to buy this smartphone for the last one month or so from the other website (Am....), but every-time I get disappointed, then on 1st June on the very first day of the Open sale I saw Flipkart is selling this phone and guess who was the Seller, non other than WS Retail (I can blindly trust this seller), so I just ordered the 3gb/32gb (Gold) variant and I got this smartphone within 5 days of time and packaging was good as usual. Hats off to Flipkart & WS Retail !
  

  Now coming to the phone's PROS and CONS which I have noticed so far. For the last few years I've used many branded smartphones like, Nokia, Samsung, Asus, Micromax and this is the first time I'm using any MI smartphone and I must say, I'm really impressed with RN3.
  

  PROS -
  

  1. MADE IN INDIA
  
  2. MIUI, the MI user interface one of the most smooth, powerful & features packed android user interface, though I think ZenUI (ASUS) is far better in-terms of customization, also ZenUI is a very user friendly UI as well.
  
  3. Very simple and sleek design, overall solid build quality, metal uni-body.
  
  4. Radio and IR blaster and USB OTG support.
  
  5. Fast and accurate fingerprint scanner. (10/10)
  
  6. You can lock & unlock any app through your fingerprint, which is a plus point.
  
  7. Stunning 13.97cm (5.5") Full HD IPS display.
  
  8. Redmi Note 3 has a Qualcomm's Snapdragon 650 64 bit CPU with two A72 cores and four A53 cores to carry out intensive tasks at once while completing simpler tasks in the background to save on battery life.
  
  9. Adreno 510 graphics processor supports DirectX, OpenCL, FlexRender and other PC gaming technologies for a richer gaming support and experience.
  
  10. The Menu, Home, and Back keys are white backlit keys.
  
  11. 4G, Dual sim and supports all bands in India.
  
  12. The excellent output from the 3.5mm jack, all you need is a good pair of earphone.
  
  13. Big 4050 mAh high-capacity battery coupled with power efficient Qualcomm Snapdragon 650 processor and the battery saving features of MIUI makes it one of the most longer battery life smartphone.
  
  14. 16MP rear camera | 5MP front camera is not bad as I read in other reviews. It clicks decent images for 12k phone. Focus processing is fast and good enough to click the beautiful snaps in daylight condition, also it has real time filters, but Yes in low-light condition it struggles a bit and after-all it's a mobile cam, so we can't expect a DSLR like quality from it.
  
  15. Bundled with good quality 2 amp charger.
  
  16. RAM - Xiaomi is really better. When you first boot the device you get around 1.8 GB free. Then after you run some 10-12 applications you may get around 1.1 GB free. This does not make the device slow and there won't be any lag.
  
  17. VoLTE - supports this. It means you can get the better call quality.
  
  18. Gaming - I'm just a moderate gamer, played a few small games and didn't find any lags.
  
  19. OS - It runs with Lollipop android 5.1.1 version, which is pretty smooth and the good news is, YES RN3 will get the OTA update of Marshmallow 6.0.1 within this year, maybe around Sept - Oct, which is confirmed by MI.
  

  CONS -
  

  1. Does NOT have Corning Gorilla / Dragontail or any kind of glass protection (can be solved using a good quality Tempered glass).
  
  2. Hybrid slot for the Micro SD and 2nd sim card (either you can use 2nd sim card or Micro SD card, which actually I don't like at-all).
  
  3. No NFC, No USB Type-C.
  
  4. No Quick Charge 2.0 (it has old previous generation fast charging, but works well).
  
  5. Non-removable battery.
  

  HEATING ISSUE - I've seen in many reviews users are complaining about 'Heating issue' !!! Oh come on guys why don't you understand if you use any electronic gadgets to the high extent then it will Heat-up for sure and guys it has a metal outer body, so it will Heat-up a bit, Yes it also Heats up while you are charging, but when it reaches 70% charging level then it starts cool down and it's cool down really fast and I don't think it's a deal-breaker.
  

  VERDICT -
  

  If anyone is looking for a budget smartphone with a Flagship like performance then don't think twice, just go for it, you will never get disappointed with your purchase. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
  

  UPDATE -
  

  I'm using this RN3 SD for the past 1.5 month or so, I'm totally AMAZE with it's performance, this is the fastest smartphone I've ever used so far !!! MI Rocks !!! Few words to those frndz who are facing so called battery heating issue, please update your RN3 SD with new MIUI 8 Global Beta ROM, definitely it will decrease your RN3 SD's battery heating problem and guyz MIUI 8 is really superb !

I am Reviewing this product after 2 weeks of use. Overal, the device is very good.
  

  PERFORMANCE: The performance is extremely good. It has Snapdragon 650(The same processor which you get on Xperia X priced at    45000). However, under heavy gaming, it may show small lags.
  


  BUILD & DESIGN: The design is truely amazing. It looks very good and is very nice to hold. But the Aluminium  Back is quite slippery. If you're getting this device, do invest in a Case.
  

  DISPLAY: The 1080p panel is very sharp. The display quality is very good. But the display doesn't have Gorilla Glass protection. So you will have to buy a Tempered Glass.
  

  AUDIO: The speakers are very loud and good. The sound from audio jack is also very good.
  

  CAMERA: I saw a lot of users complaining about the camera. But in my opinion, it might not be the best but it is good. I don't have any complaint about the front or back camera. The dual LED flash is very bright and enhances the shots in low light.
  

  BATTERY: The battery on this device is extraordinary. I can easily get a Screen On Time of around 8 - 10 hours on single charge. It will easily get you through the day. If you a light user, it can even last up to 2 days.
  

  SOFTWARE: I personally don't like the MiUi. It has a lot of bloatware. At present, the autorotation doesn't work sometimes. Hopefully, this issue will be solved with a software update very soon.
  

  HEATING: On normal usage and gaming, it will show mild heating which you can neglect. Under heavy usage( like 360   videos or VR Videos more than 15 min), the can get very hot. But one hardly watches those videos, so I guess heating won't be an issue.
  

  SERVICE: THE Xiaomi's after sale services aren't good. The PickMi service takes a lot of time. Service centers are not present everywhere. I live in Chhattisgarh. There is no Xiaomi Service Center in the whole state.

I ordered 32GB Redmi Note 3 Gold for Rs.11,999 on 2nd Jun 2016 and it was delivered on 9th Jun 2016.
  
  I was using Asus Zenfone 5 before this but the MIUI beats the Asus skin any day. Here is what I think of the phone:
  

  Design: The Gold edition is gorgeous and looks beautiful. Bezels are quite thin and the metallic body does not slip. Does not look like a mid-range phone at all. (9/10)
  

  Processor: I have not got the chance to test it fully but have been amazed so far. Snapdragon 650 works like a charm and you have enough RAM to work without any small lags. (9/10)
  

  Display: The 401ppi FHD display comes alive really great. Combine that with the plethora of available themes for mi and the phone should never feel old. Videos look great and vivid. Sunlight display works like a charm. (9/10)
  

  Camera: Camera is a weak link here. Low photography could have been better. HDR mode is a little slow and takes some time. Full light photography is good and works well. (7/10)
  

  Others: Speakers are placed behind but should have been put on the edges like in phones these days. Sound is decent, not too loud but good rendition. The network and wifi works quite better than my old Asus and is quite strong. MIUI is highly customizable and I love it already. The phone cannot be opened at all, there is a sim slot on the left side to insert SIM/Memory card.
  
  24GB is usable out of the 32GB internal memory.
  
  Fingerprint scanner took a little time to set up at first but worked like a charm thereafter.
  
  So far, have not faced any heating issues(Snapdragon 650 is a far more superior processor than the Mediatek one that Xiaomi used on the Note 3 models for China, so not really surprised).
  
  And the best part is that this is Made in India.
  

  Verdict:
  
  If you can do with the mediocre low light photography and the fixed internal memory(considering that you will use SIM in both slots), no other phone comes close to what Mi Note 3 offers. I considered Moto G4, Lenevo Zuk Z1, Lenevo K4 Note, Yu Yunicorn, Asus Zenfone Max and Coolpad Note before I finally decided on Note 3.
  

  Overall Rating - ****
  
  Would have given 5 star if the Camera had been as good as the rest of the phone.

Just to be clear.. my 3 star rating is as compared to all the phones currently in the market irrespective of their price. So considering its price, it's a very good phone. I'm writing this after using the phone for over a week.
  

  The phone has a spec sheet which is almost too good for its price. But it does indeed live up to it and the benchmarks show that. It has an amazing gpu and cpu so it can run almost any app. I'll explain the 'almost' later. The camera is average. Still quite better than its competitors. It even has an IR blaster, which is a nice little bonus.
  

  The battery life is amazing. I'm a very heavy user and it doesn't last a day, but I plug it in whenever I'm in my room and it hasn't died out on me yet. Easily provides over 7hrs SOT. There is slight heating on the top half only when playing games.
  

  Screen is good, brightness levels go from very low to very high, and colours look nice. My previous phone was Moto x2 so i do miss that infinite contrast of amoled though.
  

  Hardware wise this phone easily deserved a 4star, but MIUI. It's such a pain. It is still not polished to perfection. This is my first Xiaomi phone, so i expected miui to be running flawlessly on it. I actually loved the OS and used it 2 3 years ago on some samsung devices. There i could accept some bugs. But when it comes pre-installed, it's very disturbing. I have compatibility issues with quite a few apps. On one occasion i switched on Google voice's detect ok Google from any screen, and that resulted in muting my voice on all incoming phone calls. This was so unexpected that it took me a couple of days to find the cause of the problem.
  

  Apparently Xiaomi knows this and has provided an official method to unlock the bootloader. I wouldn't be complaining even if that worked. I get verification errors on it. And the phone still runs lollipop, how can a company this big not be able to debug it's skin in two years?
  

  Software restricts this phone from being as good as the impression its spec sheet creates. But it won't bug an average user too much. It still is an amazing phone for the price.

Redmi Note 3 is an awesome smartphone with only the LeEco Le 2 as a competitor in the price segement. I have used both of them, so I am gonna compare the two to give you a better view to choose between them.
  

  Design: Personally I loved the design of Le2. Both phones offer a nice build quality but Le2 looks more premium and slimmer.
  

  Display: Redmi offers a sharp Full HD screen. No noticible difference here.
  

  Performance: Redmi offers a powerful Snapdragon 650 SoC coupled with 3GB RAM which handles daily tasks and moderate gaming without any issues. LeEco has a slightly better 652 SoC but normally you won't notice a lot of difference.
  

  Storage: Redmi offers 32GB storage just as LeEco but additionally one of its SIM slots can be used as SD card slot and hence it gains the edge over Le2 in storage.
  

  Camera: This is where I feel both phones could have done better. That being said, the Camera's are almost equal on paper and in actuality. Although, some shots felt better on Le2.
  

  Battery: Redmi Note 3 has  a huge 4000Mah battery compared to 3100Mah in Le2. Expect a lot better battery backup in Redmi. However, Le2 features quickcharge support and comes with quick charge adapter, so it charges a lot quicker.
  

  LeEco Le 2 and Redmi Note 3 are good phones. Both has their own advantages and disadvantages. Based on requirement, the device can be selected. A nice mobile phone under 12k budget. It functions very smooth and gets a bit heat on high usage which you may notice. But its obvious as it is made of metal not plastic.
  

  Though I am not a hardcore gamer, I was playing Asphalt 8 and NFS which perfomed with no lags. Adreno 510 has done its job. But still at times I personally find it took more time loading games.
  

  Memory management is nicely done by the 3Gb RAM. It stores all the information and makes it a bit easier to switch between and operate the applications in the mobile.
  

  Camera - This is where Xiaomi has to concentrate. Pictures that are captured are of more warmth, saturated a little heavy and light exposured a lot. Low light photos are not good to be frank.
  


  Memory - You will get 25GB approx., for internal storage. And you can go for a microSD card if needed, provided only one SIM is inserted as it has hybrid SIM slot.
  

  Display - You are getting 1080p full HD display which offers a crystal clear display quality. You can enable READ MODE when you are using the device at night / reading articles in a low-light environment. No gorilla glass technology but still the display is build the way it can manage the stress.
  

  Durability - Yes, it is very durable. Even if your device is under water for 10 seconds, it works fine. It manages all the stresses and pressures. I am using the ipaky case for Redmi note 3 which you may feel a bit heavy but it protects the device so well.
  

  Fingerprint sensor - Guys, it really recognises the fingerprint so quick, yes, so quick.
  

  Worthy? - Yes, it worths all your bucks you give.
  

  Note : Its all my review, which is subjective. It might differ from another end user depending on the usage and the way they use.

It's almost a month since I recieved this product. I bought this for my Mom and she's not a heavy user. From the one month's usage here's some of my observations.
  
  Pros:
  
  Camera: Immediately out of the box, the camera wasn't working fine, but soon after on recieving an update it revved up. Daylight pictures are great. Medium light is good and low-light is okay-ish.
  
  Battery: Claimed 4100 mAh, but the software claims it to be 4000 only. But anyway the battery backup is superb for medium users, can easily expect a little over a day on one full charge. For heavy usage one full day of usage can be expected.
  
  Performance: Not faced any major issues of lags or stuttering. Memory management not too good but it's good enough for medium usage.
  
  Display: 1280*720 display with a high ppi amounts to a crisp and lucid display on this 4.7 inch screen. For watching movies and stuff. Can run 2K videos, on 3rd party players but smoothness is not guaranteed.
  
  Design: The metal body is sleek, shiny and looks premium. Using some cover is recommended as the metal body, although provides some grip but is prone to bring slippery at times.
  

  Now to the tougher part
  

  Cons:
  
  Storage: Mi started with the hybrid slot which is favoured by some people but I personally don't like it. Using 2 SIM cards restricted you to only 16 GB of storage of which a hefty amount (5-6 GB) is preoccupied by the system itself.
  
  Volte Support: Although the phone supports Volte officially, Flipkart denies it. And while using a 4g SIM card I can't use Volte with it although the same SIM card works fine on other phones. Although other Sims work fine on the same phone but this particular combination doesn't work fine.
  

  Anyway a good product for medium usage pattern and an amazing camera.

People who know me know that I'm not a fan of Apple phones, especially after having used them. Earlier, I use to compare my Moto G (2013) with it and favoured the Moto G. I also have a Moto E which is also good for its price, though I'll put it equal to the iOS based devices from Apple.
  

  Now, I got the Redmi 2 in the first flash sale from Flipkart and they delivered it in 3 days. Good. And I'll now ask Apple to beat this.
  

  Features: Excellent. Like high end androids. There are lots of settings. I spent the first day just exploring the settings. Check here:
  
  http://en.miui.com/thread-47569-1-1.html
  

  Battery: Pretty good. Lasting me more than 1.5 days as of now with moderate usage (but no videos or games).
  

  Looks: Ok. Better than I expected. Not as chiselled as HTC phones. But looks come at a price. Not a major concern for me.
  
  I would have preferred that sea-green colour but I needed a phone quickly and took the white one that was available on flipkart.
  

  Feel and build: A bit plasticky but firm enough. No crackles.
  
  It's really light. Amazingly light to hold, given the 2200mAh battery.
  
  The rear grip should have been more matte. In this, the Moto E and G are way better. But is this a dealbreaker? No.
  

  One handed operation: Yes.
  

  Software interface: Amazing. Lots of customisations available.
  

  Processing: Good, smooth with very occasional lags. I would blame the 1 GB RAM for this 64 bit architecture. No crashes yet but a couple of unknown processes restarted. Looks like the software is able to take care of itself, though. There is an in the box app which lets you clear the stuff up pretty quickly. So, nothing to worry.
  

  Camera: Did not try. I'm not a camera guy and will not be able to pronounce verdicts on them.
  

  Sound: Pleasing, Clear, Loud. Unexpected at this price range.
  

  3G and browsing: Slick.
  

  Kitkat: I thought this was taking me back from Lollypop (on my Moto G) but this is not really felt as the MIUI 6 wrapper gives a much better feel than stock android. And unlike HTC Sense, MIUI hasn't slowed the phone down.
  

  Overall, way better than most expensive phones, without that price tag. Right now, I am happy with my purchase.

column6: Great phone, great price, but it's not for everyone
column7:
I bought the Redmi 2 after reading many reviews and knowing that it's not a perfect phone. So am I happy with the phone after 2 months? Absolutely, yes!
  

  I mainly use the phone to make calls, Whatsapp, browse, navigate and take pictures. I don't play games or use FB.
  

  Why I like the phone:
  
  - Good performance. Generally fast and responsive except for some occasions. No real complaints, though.
  

  - Good battery life. I can stretch the battery to 2 days with moderate usage.
  

  - Good screen. The colour reproduction and the viewing angle are both very good. Not all HD screen have equally good viewing angles. Sun light visibility is average but generally only high-end phones have good sun light visibility. So again, no complaints at all.
  

  - MIUI is actually good. It has a lot of user-friendly features and looks quite good too. The development is quite active so updates are available.
  

  - The camera is very good in good lighting. Exposure is good, colour is good and focus is good. I have taken hundreds of photos and most of them are excellent. The ones that are not good are those taken in low light. But at this price, I accept this limitation.
  

  - A secret feature very few people know: the camera lens has a special anti-finger print coating to keep it clean. If you do get it dirty, a quick wipe with a soft cloth will clean it easily. This has helped take some excellent pictures.
  

  - Build quality is good. It's not the same as a solid Nokia or a Moto G but it does not feel cheap in any way.
  

  - Calls are clear, network connection is good. No complaints on the essential features of a mobile phone.
  


  What I dont't like:
  

  - The white back cover has a anti-fingerprint coating to keep it clean. It works pretty well but it also makes the phone a bit slippery. So a extra  back case is a must.
  

  - The charger provided is only 1 A output so the charging is a bit slow compared to other phones. This is sad because the Redmi 2 has the Quick Charge feature for fast charging. Use a higher output charger for faster charging.
  


  Why I would not recommend this phone to everyone:
  

  MIUI is a good user interface and has a lot of good features but to make full use of the features requires a bit of technical knowledge.
  

  Example 1: you can control app permissions for various things, including autostart. But this same feature will cause Whatsapp and other apps not to autostart or notify.
  

  Example 2: If you have limited data then this limit can be set in the phone and monitored. But the settings are not easy to use.
  

  So my opinion is that the Redmi or any Xiaomi phone is suitable only for people who can understand some technical details and change phone settings to suit them.Either this or have help from someone who can do all this for you!

Redmi 2 doesn't look like a Rs 6,999 smartphone from any angle, especially if you consider the display. At this price segment, we are used to displays with poor viewing angles, dull colors and usually don't have any protection like Corning's Gorilla Glass or Asahi's Dragontrail. The Redmi 2 changes all that. The phone retains the 4.7-inch 720p display specification from the Redmi 1S but it is not the same display. Xiaomi has gone with a laminated display this time, which reduces the gap between the LCD layer and the glass on top, so icons appear to be on the glass surface and you also get better viewing angles. The Redmi 2 s display is not only brighter but also reproduces colors better than most displays you'd find on smartphones in this category. It also has good outdoor legibility and comes with Dragontrail protection as well. If you factor in that at 312ppi this is actually a Retina display and look at the price point, you'd realize that Xiaomi has done something special here.
  

  Comparing it with the Redmi 1S, the Redmi 2 is thinner, lighter and generally better designed. The curved edges and corners feel good to hold though it can get quite slippery at times. Both the models have 8-megapixel rear cameras but the Redmi 2 now has a 2-megapixel front camera. Both devices have 8GB of internal storage and 1GB RAM but the Redmi 2 has a newer Qualcomm Snapdragon 410 quad-core chipset clocked at 1.2GHz. Xiaomi likes to market its 64-bit architecture but sadly the smartphone still runs on Android KitKat, which doesn't utilize any of the improvements. Xiaomi has also added a second microphone on the rear for noise cancellationand it works. In my experience, the audio quality during voice calls is top-notch.
  


  For the past three months I have been exclusively using sub-Rs 10,000 smartphones as my primary phones and the experience has been an eye opener. The Redmi 2, in many ways, is the pinnacle of what affordable smartphones are capable of doing. Take the 8-megapixel rear camera, for instance. Let me put it simply, if you are looking for an affordable camera phone, the Redmi 2 should be on the top of your shopping list. The camera quality is sort of unseen on a Rs 6,999 phone. Photos clicked in daylight are vibrant and retain sharpness. You even get the 'bokeh' effect in closeup shots. Even slightly well-lit indoor photos come out well in HDR mode. Photos clicked indoors have noise especially when viewed at 100 percent zoom but more than passable for putting up on social media networks.
  

  The front-facing camera automatically starts the  age guess  mode, where the camera guesses your gender and age. Quite fun. The front-facing camera has a wide angle for group selfies. The photos are passable and are usually have noise, but that's on expected lines. Overall, I can't think of any smartphone priced below Rs 10,000 with this camera quality.
  


  I was able to play Asphalt 8: Airborne with low graphics settings with no problems whatsoever. Of course, Temple Run 2 plays fine on it as well, so do many other popular games. There wasn't a single regular app that wouldn't work on it. Some people have faced problems with Truecaller not working on MIUI 6, but you can get that running as well by adding it into the auto start list in the app permissions from the built-in security app.
  

  That isn't to say that the Redmi 2 is perfect. In my books, Xiaomi has been a bit too ambitious running MIUI 6 with its myriad animations running on such frugal hardware. Apps take a wee bit longer to open, there is noticeable lag while switching apps and just in case you have too many apps running in the background (in my experience around six apps or more), things start slowing down. You might be trying to scroll through your Twitter timeline but it would register the scroll flick gesture as a tap, the keypad starts getting sticky and hitting the home button leads to a loading screen.
  

  But there's nothing that killing off apps in the background cannot solve. After using the phone for a couple of days, you start noticing the signs much earlier and tend to kill unnecessary background apps almost intuitively. This is something that can be improved with a software update, which I would hope is around the corner.
  

  Redmi 2 is probably the only smartphone available right now at any price point that offers dual-mode, dual-band 4G LTE connectivity on both SIM cards.There's no other smartphone priced under Rs 10,000 that has 4G/3G connectivity on both SIM card slots.
  

  The 2,200mAh battery almost lasted me for an entire day a couple of times, which again is surprising.
  

  Redmi 2 is almost the perfect sub-Rs 10,000 smartphone. Priced at Rs 6,999, Xiaomi has set a new benchmark for others to meet yet again. Higher praise than that, I cannot give.

  The good thing about this phone is a battery optimizer in built with the UI. After the phone reaches 20% it shut down all power consuming process and gives a lot of mileage w.r.t battery (a.k.a marathon mode)
  

  One can get more privacy setting without installing any third party applications. Facebook, flipkart and Google applications are pre-installed. All you need is to juice a WiFi and update.
  

  One thing I noticed is a busy RAM. Even if we kill all apps, it still shows 79% most of the time. But despite that, the phone doesn't show any sign of lag or hesitations.
  

  After connecting the phone to computer, you don't have the feature to see it as a separate USB device, but only visible as a phone device. Which makes file transfer speeds awful.
  

  About the battery, I switched on data and WiFi and kept updating and downloading stuffs, trust me it give mileage for a whole day :) and I read that Li-Po or Li-ion batteries reach full capability after one month continuous cycle of charging and discharging. So the battery performance will increase
  

  It have a great screen, crisp and bright, vibrant. The dragon-trail protective glass gives more than enough protection, so I don't advice to use a screen guard.
  

  The music app doesn't have shuffle option, but it do have option to make a song favorite by just one touch. Inbuilt video application supports mp4 3gp and most videos.
  

  Now for the negative statements, the phone gets heated very quick, but nothing that you can't handle or absent in other phones. May be its for the better functioning and life of components (I'm not the right person to say the exact technical reason for it) or its just the only flaw
  

  But for a price of 7000, you get more that what it can offer. So there is no point in complaining about just one minor issue, which is seen in almost every smartphone.
